Karnataka accounts for nearly 25% of the country’s elephant population. As per the 2023 elephant population 
estimation, the State has an estimated 6,395 elephants, highlighting its critical role in elephant conservation 
at the national level. The State also has five Tiger Reserves and, according to the All India Tiger Estimation 
2022, Karnataka is ranked as the second-largest Tiger State in the country, with an estimated population of 
563 tigers.
In a significant conservation initiative, the State has, for the first time, notified a marine wildlife sanctuary. 
An area of 5,959.32 hectares, comprising a 6 km stretch of coastal area and adjoining forest land in Honnavar 
taluk of Uttara Kannada district, was declared as the “Apsarakonda–Mugali Marine Wildlife Sanctuary” on 24 
June 2025. The sanctuary aims to protect marine biodiversity and conserve breeding and nesting habitats.
To address human–wildlife conflict and strengthen forest protection mechanisms, the Karnataka Forest 
Department has established an Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) at the State Headquarters in 
Bengaluru, along with Divisional/District Command and Control Centres (DCCCs) in 11 high Human–Elephant 
conflict divisions. These centres are envisaged to function as centralised platforms for real-time monitoring, 
coordination with field personnel, and informed decision-making through the integration of field-level data, 
surveillance systems, and technological interventions.

As directed by the NTCA, the 6th cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation Exercise is being undertaken in all 52 
divisions of the State.

7.1.4 State Sector Schemes
Special Component Plan
Under welfare-oriented forestry interventions, LPG gas connections, solar lamps, and bee-hive boxes are 
provided to Scheduled Caste beneficiaries to improve living conditions and support income generation. In 
addition, avenue plantations along roads leading to Scheduled Caste colonies are undertaken.
For the year 2025–26, a grant of Rs. 300.00 lakh has been allocated. By the end of December 2025, an 
expenditure of Rs. 184.92 lakh had been incurred, under which two free LPG cylinder refills were provided to 
13,688 Scheduled Caste beneficiaries.
Tribal Sub-Plan
To reduce pressure on forest resources, LPG gas connections, LPG cylinder refills, solar water heaters, and 
solar lamps are provided to Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries. In addition, bee-hive boxes are distributed to 
support livelihood enhancement. The program also includes the maintenance of raised avenue plantations 
along roads leading to Scheduled Tribe habitations.
For the year 2025-26, a grant of Rs.700.00 lakh has been allocated. By the end of December 2025, an 
expenditure of Rs. 416.40 lakh had been incurred, under which two free LPG cylinder refills were provided to 
32,081 Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries.
Siri Chandana Vana
The area under sandalwood plantations and naturally occurring sandalwood trees is protected and maintained 
through measures such as chain-link fencing, watch and ward, soil working, cultural operations, and other 
protective interventions.
For the year 2025-26, an allocation of Rs. 361.76 lakh has been provided. By the end of December 2025, an 
expenditure of Rs. 172.29 lakh had been incurred for the maintenance of 613 hectares of naturally growing 
sandalwood areas, recruitment and maintenance of 60 watchmen, maintenance of 12 dogs, upkeep of 
1,484.04 hectares of old plantations, 83.80 km of inspection routes, and 165 km of fire lines.

PDF_PAGE 271
263
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Development of degraded forests
Under this scheme, degraded forest areas are rejuvenated through afforestation and soil and water 
conservation measures. Where adequate rootstock exists, such areas are protected from biotic pressure to 
facilitate natural regeneration. In other areas, plantations are raised based on local requirements for small 
timber, fuelwood, and fodder.
For the year 2025-26, an allocation of Rs. 15,068.74 lakh has been provided. By the end of December 2025, 
an expenditure of Rs. 7,899.35 lakh had been incurred for raising plantations over 15,172 hectares, advance 
works in 5,989 hectares, and maintenance of plantations over 21,694 hectares.
Raising of Seedlings for Public Distribution
(a) Raising of Seedlings for Public Distribution
Under this scheme, seedlings are being raised for distribution to the public, farmers, and organizations at 
subsidized rates to plant on their lands. For this purpose, seedlings of suitable local species as per demand 
are raised in 6” x 9” and 8” x 12” sized bags every year by the department. 
During the year 2025-26, a grant of Rs.1,196.43 lakh has been allocated for the implementation of the scheme 
for raising saplings for public distribution, in which Rs.433.80 lakh was spent on the maintenance of 44.605 
lakh saplings and 34.72 lakh on raising of seedlings upto the end of December -2025.
(b) “Krishi Aranya Protsaha Yojane (KAPY)” programme
In the year 2025-26, a total of Rs.1000.00 lakh has been allocated for the disbursement of incentive funds 
to farmers under the Agricultural Forestry Incentive Scheme Program. The said grant will be allocated to the 
pending cases of payment of incentive funds to farmers in the years 2019-20 and 2020-21 and for payment of 
service amounts as per rules.out of this Rs.338.482 lakh has been spent upto end of December 2025.
Roadside Plantation Scheme
Karnataka has approximately 4,000 km of National Highways, 21,000 km of State Highways, and 38,000 
km of District Roads covered under various avenue afforestation programmes. During 2025–26, a grant of  
Rs. 4,110.076 lakh has been allocated. By the end of December 2025, an expenditure of Rs. 1,931.924 lakh had 
been incurred for maintenance of plantations along 2,608.26 km of roads, maintenance of 47,500 seedlings, 
raising of plantations along 159 km, and advance works along 128 km.
Greening of Urban Areas
The scheme aims to mitigate urban pollution arising from high population density, vehicular traffic, and 
industrial activity through the planting of ornamental, shade-giving, and fruit-bearing trees. In addition, tree 
parks, woodlots, and avenue plantations are developed in urban areas to enhance environmental quality and 
urban aesthetics.During 2025–26, a grant of Rs. 1,136.57 lakh has been allocated. By the end of December 
2025, an expenditure of Rs. 578.56 lakh had been incurred for the maintenance of plantations along 1,021.36 
km and the raising of plantations along 80 km.
Hasiru Karnataka
With increased emphasis on social forestry, indigenous tree species are planted extensively on Government 
lands around hillocks, mangroves, and lakes. In this context, the “Green Karnataka” programme, announced

in the Budget 2018–19, aims to promote tree planting at multiple levels—a tree for every household, a forest 
for every village, a mini forest for each taluk, and a forest for each district—with active participation of school 
and college students and environmental organisations.
During 2025–26, an allocation of Rs. 245.39 lakh has been allocated under the Green Karnataka scheme. By

Afforestation in Other Areas
During road widening works on State and National Highways, trees are felled, necessitating compensatory 
afforestation. For this purpose, the prescribed amounts are deposited by user agencies such as K-SHIP , KPTCL, 
KRDCL, and other utility agencies. Based on these deposits, funds are released by the Government for carrying 
out compensatory afforestation works.
For the year 2025–26, a grant of Rs. 1,500.00 lakh has been allocated, of which Rs. 1,125.00 lakh has been 
released. By the end of December 2025, an expenditure of Rs. 702.81 lakh had been incurred towards advance 
works, raising of plantations, and maintenance activities, in accordance with prescribed norms and within the 
limits of funds deposited by the user agencies.
Tree Park Scheme
The scheme aims to improve the urban environment by establishing tree parks in district and taluk 
headquarters, on forest, non-forest, or other community lands in areas with higher population density, to 
enhance public access to green spaces.
For the year 2025–26, an allocation of Rs. 2,000.00 lakh has been allocated, of which Rs. 1,000.00 lakh has 
been released. By the end of December 2025, an expenditure of Rs. 711.23 lakh had been incurred. Out of 
a total of 186 tree parks, 140 tree parks were maintained, and 18 tree parks were taken up for development 
works during the last three years.
Further, 32 tree parks have been approved under the KFDF Flexi Fund for 2024–25 and 2025–26, comprising 
24 new and 8 existing tree parks. Of these, creation of 8 new tree parks and development works in 5 existing 
tree parks are currently in progress.
Development and Preservation of Devarakadu (Daivivana)
Devarakadu forests are ecologically and culturally significant and are conserved as sacred groves to preserve 
their ecosystems in a pristine condition, allowing natural evolutionary processes to continue without 
anthropogenic disturbance. Under this scheme, Daivivanas (sacred groves) are proposed to be developed in 
each district.
For the year 2025–26, an allocation of Rs.385.00 lakh has been provided, of which Rs.257.528 lakh has been 
released. By the end of December 2025, an expenditure of Rs.142.798 lakh had been incurred. Out of a total of 
128 Devarakadus, 46 Devarakadus were maintained, and 8 new Devarakadus were taken up for development.
Further, 8 Devarakadus have been approved under the KFDF Flexi Fund for 2024–25 and 2025–26, comprising 
6 new and 2 existing Devarakadus. Of these, creation of 5 new Devarakadus and development works in 1 
existing Devarakadu are currently in progress.

7.1.5 Centrally Sponsored Schemes 
Project Tiger and Project Elephant
Project Tiger, launched in 1973, is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with funding shared 
between the Centre and the State in the ratio of 60:40 for non-recurring works and 50:50 for recurring works. 
In Karnataka, the scheme is implemented in Bandipur, Rajiv Gandhi (Nagarahole), Bhadra, BRT and Kali Tiger 
Reserves. Funds under the scheme are utilised for the protection, development, and conservation of tiger 
habitats, including fire line maintenance, habitat improvement works, infrastructure development, and other 
conservation measures. Provision is also made for payment of wages and special allowances to outsourced 
staff engaged in anti-poaching camps and to permanent staff working in tiger reserves.
Karnataka has five Tiger Reserves. As per the All India Tiger Estimation 2022, the State has an estimated 563 
tigers, ranking second in the country in terms of tiger population. In accordance with the directions of the 
National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), the sixth cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation is currently 
being conducted across all 52 forest divisions in the State.

PDF_PAGE 274
266
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Under the Project Elephant scheme, priority is accorded to the protection and conservation of elephant 
habitats, particularly in the Mysuru and Dandeli–Bhadra Elephant Reserves, along with implementation of 
measures to mitigate human–elephant conflict. The Central Government has merged Project Elephant with 
Project Tiger from 2023–24, with funding support in the ratio of 60:40 (Centre:State).
The merged scheme supports elephant habitat conservation in National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries across 
regions including Kolar, Bannerghatta National Park, Ramanagara, Mysuru, Hunsur, Madikeri, Mangaluru, 
Belagavi, Chamarajanagar, Virajpet, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, and Uttara Kannada. Major activities 
include construction and maintenance of elephant-proof trenches and solar fencing, establishment of Rapid 
Response Teams, anti-poaching camps, elephant driving squads, capture and relocation of problematic 
elephants, procurement of tranquilising equipment and medicines, staff and veterinary training, and 
awareness programmes.
As per the 2023 Elephant Estimation (direct count method), Karnataka has an estimated 6,395 elephants, 
accounting for the highest elephant population in the country.
The budget of Rs.7483.34 lakhs earmarked during 2025-26 of which central share 4175.17 lakhs and state 
share 3308.17 lakhs. The expenditure up to December 2025 was 3581.62 lakhs against the release 4129.42 
lakhs.
Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (IDWH)
Under this project, funding is shared between the Government of India (60 per cent) and the State 
Government (40 per cent).Protection and conservation measures are being implemented across 5 National 
Parks, 37 Wildlife Sanctuaries, 19 Special Protected Areas, and 1 Community Reserve under the Wildlife Unit. 
The project focuses on the conservation of priority species and habitats, including the Great Indian Bustard 
landscape, Arabian Sea Humpback Whale, Olive Ridley Turtle, Vulture Breeding Centres, and Hornbill species.
The scheme supports the establishment and operation of anti-poaching camps for protection of wildlife and 
protected areas, including payment of wages to outsourced personnel. It also covers habitat development 
activities such as construction and maintenance of water bodies, removal of invasive weeds, restoration of 
grasslands, and forest fire prevention and protection measures.
The budget of Rs. 2776.00 lakhs earmarked during 2025-26 of which central share 1558.00 lakhs and state 
share 1218.00 lakhs. The expenditure up to December 2025 was 163.20 lakhs against the release 728.51 
lakhs.
National Bamboo Mission
The National Bamboo Mission (NBM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched by the Ministry of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, with a 60:40 Centre–State funding pattern, effective from 2018–
19. The scheme aims to promote bamboo development in forest areas through Forest Development Agencies 
(FDAs) with the support of Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs), and in non-forest areas through 
Bamboo Development Agencies (BDAs).
For the year 2025–26, a provision of Rs. 1,158.11 lakh has been made in the State Budget for implementation 
of the scheme. The Government of India has approved an Annual Action Plan of Rs. 2,316.20 lakh for the year 
under the 60:40 sharing pattern and has sanctioned Rs. 694.86 lakh as the first instalment. Accordingly, the 
State Government has released Rs. 1,158.11 lakh, including its share of Rs. 463.25 lakh, to the Department. 
The funds have been further released to the implementing officers through the SNA–SPARSH module for 
execution of works.

PDF_PAGE 275
267
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Conservation and Management of Mangroves
The scheme aims to prevent and mitigate coastal erosion through mangrove conservation and management. 
Activities include raising and maintenance of mangrove plantations and awareness and training programmes 
among coastal communities. The programme is implemented in the Honnavara, Mangaluru, Karwar, and 
Kundapur Divisions. For the year 2025–26, a budget provision of Rs. 50.00 lakh has been made.
Green India Mission
The Green India Mission (GIM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, recognising the role of forest and tree cover in environmental 
improvement, climate change mitigation, food and water security, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood 
security of forest-dependent communities.
The key objectives of the Mission are to increase and improve forest and tree cover over 10 million hectares, 
enhance ecosystem services including biodiversity, water conservation and carbon sequestration, and 
augment forest-based livelihoods of approximately three million people living in and around forest areas.
The programme has been under implementation in Kalaburagi, Hassan, and Sirsi forest divisions since 2015–
16. For the year 2025–26, an allocation of Rs. 836.78 lakh has been provided in the State Budget, comprising 
a Central share of Rs. 502.07 lakh and a State share of Rs. 334.71 lakh.
During the year, the Government of India sanctioned and released a first instalment of Rs. 95.00 lakh towards 
pending liabilities of 2024–25. Correspondingly, the State Government released Rs. 158.34 lakh, including its 
share of Rs. 63.34 lakh, to the Department. The funds have been further released to implementing officers 
through the SNA–SPARSH module for execution of works.
Forest Fire Prevention and Management (FPM) Scheme
Forest Fire Prevention and Management is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with a 60:40 cost-sharing pattern 
between the Government of India and the State Government, aimed at the overall protection of forests 
from fire. The scheme supports activities such as creation and maintenance of fire lines, construction of 
water storage structures, procurement of modern fire-fighting equipment, forest fire prevention measures, 
and awareness campaigns. Up to the end of December 2025, an amount ofRs. 75.00 lakh has been released 
under the scheme, comprising a Central share of Rs. 45.00 lakh and a State share of Rs. 30.00 lakh. Of this, 
Rs. 72.956 lakh has been utilised.
Nagaravana Scheme
With increasing urbanisation, pollution levels in towns and cities have risen sharply, leading to health hazards 
and adverse impacts on daily life. To promote an eco-friendly environment, enhance green cover, and improve 
biodiversity, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, has proposed the 
implementation of the Nagaravana Scheme in urban areas.
During 2025–26, 10 new proposals have been submitted to the Government of India for approval, and

7.1.9 Externally Aided Project 
Karnataka Stregthening Coastal Resilience and the Economy Project (KSHORE)
The objective of this project is to prevent plastic waste from entering the oceans/seas through rivers and to 
reduce plastic waste in the water bodies of the coastal districts of the state and reduce public health risks, 
restore coastal and marine ecosystems, and create sustainable livelihoods through a circular economy.
A grant of Rs. 5000.00 lakh has been allocated for the implementation of the plan for the year 2025-26 and 
the first instalment of grant of Rs. 1250.00 lakh has been released. 
7.1.10 Achievements and Challenges
 Y To focus on eviction of forest land encroachments, mutation of forest lands in revenue records, 
implementation of the Forest Rights Act (FRA), boundary consolidation, biodiversity conservation, and 
mitigation of human–wildlife conflict.
 Y During April-December 2025, 2,520 acres of forest land were reclaimed from encroachment in 463 cases. 
However, eviction remains pending in 1,22,201 cases, involving 2,15,393 acres, indicating the scale and 
complexity of the challenge. To strengthen monitoring, the Department has operationalized a Satellite 
Surveillance System (Forest Cover Change Alert System), which generates real-time alerts based on 
satellite imagery, enabling prompt field action and initiation of proceedings under Section 64(A) of the 
Karnataka Forest Act, 1963.
 Y The State has a total forest area of 40,67,823 hectares, of which 30,27,799 hectares have been mutated 
in revenue records, achieving 74 percent progress. Mutation of the remaining 10,40,024 hectares is 
under various stages of completion.
 Y According to the progress report provided by the social welfare department, implementation of the Forest 
Rights Act continues alongside conservation objectives. As of December 2025, 2.95 lakh applications were 
received, of which 16,700 title deeds were distributed. 16,043 applications remain under consideration, 
while 2.62 lakh applications were rejected due to various reasons.
 Y To strengthen protection of forest boundaries, an allocation of Rs.1,800.00 lakh was made during 2025-
26 under Capital Outlay on Forestry and Wildlife. Against Rs.500.00 lakh released, an expenditure of 
Rs.423.21 lakh (as on 19.01.2026) was incurred for survey, demarcation and boundary consolidation, 
resulting in the construction of 6.24 km of compound wall, 13.08 km of barbed wire fencing, and 2.27 
km of chain-link fencing.

 Y The Department manages an extensive protected area network comprising 5 National Parks, 37 Wildlife 
Sanctuaries (including 5 Tiger Reserves), 19 Conservation Reserves and 1 Community Reserve, covering 
11,399.49 sq. km, which constitutes 26.08% of the State’s forest area. Sustained conservation measures 
have yielded positive outcomes, with Karnataka ranking second in the country for tiger population (563 
tigers, 2022 estimation) and first in elephant population (6,395 elephants, 2023 estimation).
 Y To mitigate human-wildlife conflict, the State has created 428 km of railway barricades, 1,360.87 km of 
solar fencing, and 1,775.41 km of elephant-proof trenches. Institutional measures include the declaration 
of Hesarghatta Grassland as a Conservation Reserve and the launch of a Bandipur Elephant Task Force in 
2024-25.
 Y Afforestation and greening initiatives continued during 2025-26, with 2.87 crore saplings planted over

agroforestry programmes. Urban environmental quality was enhanced through the State Sector Tree 
Park Scheme, providing green recreational spaces in towns and cities.

which Rs.9.91 lakh was realized up to December 2025. Additionally, 87.91 tonnes of quality seeds were 
collected and distributed to research circles and field units. Research proposals were vetted through 
the Research Advisory Committee (RAC), while the ICT Center continued to expand digital platforms to 
improve transparency, accountability and process automation in forest governance.
Major IT systems including the below mentioned applications are developed and deployed:
1. e-Parihara: Online system for processing of ex-gratia sanctions to the aggrieved in case of man-wild 
animal conflict cases
2. e-Timber: Management of timber depot stocks in Government Timber depots across the State and 
e-auctioning of timber and other forest produce through online platform.
3. Sawmill Management System: Online system for renewal of Sawmill licenses across the State and 
management of wood consumption.
4. Forest Produce Tracking System: Monitoring of transit of mineral ore from forest leases, from source to 
sink. Issuance of online transit permits for transportation of ore.
5. e-Sasyakshetra: Online portal for management of seedling stock across forest nurseries. Provision for 
query on seedling availability and its subsequent disposal to public and departmental plantations.
6. e-Felling and Transit Permission System: Online system for according permission for obtaining permission 
to fell trees grown on private lands and subsequent approvals for removal of such felled material.
7. Compendium of HR Database:  Exhaustive database of Forest frontline staff. Transfer and Counselling 
Management System for frontline staff. Application for “Aranya Keerti” system for processing applications 
for Chief Minister’s medal for meritorious service.
8. e-Evaluation: Online system for evaluating various departmental works implemented under various 
schemes. Valuating the success of implementation of schemes and models and their effectiveness.
9. Forest Geospatial Information System: Compendium of all forest notifications and cadastral level 
geospatial databaseof all forest lands.
10. Forest Fire Management and Analysis Portal:  GIS, Remote sensing and MIS based system for 
dissemination of forest fire alerts and end to end system for capturing mitigation measures and with a 
forest fire forecasting model.

7.1.11 Karnataka Biodiversity Board
The Karnataka Biodiversity Board was constituted on 01.08.2003 under Section 22 of the Biological Diversity 
Act, 2002, with the mandate of sustainable management of biological resources and equitable sharing of 
benefits arising from their use.To operationalise the Act, Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) 
have been constituted in all Gram, Taluk and Zilla Panchayats, as well as Urban Local Bodies across the State 
following the amendment to the Act in 2023, conservation of biodiversity at the local level is undertaken 
through these committees.
The Board regularly conducts training programmes, workshops and awareness campaigns for communities, 
line department officials and frontline forest staff on biodiversity conservation, sustainable use of biological 
resources and implementation of the Act.
Objectives of the Board
1. The c onservation of biological diversity.
2. The sus tainable use of the components of biological diversity.
3. The f air and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of the utilization of biological resources.

7.1.12 Coastal Regulation Zone Management
As per the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) Notification S.O. 19(E) dated 
06.01.2011, the coastal stretches up to 500 metres from the High Tide Line (HTL) on the landward side, areas 
up to 12 nautical miles seaward, and tidally influenced water bodies and their banks (up to 100 metres) 

PDF_PAGE 281
273
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
are notified as Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ). These areas are classified into four categories—CRZ-I to CRZ-
IV—based on ecological sensitivity and land-use patterns, with specific regulatory norms and enforcement 
mechanisms.
The Karnataka State Coastal Zone Management Authority (KSCZMA) has been constituted under the 
chairmanship of the Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment, to ensure 
compliance with CRZ provisions. The revised Coastal Zone Management Plan (CZMP), prepared by the 
National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), Chennai, under the CRZ Notification, 2011, 
was approved by MoEF & CC on 07.08.2018, with further approval for revised CZMP maps accorded on 
02.09.2022 under CRZ Notification, 2019.
In compliance with the Hon’ble NGT directions (OA No. 04/2013 dated 11.04.2022), the Government of 
Karnataka engaged NCSCM to prepare a Shoreline Management Plan (SMP). Accordingly, the SMP for the  
320 km Karnataka coastline was submitted by NCSCM on 07.11.2024.
7.2  WATER RESOURCES
The Water Resources Department (Major and Medium Irrigation) is one of the major Department in the 
Government of Karnataka. Irrigation is an important source of raising productivity in agricultural sector. 
Annual rainfall of the State is 1,355 mm. More than 73% of this rainfall is received from the  South – West 
monsoon. Expansion of both the groundwater and surface water resources has helped to increase the  
cultivated area under irrigation in the state over time. Around 80% of fresh water is used for irrigation purpose 
and remaining for domestic, industry purposes.

7.2.6 Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam (KBJNL)
The Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam was established by the Govt. of Karnataka vide G.O. Dtd:06.05.1994 under 
Companies Act 1956 to accelerate the implementation of Upper Krishna Project and to enable the Govt. to 
borrow funds from external sources. This Nigam started functioning from 19.08.1994.
(A) Implementation of Upper Krishna Project
(a) Upper Krishna Project Stage – I &II 
The Upper Krishna Project Stage I & II (UKP Stage-I&II) was envisaged for utilization of 173 TMC allocated 
under Krishna Water Dispute Tribunal Award–I (KWDT-I) to provide irrigation for 6.22 Lakh Hectare in Yadgir, 
Kalaburgi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot & Raichur Districts of Northern Karnataka. UKP Stage-I&II are completed in 
2012-13 and Irrigation Potential of 6.20 Lakh Hectare has been created and completion report of the projects 
submitted to Central Water Commission (CWC). 
(b) Upper Krishna Project Stage – III
The Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-II (KWDT-II) has passed an award in December, 2010 and Further Report 
in 2013 allocating 173 TMC of water to the Karnataka State. Out of this, 130 TMC is the share of Upper Krishna 
Project Stage-III (UKP Stage-III). The KWDT-II Award is yet to be Gazetted by Govt. of India
The utilization of allocated 130 TMC under UKP Stage-III involves raising the storage at Almatti Reservoir from 
RL:519.60 Mt to RL:524.256 Mt. (additional storage of 100 TMC) and it is contemplated to provide irrigation 
for 5.94 lakh Hectares of command area in Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Kalaburgi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal and Gadag 
districts of Northern Karnataka.  
The Govt. of Karnataka had accorded administrative approval to the Revised Estimated cost of UKP Stage-III 
for Rs.51,148.94 Crore (2014-15 price level), vide GO Dtd:09.10.2017. The cost of LAQ and R&R of UKP Stage-
III is Rs.30,143.17 Crore. 
Under UKP Stage-III, the works under 9 Project Sub components, viz; Mulwad, Chimmalgi, Mallabad, Herkal, 
Koppal LIS, Indi & Rampur LIS Extension, Narayanpur Right Bank Canal Extension and Bhima Flank are in 
various stage of progress. 
The implementation of UKP Stage-III also involves Acquisition of 1,33,867 Acres of Land and Rehabilitation 
and Resettlement (R&R) of 20 Villages to be submerged under backwaters of Almatti Reservoir including R&R 
of part of Bagalkot Town.

(A) Implementation of Projects under VJNL 
(a) Upper Bhadra Project 
Upper Bhadra Project envisage providing irrigation for 2,25,515 Hectares (5,57,022 Acres) of land in drought-
prone areas of Chitradurga, Chikkamagaluru, Davangere, and Tumkur districts of Central Karnataka through a 
Micro-Irrigation system and to fill 367 tanks in these districts to their 50% capacity.
Govt. of Karnataka has accorded the administrative approval to the Re-revised DPR of the Bhadra Upper 
Project amounting to Rs. 21,473.67 Crore vide G.O. Dtd:16.12.2020.
The Project in the first stage involve lifting of water from the Tunga River to the Bhadra Reservoir (Package 1) 
and is in progress and it is planned to complete the work by March 2026. Further, the works of lifting 29.90 
TMC of water from Bhadra Reservoir to Ajjampura Tunnel (Package-2) and conveying water to Chitradurga 
Branch Canal (CBC) &  Tumkur Branch Canal (TBC) through Ajjampura Tunnel (Package-3) are completed. Also 
water has been released to Vani Vilasa Sagar Reservoir since 2019–20.
Under Stage-2 of the Project works of Tarikere Lift Scheme, Chitradurga Branch Canal, Tumkur Branch Canal 
works are in various stage of progress.  Further, the Micro-irrigation works taken up under Chitradurga, 
Tumkur and Jagalur Branch and Tank filling works in Hosadurga, Holalkere, Jagaluru, Challakere, Molakalmuru 
and Pavagada taluks under Chitradurga Branch Canal, as well as in Sira, Hiriyuru & Chikkanayakanahalli taluks 
under Tumkur Branch Canal are also at different stages of progress.
The Central Government in the Budget Speech of 2023-24, announced amount of  Rs.5,300.00 Crore as 
Central Assistance to the Upper Bhadra Project. The Government of Karnataka has requested Govt. of India 
for early release of grants to UBP under the PMKSY-AIBP Scheme. 
Cumulative expenditure incurred up to end of December 2025 is Rs.11329.84 Crore.
(b) Yettinahole Drinking Water Project
To mitigate the problem of acute drinking water in drought prone areas especially in Chikkaballapur, Kolar 
Districts and other needy areas of Hassan, Chitradurga, Tumakuru, Bengaluru South, and Bengaluru Rural 
Districts, the Govt. of Karnataka has accorded administrative approval to re-revised DPR of Yettinahole 
Drinking Water Project amounting to Rs.23,251.66 Crore vide G.O. Dtd:10.01.2023 for diverting 24.01 TMC 
of water to cater the drinking water needs and filling up of 527 MI Tanks to its 50% capacity for ground water 
recharge. The project has been taken up in two stages. 
Under Stage-I of the project lift component and electrical works were completed and successfully 
commissioned and was inaugurated by the Hon’ble Chief Minister and Hon’ble Deputy Minister, Govt. of 
Karnataka on 06.09.2024. 79.50 Cumecs of water has been lifted to DC-4 and conveyed upto Km.32.50 of 
Gravity Canal. Further, 1.15 TMC of water had been temporarily let out to Vani Vilasa Sagara through Veda 
valley from Canal Escape at Km.32.50, during 2024-25 & 2.13 TMC during current water year 2025-26.

7.2.9 Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited (CNNL)
The Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited (CNNL) was established by the Government of Karnataka on 03.06.2003 
under Companies Act 1956 to accelerate the implementation of Cauvery Basin Projects in Karnataka. 
The Cauvery basin in Karnataka is 34,273 Sq.Kms which constitutes about 17.99% of the geographical area of 
1,91,791 Sq.Km in Karnataka. Major Rivers flowing in this basin are Harangi (50 KM), Hemavathy (245 KM), 
Lakshmanatheertha (131 KM), Kabini (230 KM), Shimsha (221 KM), Suvarnvathi (88 KM), Arkavathy (161 KM) 
and the main river Cauvery (381 KM). The Cauvery Basin is spread across 11 districts.
(A) Implementation of Projects under CNNL 
There are totally 29 potential oriented schemes taken up under the jurisdiction of CNNL, out of which 4 are 
Major Projects, 18 are Medium irrigation Projects and 7 allied LIS which are completed. Presently, the works 
under Yagachi Project and Kachenahalli Lift Irrigation Schemes are in progress.
(a) Yagachi Project
The project envisages the construction of a composite Dam across Yagachi River a tributary of Hemavathy 
near Chikkabyadagere village in Belur taluk of Hassan district.
The planned utilisation under the project is 5.74 TMC to create an ultimate irrigation potential of 15,575 
Hectare including Kyathanahalli LIS. The taluk benefitted by this project are Hassan, Belur and Alur of Hassan 
District. 
Kyathanahalli LIS is a part of Yagachi Project and is completed. Kamasamudra Branch Canal under Yagachi 
Project is under progress. The irrigation potential created under Yagachi project (including Kyathanahalli LIS) 
since inception to the end of December 2025 is 10,148 Ha. 
(b) Kachenahally LIS
The project envisages to lift 0.73 TMC of water in 3 Stages from Hemavathy River near Kachenahally Village 
in Channarayapatna taluk of Hassan District. The ultimate potential to be created is 5,100 Hectare. 1st Stage 
works are completed. In The 2nd Stage Main Canal is completed and Distributary Network are under progress. 
Irrigation potential created under Kachenahally since inception to the end of December 2025 is 2,428 Ha.  
(c) Modernisation of Anicut Canals
Under the jurisdiction of CNNL, 26 Anicut Canals/ Branch Canal modernization project works are taken up in 
phases with the total estimated cost of Rs.1,831.00 Crore. Among these, 23 works are completed and three 
works are under progress. The cumulative expenditure incurred up to end of November-2024 is Rs.1,790.47 
Crore.
(d)  Improvements of Canal System
Total 61 modernization works at a cost of Rs.4,924.34 Crore have been taken up in CNNL out of which 32 
works are completed, 17 works are under progress and Tender in under process for 12 works. Cumulative 
expenditure incurred up to end of December 2025 is Rs.3077.02 Crore.

7.2.10 Inter-Linking of River Projects
(a) Godavari - Cauvery link and Bedthi-Varada (Hirevaddatti) Link
The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) under the Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS) has proposed the 
implementation of diversion of 147.93 TMC surplus waters in Godavari basin to Cauvery through Godavari 
-Krishna - Pennar - Palar – Cauvery link (Godavari-Cauvery Link) project.
The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has proposed a total allocation of 34.40 TMC of water for 
Karnataka, including 15.90 TMC of water under the Godavari-Cauvery Link Project and 18.50 TMC of water 
under the Bedthi-Varada (Hirevaddati) Link Project. The state has given its consent to the NWDA for the 
preparation of the DPR for the Bedthi-Varada (Hirevaddati) Link Project.
The State of Karnataka has urged before the NWDA and Ministry of Jal Shakti for considering the equitable 
allocation under Godavari-Cauvery Link Project on par with other beneficiary States viz., Telangana, Andhra 
Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
(b) Krishna (Almatti) - Pennar Link
Krishna (Almatti) – Pennar Link Project envisages transfer of surplus waters of 1558 MCM (55 TMC) from 
Almatti Reservoir that would be available due to the transfer of surplus water from Mahanadi & Godavari 
Rivers to Krishna, by way of successive substitution.

7.2.12 Major Achievements of Department during 2025-26
Financial and Physical Progress
A total grant of Rs.18,826.93 Crore has been provided to the Water Resources Department (Major and 
Medium Irrigation) for 2025-26. By the end of December 2025, Rs.8,980.00 Crore has been achieved and 
59,181 Acres (23,960 Hectare) of irrigation potential has been created. 
Replacement of all 33 Gates of Tungabhadra Reservoir
In the wake of the emergency situation in which Spillway Gate No.19 of the Tungabhadra Reservoir was 
washed away last year, the Tungabhadra Board has decided to replace all the 33 gates and has awarded the 
replacement of gates work on tender basis. Currently, out of the 33 spillway gates, the fabrication of 15 gates 
has been completed, the fabrication of 8 gates is in progress, and the installation work of Gate No.18 is in 
progress.
Mekedatu Project
Mekedatu Project envisages the construction of a Dam with a storage of 67 TMC of water across the main 
river Cauvery. The Project envisages (a) Utilization of 4.75 TMC (Consumptive Use) for drinking purposes 
including Bengaluru, (b) to regulate the monthly flows to Tamil Nadu at Biligundulu & (c) Generation of Power 
of 400 MW.
The Hon’ble Supreme Court on 13.11.2025 dismissed all the cases filed by the State of Tamil Nadu against 
Karnataka in connection with the implementation of the state’s ambitious Mekedatu balancing reservoir 
project in the Cauvery Basin.
To expedite the works related to Mekedatu project, a team of officials to work under the Director, KERS has 
been constituted. Further, a suitable office in Bengaluru South has also been ordered for its establishment for 
the working of said team. 
The State Government has urged the Ministry of Jal Shakti and Central Water Commission, GoI, to take up the 
appraisal of DPR of Mekedatu Project expeditiously and accord requisite approval to the project, since there 
is no impediment from the legal or any other point in view.

Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Rules, 2025
The Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Rules, 2025, has been officially notified in the Karnataka Gazette on 
17.12.2025. The said Rules provide the specific, procedural details for implementing the broader, substantive 
framework for the provisions of the Act including Karnataka Irrigation (Amendment) Bill, 2024. 
State Water Policy – Meetings of High Level Water Policy Committee & Inter-Departmental State 
Water Resources Authority
The State of Karnataka has brought in “State Water Policy, 2022” in August-2022. The policy was framed to 
address the new challenges and to make it more comprehensively Integrated Water Resource Management 
(IWRM) oriented in order to address the growing inter-sectoral demands of water and ensure water, food and 
economic security of the State.
During 2025-26, Meeting of 3rd High Level Water Policy Committee under the Chairmanship of Chief Secretary 
to Govt. has been conducted on 16.04.2025.  Further, 1st meeting of the ‘Inter-Departmental State Water 
Resources Authority’ under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Deputy Chief Minister, and Hon’ble Minister for 
Water Resources, Govt. of Karnataka is held on 16.12.2025 at Suvarna Soudha, Belagavi. 
Study on Pollution in Vrishabhavati and Arkavati Valleys
A Committee comprising Technical Experts and Departmental Officers, has been constituted vide Govt. Order 
Dtd:13.06.2025 to conduct an extensive study on the pollution of Vrishabhavati and Arkavati valleys and to 
suggest measures to prevent pollution for safe environment and ecology of the valleys. 
Performance study of lift Irrigation Schemes
The Government has constituted a Committee vide Govt. Order Dtd:22.09.2025, comprising Public 
representatives and Retired Officers/ Technical Experts, to undertake studies on performance of the Lift  
Irrigation Schemes under the purview of State Water Resources Department and Minor Irrigation to give its 
suggestions / recommendations to enhance the performance of LI Schemes and their efficiency levels. 
Committee of Technical Experts to formulate plans to bring dry land in the state under irrigation
A Committee of Technical Experts has been constituted to formulate the plans for effective utilization of 
water resources in the State, conduct comprehensive study for bringing dry land in the State under irrigation, 
monitor the natural resources and water requirements of the coastal area. 
Committee for finalizing Uniform Guidelines and Procedure for Preparation of Estimate, DPR & 
DTP (Standardization)
A Committee has been constituted vide Govt. Order Dtd:12.06.2025 to prepare Uniform Technical Standards/
Guidelines for preparation of Estimates/DPRs/DTPs under the four Nigam of Water Resources Department. The 
suggestions / recommendations of the said Committee will facilitate way forward for effective implementation 
and management of projects being undertaken in the Water Resources Department. 
Re-constitution of State Committee of Dam Safety (SCDS)
For proper surveillance, inspection, operation and maintenance of the specified dams and for prevention of 
dam failure related disaster and to provide for institutional mechanism to ensure their safe functioning, State 
Committee of Dam Safety has been re-constituted vide Govt. Order Dtd:22.08.2025.

7.2.13 Challenges
 Y Delay in land acquisition process: The progress of the projects is being hampered due to the delay 
caused in the land acquisition process and court litigations for seeking higher compensation by land 
owners. 
 Y  Balance Cost of Projects : The total balance cost of projects being implemented under the department is 
more than Rs.1.00 lakh crore. However, the annual budget provided to the department is subject to limit, 
leading to slow progress of projects.
 Y  Delay in release of Central Assistance : Delay in release of Central Assistance from Govt. of India for the 
ongoing projects undertaken for implementation under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS), has led to 
the slow progress of the projects.
 Y  In ter-State Water Disputes : Delay in adjudication of long pending cases in Tribunals/Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, related to Inter-State Water Disputes effecting the implementation of projects and utilizing 
allocated water to the State by the Tribunal Awards. 
 Y Climate Change Impacts: Erratic rainfall and prolonged droughts impacting river flows and overall supply.
 Y Irrigation Inefficiency: Agriculture consumes most water, but productivity and efficiency need significant 
improvement for better water management.
 Y Financial Sustainability: Nigams under WRD struggle with low cost recovery of water charges effecting 
insufficient revenue needed to maintain and expand infrastructure. 
7.2.14  Way Forward
 Y Integrated Water Management
 ) River Basin Planning: Comprehensive management of river valleys and groundwater.
 ) Stakeholder Participation: Involving farmers and users in water management policy.
 Y  Supply Augmentation & Treatment
 ) Treated Wastewater Reuse: Developing strong policies and infrastructure for using treated sewage 
in agriculture, industry, and non-potable urban uses. 
 ) Tank Rejuvenation: Restoring tanks to act as sources for groundwater recharge.
 Y  Demand Management & Efficiency
 ) Efficient Irrigation: Promoting micro-irrigation (drip, sprinkler) and low-water-consumption crops 
in agriculture.
 ) Water Use Efficiency (WUE): Improving water productivity in all sectors.
 Y Technological & Infrastructure Modernization
 ) Smart Water Grids: Leveraging technology for better water monitoring and management.
 ) Leakage Reduction: Modernizing irrigation distribution networks to reduce losses.
 Y Policy & Governance
 ) Future Utility: Transforming water entities into future-ready utilities.
 ) Establishing State Water Commission: To scientifically manage water resources, advise on 
conservation, resolve inter-state water disputes, plan for future demand, and guide sustainable 
irrigation.

7.2.15 Minor Irrigation (Surface water)
Projects having atchkat up to 2,000 Ha. are classified as Minor Irrigation schemes. Projects having atchkat 
between 40 Ha to 2,000 Ha are under the jurisdiction of the Minor Irrigation Department.  These include tanks, 
pickup, Bhandaras, Barrages and Lift Irrigation Schemes.  These Minor Irrigation projects are widely spread all 
over the state. Presently, there are 12,591 minor irrigation projects in existence under the jurisdiction of this 
Department with a cultivable command area of 9,33,230 hectares.  
Minor Irrigation Department is having 3242 Irrigation tanks and 539 Percolation tanks. These tanks are being 
inspected twice in a year by the concerned Executive Engineers and Assistant Executive Engineer. The defects 
noticed during inspection will be recorded in the inspection report. Necessary repair works will be taken up 
from the grants made available during the year on priority. The minor irrigation scheme progress from the 
year 2020-21 to 2025-26 (Upto end of the December 2025) is provided in the Table 7.30.

7.2.16 State Schemes
Construction of new tanks: Under this head of account, new tanks are constructed and water is being stored 
during rainy season to supplement the deficit of water to the crops during non-rainy period or scarce rainfall 
period. Earthen bunds are constructed across the rivers, streams etc., and the water is being stored during 
rainy season which will be utilized for irrigation during deficit rainfall period. The Minor Irrigation Department 
is involved in proper distribution of stored water to the fields for irrigation by gravity flow. Construction of 
new tank is being carried out from state fund and also from NABARD loan assistance. Construction of the 
Percolation tanks are also being done under this head of account which are mainly intended to recharge the 
Ground Water table and help in raising the water level in the bore wells and open wells in the surrounding 
area which will be used for irrigation.
Modernization of tank: Under this head of account, Department is taking up modernization of tanks under 
which the works such as strengthening of bund, repair of waste weirs, canals including lining of canals are 
being taken up.  
Construction of Barrage, Anicut, Etc. Under this head of account, Department is taking up the construction of 
barrages, bridge cum barrages, vented dams, salt water exclusion dams, anicut and pick-ups across rivers and 
streams to store water.  Permission is being given to the farmers to lift water from these storage structures for 
irrigation by using their own pumps. As a result, there will be increase in ground water table in the surrounding 
area and water will be available in the open wells and bore wells.  Thereby, farmers will get water for irrigation 
and also drinking purposes. 
Lift Irrigation Schemes: Under this head of account, Department is implementing the lift irrigation schemes 
to lift water from the rivers, streams, and other surface water sources to an elevated area and to provide 
irrigation to the farmer lands.

PDF_PAGE 296
288
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Apart from this water is lifted and pumped to tanks under tank filling schemes. Also, the secondary treated 
water of Bengaluru City is pumped to tanks in Bengaluru Rural, Bengaluru urban, Bengaluru South, Kolar, 
Chikkaballapur and Tumakuru Districts under Tank filling Schemes. 
Special Component Plan : Under this head of account, department has taken up MI Schemes such as 
construction of new tanks, anecut / pickup bhandars, modernization of tanks and lift irrigation schemes etc., 
to create irrigation facility to the lands belonging to scheduled caste beneficiaries. 
An expenditure of Rs.103.36 Crore is incurred against the grant of Rs.350.00 Crore during 2025-26 (End of 
December 2025). Irrigation facility of 1696.02 Ha is created against the target of 3501.69 Ha. during 2025-26 
(End of December 2025).  These schemes are being handed over to respective beneficiaries after construction.
Tribal Sub plan: Under this head of account, department has taken up MI schemes such as construction of 
new tanks, anecut,pickup bhandars, modernization of tanks and lift irrigation schemes etc., to create irrigation 
facility to the lands belonging to scheduled tribe beneficiaries.
An expenditure of Rs.55.65 Crore is incurred against the grant of Rs.170.10 Crore during 2025-26 (End of 
December 2025). Irrigation facility of 1160.75 Ha is created against the target of 2226 Ha. 2025-26 (End of 
December 2025). These schemes are being handed over to respective beneficiaries after construction.
Pashchima Vahini: Vented dams are constructed under “PaschimaVahini” project to collect and store water 
flowing in west-flowing rivers of coastal districts. A total of 280 works have been approved under the scheme, 
with an estimated cost of Rs.104.36 crore.  An expenditure of Rs.66.67 crore is incurred against the grant of 
Rs.100 crore during 2025-26 (End of December 2025).
Land Acquisition/charges & settlement of claims: Under this head of account, an expenditure of Rs.81.55 
crore is incurred against the grant of 100.00 crore during 2025-26 (End of December 2025). Mainly this grant 
has been utilized to make payments to land acquisition cases involving enhancement of land values including 
the interest as per the court orders.
Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP) Major works: Government of India is giving approval for 
taking up of the new minor irrigation works involving the creation of fresh irrigation facility since 2009-10, 
in the Drought Prone Area Development Programme (DPAP) taluks under Accelerated Irrigation Benefit 
Programme (AIBP).
Minor irrigation department is implementing 1,273 minor irrigation works with an estimated cost of Rs.955.08 
crore after obtaining approval to these works in 10 batches since 2009-10.  So far 1,157 works are completed 
and the new irrigation facility is created in  10,255.00 Ha.
State Schemes Flood Control Works: The Department is implementing River bank protection works to prevent 
damages due to floods.   The river banks are being protected by the construction of retaining wall to the river 
banks for the prevention of loss of lives and properties due to the erosion of the banks during the floods in 
rivers and streams.  
Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority: The Authority started functioning from December 
2017.  The functions of Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority include Conservation of 
Lakes/Tanks, rejuvenation, Ground Water Development, Environmental Protection, Wet Land Development, 
Water Management, Agriculture and Horticulture Development, Development of Agriculture based Industries 
etc., either directly or through Departments/Agencies.

7.2.18 Way Forward
Promote sustainable agri-practices by creating awareness of the existing schemes around subsidizing micro-
irrigation (Per Drop More Crop, Micro-Irrigation Fund), preserving soil health (Paramparagat Krishi Vikas 
Yojana, Soil Health Card) and host of initiatives under National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. Prioritize 
districts like Belagavi, Raichur, Vijayapura, Bagalkot which have high potential for micro irrigation.
A holistic approach including precision farming, protective cultivation, automation in irrigation, fertigation, 
use of treated waste water for irrigation and collective farming are some of the methods suggested to address 
major concern of water scarcity in the state. A marked shift from traditional method of irrigation to innovative 
micro irrigation system is the solution to conserve  water and thus increase the availability of water for various 
other purposes. Adoption of poly houses, net houses, green houses will not only save water, energy and 
labour costs but also will increase crop productivity and quality of the produce. Converting more and more 
areas of canal based and tank based flood irrigated land into drip irrigation leading to substantial reduction in 
the usage of fresh water. These key measures are expected reduce water scarcity to a large extent in the state.
NEERIDDARE NALE 
“Neeriddare Nale” (meaning “Water is Future”) is a Karnataka government initiative launched in October 
2025 to conserve groundwater, boost water table levels, and raise awareness in overexploited areas, involving 
AI for monitoring, lake rejuvenation, and community participation, with actor Vasishta Simha as its brand 
ambassador. 
Key Aspects of the Initiative
 Y Goal: Develop groundwater, conserve traditional water sources, and manage water sustainably.
 Y Scope: Implemented in 525 Gram Panchayats across 27 taluks in 15 critical districts.
 Y Technology: Plans to use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to monitor groundwater in thousands of lakes.
 Y Activities: Includes lake rejuvenation, which has already shown improved water tables and increased 
agricultural output.
 Y Brand Ambassador: Actor Vasishta Simha appointed to connect with the youth on water conservation. 
Why it Matters
 Y Addresses severe water scarcity and groundwater depletion in many parts of Karnataka.
 Y Focuses on community involvement and sustainable practices for long-term water security.

7.3 GEOLOGY AND MINING SECTOR 
INTRODUCTION
The Department of Mines and Geology is one of the leading scientific and technical department of the State 
with a long history of 131 years. Major functional activities of the department include mineral exploration, 
assessment of mineral wealth, quality analysis, sanctioning of mining leases and quarrying leases through 
the minerals administration which also include collection of royalty and regulation of unauthorized mining 
activities. The contribution of the department is immense in sustainable development of the State by 
promoting environment friendly and scientific mining.

7.3.2 Major Achievements of the Department
 Y To supervise all mineral transportation vehicles movement from the centralized tracking platform of 
Department and to regulate illegal mineral transportation “One State One GPS” application has been 
introduced on 08.03.2023. All major and minor minerals transporting vehicles fitted with AIS-140 
certified GPS devices and to integrate with “One State One GPS” centralized system and with regard 
to monitoring the movement of all mineral-transporting vehicles registered under the said centralized 
system. Till now, 69,000 vehicles have been registered in One State One GPS and also Rs.10.00 crores fine 
has been collected from vehicles violating the rules.
 Y In the current financial year, a total of 10,264 mineral transportation vehicles have been registered 
under the said centralized system, and a total fine of Rs.2.98 crores has been collected from various GPS 
violation cases.
 Y In order to computerize the mineral administration of the department a new application called ILMS 
(Integrated Lease Management System) has been developed by the Centre for Smart Governance with 
new technology and has been successfully implemented on 12.12.2024. In continuation of this, in 2nd 
phase of the new ILMS software development, design work and new sub-modules such as mineral sample 
collection and analysis, EODBS, e-market reservation, DCB and auditing, Integrated CCTV surveillance, 
Fine and fee collection system, integration with RTO, GST, PAN, Conveyor, IBM, PGS & auction platform, 
role wise real time dashboard development is under progress.
 Y The Karnataka Minor Minerals Rules, 1994 have been amended to make it mandatory to generate e-way 
bill through the Goods and Services Tax portal for the transportation of minor minerals, accordingly 
notification has been made vide No.CI/MMN/137/2025, dated: 20.09.2025.  It is expected to generate 
additional revenue by preventing royalty and GST evasion.
 Y Karnataka State Remote Sensing Application Center has been awarded to carry out Drone/DGPS survey 
in the quarry leased areas in all the districts of the state to freeze the existing ground level (Reduced 
Level). At present in all the districts Drone/DGPS survey is completed and the data processing work is 
under progress.
 Y Karnataka Minor Mineral Concession (Amendment) Rules-2023 and 2024 are being implemented to 
provide sand to the public and government works at fixed rates by transparently allotting sand blocks

7.3.5 National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust
As per the section 9(C) of Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2015, all the 
major mineral lease holders are required to pay 2% of the royalty to the National Mineral Exploration and 
Development Trust (NMEDT) constituted by the Government of India. This fund is managed by the Central 
Government and by utilizing these funds upon taking the concurrence of respective State DMG’s and within 
the approval of NMEDT the agencies notified by the Central Government like GSI, MECL and KIOCL etc., and 
also through the concerned State Mines and Geology Departments, exploration activities of major minerals 
is being carried out.
During the period 2015-16 to 2025-26 (up to December 2025) an amount of Rs.5115.58 lakhs has been

7.3.8 Minor Mineral Administration
723 specified minor mineral quarry leases (including ornamental granite) over an extent of 3380 acres and 
3286 non-specified minor mineral quarry leases (excluding ordinary sand) over an extent of 12216 acres 
have been granted in the State of Karnataka. In this year, till December 2025, the department has granted/
executed 171 non-specified minor mineral over an extent of 867 acres and 44 specified minor mineral over 
an extent of 201 acres quarry leases.
Sand Mining as per Karnataka Minor Mineral Concession (Amendment) Rules – 2023 & 2024
 Y  The Government has issued guidelines and tender document on 03.12.2024 for the disposal of sand 
blocks available in the high order stream/river beds available in the State through tender for sand mining 
from Government-owned institutions/Government departments. Sand contractors who have obtained 
contracts through tender have been permitted to supply sand to the public and for government works at 
the fixed rate of Rs.850/- per unit.
 Y  Acc ordingly, at present, a total of 338 sand blocks have been identified in IV, V order streams and higher 
order stream/river beds in the State for granting sand mining lease through public tender. Out of these, 
42 sand blocks have been reserved for government works. Notification has been issued for auctioning 
270 sand blocks, and currently, 248 sand blocks have been brought under the e-tender process. The 
auction process has been completed for 172 sand blocks, out of which 44 bids have been rejected. Letters 
of intent have been issued for 106 sand blocks. The auction process is in progress for 76 sand blocks. 
Further, necessary steps are being taken to auction the 44 rejected sand blocks and 26 non-notified sand 
blocks through tender process.

7.3.9 District Mineral Foundation Trust
Government of India has amended the MMDR Act w.e.f 12.01.2015 where in under Section 9(B) a provision 
has been made to establish a trust called the “District Mineral Foundation” which is a non-profit body to 
formulate and implement programs for the development of the people living in the mine-affected area and 
supplemented by the guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Khanija Kshetra  Kalyana  Yojana issued on 16.09.2015.
The State Government vide G.O. dated 05.11.2015 notified the establishment of District Mineral Foundation 
(DMF) in each of the district of Karnataka. Further, the State Government, in exercise of the powers conferred 
by Section 15(4) of MMDR Act, framed the Rules of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) on 11.01.2016 under 
the guidelines of Pradhan Mantri KhanijKhsethra Kalyan Yojan (PMKKKY) and same has been amended on 
25.07.2016, 08.03.2018 and 06.05.2020.
In respect of major mineral, Government of India vide Notification dated: 17.09.2015 has directed to collect 
the DMF from
(i) Min ing lease granted after 12.01.2015, Collection of DMF amount at the rate of 10% on royalty.
(ii) Col lection of DMF amount for Mining lease granted on or before 12.01.2015 at the rate of 30% on royalty. 
As per order dated: 13.10.2017 passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Transfer Case (Civil) No: 43/2016 
FIMI v/s Union of India and others, collection of royalty as per the DMF rules with effect from 17.09.2015. 
Accordingly, DMF amount is being collected from the mining lease holders.

7.3.10 Rule 18 of DMF Amendment Rules 2018
1. 10%  of the fund is earmarked for endowments purpose (as amended on 08.03.2018) after closure of 
mining activity in the affected areas.
2. 5% of the funds from DMF is earmarked for administrative purpose, out of which 4% is to be utilized for 
the administrative purpose at the District level and remaining 1% is to be transferred to the Department 
for the maintenance of the State Level Monitoring and Evaluation Cell and to meet the administrative 
expenses.
3. R emaining 85% shall be utilized for implementation of projects and schemes prescribed under Pradhan 
Mantri Khanij Khsethra Kalyan Yojana (PMKKKY) in the ratio of 60:40, for high priority areas and other 
priority areas, respectively.

7.3.11 Comprehensive Computerization of Mineral Administration
To deliver effective e-mineral administration in the Department of Mines and Geology, the Integrated Lease 
Management System (ILMS) was designed in 2011 and has been successfully implemented.
Under this centralized system, systematic and rule-based management and regulation of mining operations 
activities in mining lease and the transportation of minerals from the mining lease areas to end users are 
tracked digitally in real time. The system enables issuance of permits for mineral transportation, registration of 
mining lease holders and mineral-based industries, e-return submission by lease holders, mineral purchasers 
and mineral-based units, and integration with the Forest Department, (Forest Produce Tracking System - 
FPTS), Google and online payment through integration with the Treasury Department’s K-II software.
As information technology is changing rapidly, it is necessary to upgrade the mineral administration system in 
the department. This will help improve the quality of existing services and provide additional services so that 
the public and entrepreneurs can receive services on time.
Therefore, a work order has been issued to the Center for Smart Governance to design a new ILMS software 
similar to the current ILMS system, migrating the data from the existing ILMS in phase I and development of  
additional modules in Phase II.
Accordingly, in the first phase, CSG redesigned ILMS 1.0 and migrated the existing data. The new ILMS system 
was successfully implemented on 12-12-2024.
In the second phase, that is during the years 2025–26 and 2026–27, steps will be taken to develop the 
following modules.
1. KY C Module
2. e-Mark etplace Portal for Online Booking
3. Aut omated Acknowledgement of Mineral Receipt by End Users
4. R econciliation (Mineral Grade and Quantity/Value)

7.4 CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION MEASURES
7.4.1. Mainstreaming the Karnataka State Action Plan on Climate Change-State-Level Capacity 
Building on KSAPCC Monitoring Dashboard
To effectively implement the climate actions targeted under KSAPCC V.2, the Government of Karnataka has 
issued a G.O. (No. FEE 151 ENV 2024, dated 24.03.2025), enabling the departments to constitute committees 
to monitor and evaluate the progress of the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). A total of 15 departments 
have identified and initiated implementation of over 90 KPIs related to climate adaptation and mitigation 
across their respective programmes.
To support real-time monitoring, EMPRI, in partnership with the Centre for Environment Education (CEE-South), 
Bangalore, has developed the KSAPCC Monitoring Dashboard. A state-level hands-on training programme 
was conducted during 28–29 October 2025 at The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Bangalore, for over 95 nodal officials 
from 15 departments, enabling improved reporting efficiency and data-driven climate decision-making.
Figure 7.6 : Training to the departmental officials on KSAPCC Monitoring Dashboard https://ksapccmonitoring.in
7.4.2 Departmental Capacity Building and Trainings conducted by EMPRI
1) District-Level Trainings for Government Officials on State Climate Actions
To ensure climate-responsive planning at the district level, EMPRI has conducted capacity- building 
programmesfor the district-level officials across all 31 districts of Karnataka, covering over 10 different sectors 
including Agriculture, Forestry, Water, Livestock, Coastal and Fisheries, Energy, Health, Transport, Urban 
Development, and Waste Management.  A total of 1,447 government officials were trained. The trainings 
enhanced understanding of climate vulnerability, departmental KPIs, and the integration of climate adaptation 
and mitigation measures into local planning frameworks.
2) Radio Programme for Public Outreach – “Havamana Mitra”
To enhance public awareness and outreach on the climate change action plan in the state, EMPRI has 
launched the radio program“Havamana Mitra,” broadcasted through Akashavani (612 kHz). The programme 
aims to strengthen climate literacy, particularly among rural and agriculture-dependent communities. Of the 
24 programmes planned for the year, 15 have been successfully broadcasted, featuring experts, farmers, 
and government officials discussing climate-resilient agriculture, water conservation, sustainable resource 
practices, and heat preparedness measures.

7.5 KARNATAKA STATE NATURAL DISASTER MONITORING CENTRE - KSNDMC
Karnataka has been subjected to various Natural Disaster, both Hydro Meteorological and Geological 
successively every year. Devastating weather phenomena like successive Drought, Flood, Hailstorm, strong 
surface winds and intense vertical wind shear have been causing loss of life and property in the State as 
below:
 Y 80% of the Geographical area in the State is prone to Drought.
 Y 22% of the Geographical area in the State is prone to moderate earthquake risks.
 Y 24% of the Geographical area in the State is prone to cyclone and heavy winds.
 Y Landslides do affect the areas with slopes of more than 30%.
 Y The 320 k.m. coastal line is prone to sea erosion and Tsunami threat.
 Y Hailstorms are experienced almost every year and cause damages to crops, human lives and livestock.
 Y Thunderstorms, cloudburst and lightning cause considerable damages and loss to lives and properties.
 Y All the districts in the State are vulnerable to more than one natural hazard.
To monitor and mitigate the impact of these Disasters, for the first time in the Country, Govt. of Karnataka 
installed an Institutional Mechanism in the form of “Drought Monitoring Cell” (DMC) in 1988. Subsequently, 
DMC was renamed as “Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre” (KSNDMC) with a mandate of 
Monitoring all the Natural Disasters in the State. Since 2007, KSNDMC has taken up pioneering and path 
breaking initiatives towards monitoring all the Natural Disasters. 
KSNDMC has Core activities, which include maintaining and updating database on drought and flood 
parameters, preparation and issuance of periodical reports on drought indicators and conducting integrated 
studies on Drought Management in the Drought-prone districts of Karnataka.
Weather Monitoring
Karnataka, the 8th largest State in the Country in terms of geographical area (19.1M. sq.km) is one of the 
States having largest rainfed agriculture area in the Country heavily dependent on Monsoon rainfall, while the 
spatial and temporal distribution of rainfall varies significantly within the State. For implementing sustainable 
agriculture practices and protecting the livelihood of the farmers, the reliable weather data observed on the 
ground and weather forecast with a high spatial and temporal resolution are very important. Thus, in order to 
capture the variation in the rainfall distribution and to cater to the needs of weather information to different 
sectors, including the farming sector, a unique model of Weather Monitoring Network has been designed, 
developed and operationalised in the State by KSNDMC.
It has established a network of GPRS enabled and solar-powered 6,605 Telemetric Rain Gauges (TRG) at all 
the Grama Panchayaths at every 25 sq. km and 843 Telemetric Weather Stations (TWS) at all the Hoblis at 

PDF_PAGE 316
308
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
every 250 sq. km in the State. The weather data comprising Temperature (⁰C), Relative Humidity (%), Wind 
Speed (m/s), Wing Direction (Degrees), Rainfall amount (mm) and intensity (mm/hr). Data is being collected 
at every 15 minutes through these weather monitoring stations. The density of weather monitoring stations 
network is the highest and first of its kind in the country.
It generates Rainfall / Weather Forecast for Karnataka every day in collaboration with national agencies like 
Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmadabad and Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), Sriharikota, 
Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) and India Meteorological Department (IMD), MoES, Govt. of India. 
Short Range Weather Forecast: which Includes forecast for rainfall, temperature, cloud cover, wind speed 
and direction at Grama Panchayath level for the entire State. Rainfall related Drought indicators are rainfall 
deficiency, Dry spell standard precipitation index and moisture adequacy index.
Flood Monitoring
Flood is one of the most common and recurring Natural Disasters in the State, in the recent decades. Large 
parts of North Interior Karnataka, which is under Krishna River basin, is prone to severe floods. Similarly, the 
Malnad region and parts of South Interior Karnataka, which are in the Cauvery River basin, are also prone 
to floods and associated with landslides/mudflows. Heavy and high-intensity rainfall during the Monsoon 
season has been causing floods in one or the other parts of the State resulting in loss of life, livelihood, 
property, enormous damage to the standing crops, destroying critical infrastructure. Considering the flood 
severity over the State a dedicated Flood Forecast Cell with a group of officials was created at KSNDMC, which 
facilitates the stakeholders to take appropriate measures to mitigate the impact of floods, for providing flood 
forecast, alerts and early warnings. 
Urban Flood Monitoring
An integrated Urban Flood Monitoring Model for Bengaluru City (UFM) is being developed by KSNDMC 
in collaboration with Indian Institute of Science (IISc) Bengaluru, to manage floods in the city. An efficient 
forecast system with a well-established network of 100 Telemetric Rain gauge Sensors and 12 telemetric 
weather stations with integrated two-dimensional flood model, along with 26 water level sensors, provides 
information on the spread of the flood water (vis-à-vis flood inundation). An automated information 
dissemination Web Portal and a Mobile app named Bengaluru Meghasandesha (BMS) has been developed to 
disseminate relevant information to stakeholders.
KSNDMC has established a smart weather monitoring system comprising (75 Telemetric Rain Gauges, 29 
Telemetric Weather Sensors and 50 water level sensors) using an ICT enabled sensors network and hydrological 

PDF_PAGE 317
309
Natural Resource Management and Environment 
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
model. This system continuously monitor dynamic weather condition and provide S & T based inputs for 
effectively managing the urban flood events in Smart cities of Belagavi, Mangaluru and Hubballi-Dharawada.
Seismic Monitoring
KSNDMC at its Master Control Facility (MCF) is receiving the Seismic data on real time from the 14 remote 
Observatories through VSAT & GPRS modes. The data received to KSNDMC is being monitored by the scientific 
personnel and information pertaining to local earthquakes is being marked for further analysis. Necessary 
processing techniques are adopted by applying required filters to the recorded seismic data to enhance 
the seismic signal and suppress local noise level. The analyzed earthquake event is initially disseminated to 
officials of the District, Taluk, Grama Panchayath and Dam Authorities through SMS. Subsequently a technical 
report with be disseminated detailing the geology of the area where the tremor was felt, presenting the 
recorded seismograms with markings of primary and secondary waves, mapping the faults, major & minor 
lineaments in the area, (if any), and outlining Do’s & Don’ts during an earthquake along with safety measures 
for the local community.
The processed information from the above stations is also being made available to the users through the 
Centre’s web portal at www.ksndmc.org and via e-mails. To address the Seismicity in the State, KSNDMC 
has established a network of 14 VSAT enabled and solar powered permanent seismic monitoring stations at 
different vulnerable locations across the State. Through this network of Stations, KSNDMC is monitors local, 
regional and teleseismic earthquakes.
Early warning dissemination through centralized wireless broadcasting system
In order to provide early warning with sufficient lead time to the vulnerable community to take appropriate 
action and mitigate the impact of any disaster, a comprehensive Early Warning System with last mile 
connectivity is being installed in 104 highly disaster vulnerable Grama Panchayaths in Karnataka. The State-
of-the-art technology driven system is designed for disseminating necessary and precautionary messages 
through public announcements from central system directly to the vulnerable Grama Panchayaths. The 
solution follows a 3-tier system where messages can be relayed directly from State or District or Taluk 
Headquarters to the Grama Panchayaths.
Risk Transfer Mechanism
The high-resolution weather data collected from the ground level has been used for the implementation of 
Crop Insurance Scheme in the State, which is considered as a risk transfer mechanism. The weather data is 
used at different levels. First, it is used in designing the Term-sheets in case of Restructured Weather Based 
Crop Insurance Scheme (R-WBCIS) wherein area-specific and crop-specific term sheets are designed by 
agencies using high-resolution historical weather data. Similarly, the ground-level weather data is also being 
used by the public for claiming insurance for the damage loss of property incurred due to weather aberration. 
Incidences of damage to industrial sheds or the chimneys due to high wind activity are being established and 
assessed using the weather data collected from the TWS station network. Likewise, damages to the poly-
houses installed for floriculture and/or cash crop cultivation are also assessed using the weather data.
Water Resource Management
The information on the weather, based on the high-resolution data, and weather forecast is also being used 
for the efficient management of the water resources in the State. For instance by considering the available 
water storage in the Reservoirs, the current inflow based on the ongoing rainfall activity in the catchment 
and expected inflow based on the rainfall forecast, the water is allocated / utilized for drinking, industries and 
irrigation for the agriculture.

Information Dissemination Mechanism
Information Dissemination play an important role in disaster risk reduction. KSNDMC has deployed various 
dissemination systems to communicate disaster-related information through Alerts, Advisories and Early 
Warnings to all the Government Executives & Community at last mile in real-time. High Spatial and Temporal 
resolution data thus collected from the ground on various parameters are being converted into information. 
Subsequently, in conjunction with the weather forecast, the meteorological information is used to generate 
customized weather Advisories which are disseminated to the users. This has enabled the stakeholders at all 
levels to take appropriate decisions at the right time in the domain of Drought Monitoring & Management, 
Crop Assessment Survey Mechanism, and Water Resource Management. Implementing Insurance Schemes 
and Power generation and Grid load management.
24x7 Interactive Help Desk “VARUNA MITRA”

& advisories across the State farmers and to the wider community. Leveraging this existing mechanism at

7.6 WASTE MANAGEMENT IN KARNATAKA-REALITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES
7.6.1 Solid Waste Management in Karnataka
Karnataka is one of the major contributors to solid waste in India, primarily due to its urban centers like 
Bengaluru, Mysuru, and Hubli-Dharwad. Bengaluru, the state’s capital and IT hub, generates the most 
significant amount of solid waste, followed by other cities and towns.
According to reports, Bengaluru alone generates around 5,000 to 6,000 metric tons of solid waste per day. 
This number increases as the population grows and urban sprawl continues. Karnataka’s waste generation 
is largely a result of Residential waste, Commercial and industrial waste, Waste from street cleaning and 
Construction and demolition waste.
Karnataka has implemented several measures to handle the growing waste management challenge. These 
efforts includes door to door waste collection, segregation, processing, recycling and disposal mechanisms. 
The state government, along with municipal corporations, has developed waste management policies and 
has been actively pursuing solutions to improve the situation.
Bengaluru, which was once struggling with overflowing landfills, has now started the process of creating 
sanitary landfills that meet modern environmental standards.
