Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Project (SVEP)
Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Project (SVEP) aims to support rural poor come out of poverty by helping 
them set up enterprises and provide support till the enterprise stabilizes. It provides financial support through 
Community Enterprise Fund to the Entrepreneurs and links them to bank for MUDRA loan and other financial 
services. The total project cost for implementation of project in a taluk for duration of four years is Rs.6.50 
crore per block, supporting at least 10000 enterprises owned and managed by SHG women. 4408 SHG women 
entrepreneurs have been supported under the SVEP program.
AGEY (Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana)
AGEY aims to improve rural connectivity by linking remote villages with essential services such as markets, 
education and healthcare through SHG/CBO-managed transport services. The scheme supports livelihoods 
and local economic development by providing interest-free loans for vehicle purchase. During 2025–26, an 
amount of Rs.2.33 crore has been released for the procurement of 29 vehicles across 18 districts.

RSETIs are providing training to rural youths on self-employment in different trades. In Karnataka State, 32 
RSETIs are working in all 30 districts with well-established infrastructure and human resources. Training is

Akka Cafe
The Akka Cafe initiative, launched in 2024–25, empowers SHG women to run cafes serving nutritious local 
cuisine, generating livelihoods for 5–10 women per outlet. Two models are supported—Premium (Rs.15 lakh) 
and Classic (Rs.7 lakh) for renovation, branding, and equipment. Out of 62 targeted cafes, 25 are operational, 
11 have completed renovation and 26 are under renovation. For 2025–26, 137 proposals have been received, 
and administrative approval has been granted for Rs.6.29 crore to establish 43 cafes. Under capacity building, 
186 women entrepreneurs across 30 Enterprise Groups in 20 districts received training on operational 
efficiency, service quality and enterprise sustainability, supporting food-based livelihoods and local economic 
development.
National urban livelihood mission
Deen Dayal Anthyodaya Yojana -National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY- NULM)-2022-23
Swarna Jayanthi Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) was restructured and renamed as National Urban Livelihood 
Mission (NULM) which was approved by the GoI on 24th September 2013. GoI for implementation in 311 
Urban local bodies. This scheme is implemented with the support of Central and State Government and the

PM Street Vendor’s Atma Nirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) - A Special Micro Credit Facility for Street 
Vendors
The scheme is implemented from July 01, 2020. Under this scheme, benefited over 68 lakh street vendors 
across India. Recently, the Union Cabinet approved its restructuring and extension till March 2030 to increase 
its reach and impact. The restructured scheme will provide better financial access, promote digital use, build 
vendor skills and support the overall socio-economic growth of street vendors and their families.
The scheme aims to address the vulnerabilities of the street vendors through a multi-pronged approach 
which includes:
 Y Recognition of street vendors.
 Y Financial inclusion by providing loan in 3 tranches (1st – 15000, 2nd – 25000 and 3rd – 50000) with 7% 
interest subvention.
 Y Access to UPI linked credit card with a limit of Rs. 10000/- and will be increased to Rs. 30000/- valid for 
a period of 5 years.
 Y Enhancing digital transaction up to Rs.100 per month (Rs.1 per transaction) with maximum cashback of 
Rs.1,200 per year in each tranche and Wholesale digital purchases – up to Rs.100 per quarter (@ Rs.20 
per transaction for 5 such transactions) for 4 quarters for conducting digital transactions on wholesale 
purchases of at least Rs.2,000, with a maximum cashback of Rs.400 per year
 Y Capacity building for street vendors with focus on entrepreneurship, financial literacy, digital literacy, 
packaging etc in convergence with capacity building programs implemented by various Ministries/ 
Departments in GoI.
 Y Linkages to Social Security schemes by strengthening the safety net for beneficiaries’ families, enhancing 
their living conditions.
 Y This Scheme is fully 100% sponsored by the Central Government. The scheme will have the managed 
structure at the Central, State and ULBs level for the effective implementation and monitoring of the 
scheme. The PM SVANidhi scheme is implemented in all the Urban Local Bodies in the state of Karnataka.
Revised target of 8,42,200 has been allocated to Karnataka under PM SVANidhi Scheme 2.0.  As on January 
2026, out of 4,70,327 eligible applications, loan has been sanctioned for 4,17,679 beneficiaries amounting 
of Rs.425.35 crores and Rs.415.00 crores have been disbursed to 4,09,846  street vendors and Karnataka is 
currently placed 7th at the national level.

Challenges
Lack of Awareness: The basic challenges are that many programmes like Awareness, Training etc. are 
implemented in PPP mode involving Self-help groups and NGOs. A suitable mechanism for the monitoring of 
these NGOs and Self-help groups at District and Taluk level is to be established. 
Low Aspirational Value: Limited career pathways in vocational education. The skill development mission in 
the State needs support and cooperation from different stakeholders for capacity building of the youths to 
seek job opportunities in the global job markets and also promote self-employment for accomplishing the 
aspirations of youths and utilization of their talents and capacities.
Trainer Shortage and lack of technology usage: Insufficient high-quality trainers & industry exposure. The 
shortages of faculties in all wings also need urgent attention. Limited integration of emerging technologies 
(AI, IoT & Robotics) in the skill programs.
Gender Disparity: Uneven participation across districts & sectors. Low enrolment of women in manufacturing 
related skill development programs.
Industry co-ownership: Suboptimal Industry participation in curriculum co-creation, OJT and hiring.
Traditional Livelihood Gaps : Lack of formal integration & market linkages.
Funding Constraints: High-cost emerging tech courses not viable under current common cost norms. 
The cooperation of the Banks in providing the required loans to the identified, trained entrepreneurs at 
appropriate time has to be ensured to achieve the objective of the schemes. 
Curriculum lacking Life skills: Communication, building EQ, resilience at work. Etc., not embedded in skill 
training.
Building market credibility for NSQF certification: This issue is closely tied to the quality of assessments. Lack 
of qualified and certified assessors, lack of standardized assessments, lack of stringent monitoring leaves the 
system vulnerable to malpractice which weakens the market trust and acceptance.
Quality Training: High-quality training remains limited, especially in rural and remote areas.
Weak Linkage: Between education, skill development and employment policies, placements, tracking.
Way Forward
The roadmap ahead focuses on enhancing partnerships, expanding training programs and ensuring sustainable 
growth in the skill development sector for all citizens.
 Y Karnataka Skill Development Policy for holistic approach to cater to all the sectors and strategic 
collaborations with all departments and prominent industries.
 Y Chief Minister’s Kaushalya Karnataka Yojane 2.0 Guidelines to focus on Industry Linkage for aligning the 
Karnataka’s pool of talent towards the vision of having a Ready Workforce by 2030.
 Y Onboarding Catalyst agencies, Facilitators for strengthening & delivering right placements to the trained 
candidates. 
 Y Full integration of Kaushalkar LMS with Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH); use of AI for skill gap analytics and 
personalized learning.

PDF_PAGE 386
378
Skill, Entrepreneurship and Labour & Employment
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
 Y Operationalize Skill Advisory Committees at state and district levels; integrate skilling targets with 
departmental KPIs.
 Y Advocate for revised cost norms; leverage CSR funds and PPP models for infra augmentation; pilot 
outcome-based funding.
9.2 LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT
9.2.1 Introduction
The  Lowest Unemployment Rate 2.8% is recorded in Karnataka  after Gujarath in the country and also it is 
below the All India  average of 5.2 % as per Periodic Labour Force Survey PLFS) Quarterly Bullet in Report  July 
–September 2025  (age 15 years and above ) demonstrating superior employment generation and a highly 
efficient job market. Karnataka outperforms India across all labour indicators with Worker Population Ratio 
55.6% as against All India average of 52.2%, Labour Force Participation Rate of Karnataka is 57.3% and All India 
average of 55.1%, Karnataka’s labour market data reveals a state economy operating at high efficiency with 
strong job creation, widespread economic participation and minimal unemployment with efficient labour 
market: as per Periodic Labour Force Survey  Quarterly Bulletin Report  July –September 2025  (age 15 years 
and above).
The Karnataka Labour Department has introduced progressive legislation and rules were notified during 2025-
26 to expand social security coverage to previously unorganized workforce sectors, including the Karnataka 
Cinema and Cultural Activities Workers (Welfare) Cess Act, 2024 for entertainment industry workers, the 
Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 for app-based and gig economy 
workers, and the Karnataka Domestic Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Bill, 2025 currently in draft stage, 
collectively aimed at providing welfare benefits and social protection to vulnerable worker categories in the 
evolving labour market.
As a Progressive Labour Policy initiative in the state, a menstrual leave policy is being implemented from 
November 12, 2025, providing one day of paid leave per month to women employees (aged 18-52 years) in 
registered establishments.
9.2.2  Labour Department
Vision and Mission of Labour Department
Vision
“Making Karnataka as a model state for global investment and sustainable industrial production based on the 
twin principles of decent quality employment generation and inclusive all-round development of working 
class by designing and implementing feasible creative approaches and pragmatic operational strategies”.
Mission
“To evolve model frameworks in respect of Labour Legislation, Policies, Action Plans, Schemes and Programs 
by involving all the parties vitally concerned and implementing the same using advanced technologies so 
as to achieve efficiency and effectiveness in reaching the target group and thereby ensuring Karnataka’s 
competitiveness in the domestic and global market as a preferred destination for investment and decent 
quality employment generation”.

Implementation and Progress of Various Labour Acts in Karnataka
A major issue in the area of labour reforms is how to ensure minimum conditions of decent work and livelihood 
in the unorganized or informal sector of the economy. The limited applicability of important laws and the 
application of number filters have led to the emergency of a dual labour market with the resultant implication 
of the overwhelmingly larger sections of the unorganized sector labour being deprived of protection from 
laws in many spheres. Labour regulations can be broadly grouped into four broad areas, based on the aspects 
of employment covered by them, conditions of work, wages and remuneration, employment security and 
industrial relations and social security and welfare of workers. The remarkable achievements in the matter of 
enforcement of various Acts in terms of prosecution and imposition of fine.
 Y By Government Order No: LD 466 LET 2023, dated 12-11-2025, with the intention of enhancing health, 
efficiency, mental well  being and performance of women employees between 18 to 52 years of age, 
working in the establishments registered under Factories Act, 1948, Karnataka Shops and Commercial 
Establishments Act, 1961, Plantation Workers Act, 1951, Beedi and Cigar Workers Act, 1966 and Motor 
Transport Workers Act, 1961, it is ordered to provide one day of paid leave per month to all permanent/
contractual/outsourced women during their menstrual cycle, restricting to 12 days per year.
 Y A total of 57,155 inspections have been conducted under various labour laws and 6,966 cases have been 
filed against erring employers for violation of the Act. A total of 1,378 cases were disposed of in various 
courts and a sum of Rs. 77,78,300/- was levied in fine.
 Y Out of 567 cases received during the period from 01.04.2025 to 30.12.2025 under the Industrial Disputes 
Act, 1947 and 564 cases have been disposed of and 03 cases are pending. 
a. Strikes and Lockouts – The number of strikes and lockouts indicate the level of industrial peace in a 
State. Karnataka is by and large, a peaceful state as far as industrial environment is concerned. No strikes, 
lockouts, layoffs reported during the year.
b. Absenteeism – The absenteeism of workers in the industries for the year 2025-26 stood at 11.27% till the

9.2.2(1) Karnataka Labour Welfare Board
The Karnataka Labour Welfare Board came into existence in 1969 to promote the welfare of workers in the 
state of Karnataka. A fund has been established under the Karnataka Labour Welfare Act, 1965 to provide 
financial assistance to workers and carry out activities.To this fund, a contribution of Rs. 20/- per employee, 
Rs. 40/- per employee from the employer and Rs. 20/- per employee from the government, totaling Rs. 80/- 
per employee, is collected from factories, plantations, motor transport establishments, shops and commercial 
establishments registered with the Karnataka Labour Welfare Board, employing more than 50 workers.

employment to youth belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The benefits are as follows:
1. R eimbursement of employer-paid ESI and EPF contributions for two years, subject to a maximum of 
Rs.3,000 per month per candidate.
2. R eimbursement of apprenticeship stipend for candidates undergoing apprenticeship training for two 
years, up to Rs.5,000 per month.
3. R eimbursement of wages up to Rs.7,000 per month for two years if apprentices are permanently 
employed after training.
4. R eimbursement of wages up to Rs.6,000 per month for two years for candidates newly recruited into 
permanent positions.
Under these benefits, a total of Rs.4.80 crore has been reimbursed to employers, including partial wage 
reimbursement, in respect of 899 candidates.

Vision & Mission
To become a leading organization in providing value added services to protect the workers and work 
environment in factories from Industrial Occupational Hazards by disseminating knowledge & information to 
all the stake holders. To ensure greater awareness and participation of all the stake holders in achieving work 
safety, better health and work environment through capacity building measures and knowledge dissemination 
programmes. 
Department of Factories, Boilers, Industrial Safety and Health carries the responsibility of ensuring Occupational 
Safety, Health and Welfare of all the workers in the registered factories through effective enforcement of, 
 Y  The Factories Act, 1948 and the rules made thereunder.
 Y The Karnataka Factories Rules, 1969 and the rules made thereunder.
 Y The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the rules made thereunder.
 Y Maternity Benefit Act 1961 and the rules made thereunder.
 Y For Building and other Construction activities, The Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation 
of Employment and Condition of Services) Act-1996 and rules made there under.

9.2.2 (d) PeriodicLabour Force Survey (PLFS)
Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) of National Sample Survey (NSS) are the Primary source of Labour market 
data at National and State level in India. This is the Quarterly Bulletin Report based on the data collected in 
Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) during PLFS July-September 2025. 
Labour Force Participation Rate measures the proportion of working-age population (15 years and above) 
that is actively participating in the labour market, either by working or actively seeking work.

Karnataka’s Labour Market Strengths
1. Efficient Labour Market: High LFPR (57.3%) combined with high WPR (55.6%) and low UR (2.8%) indicates 
an efficient labour market that successfully matches workers with jobs
2. Rural Economy Excellence:
 ) Highest rural LFPR among males (79.9%).
 ) Highest rural WPR (58.8%).
 ) Very low rural unemployment (2.5%).
 ) Demonstrates thriving rural economy with diverse opportunities.
3. Urban Job Creation:
 ) Urban WPR exceeds national average by 4.2 percentage points.
 ) Urban unemployment half the national rate.
 ) Shows robust urban economic growth.
4. Gender Inclusion
 ) Female LFPR and WPR exceed national averages in both rural and urban areas.
 ) Female unemployment rates below national averages.
 ) Gender parity in rural unemployment.
5. Minimal Leakage: The gap between LFPR and WPR is minimal (1.7 percentage points), meaning most 
people who want to work find employment.
Conclusion
Karnataka’s labour market data reveals a state economy operating at high efficiency with strong job creation, 
widespread economic participation, and minimal unemployment. The state successfully outperforms national 
averages across all key metrics and all demographic segments (rural/urban, male/female), positioning it as 
one of India’s strongest and most inclusive labour markets.
9.2.3 Achievements
1. Efficient Labour Market: Karnataka outperforms India across all labour indicators with Worker Population 
Ratio 55.6% as against All India average of 52.2%, Labour Force Participation Rate of Karnataka is 57.3% 
and All India average of 55.1%, Karnataka’s labour market data reveals a state economy operating at high 
efficiency with strong job creation, widespread economic participation, and minimal unemployment as 
per Periodic Labour Force Survey  Quarterly Bulletin Report  July –September 2025  (15 years and above).
2.  The  Lowest Unemployment Rate 2.8% is recorded in Karnataka  afterGujarath in the country and also it 
is below the All India  average of 5.2 % as per PLFS Quarterly Bulletin Report  July –September 2025  (15 
years and above ) demonstrating superior employment generation and a highly efficient job market.
3.  High LFPR (57.3%) combined with high WPR (55.6%) and low UR (2.8%) indicates an efficient labour 
market that successfully matches workers with jobs.

36.5 lakhs of Insured Persons and about 141.62 lakhs of their family members through a network of ESI 
Hospitals.
6.  K arnataka Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare  Board has provided financial assistance 
to eligible registered beneficiaries under various welfare and social security schemes, during the year  
2025-26 (Up to December), 6,22,429 beneficiaries have availed benefits under various schemes 
amounting to Rs.797.60 crore. 
7.  39, 973 beneficiaries availed financial assistance of Rs.35.59 crore provided under the welfare schemes of 
The Karnataka Labour Welfare Board up to December 2025.
8. 7.39 crore persondays employment is provided under MGNREGA scheme as on  02.02.2026 during 
the year 2025-26 and 10.27 crore persondays wage employment generated provisional under state 
government major programmes as on December 2025. 
9.2.4  Challenges
1. Resource Constraints
 Y Child Labour Abolition Society requires additional funds beyond administrative expenses
 Y ESIS budget reduced from Rs. 51 crore to Rs. 10 crore, limiting planned improvements
 Y Need for sustained funding for welfare schemes
2. Rapid Industrialization
 Y Increasing use of hazardous chemicals and processes
 Y Need for continuous skill upgradation of inspection staff
 Y Growing informal sector requiring social security coverage
3. Coverage Gaps
 Y Large unorganized sector still outside social security net
 Y Limited awareness among workers about available schemes
 Y Geographical reach in remote areas
4. Infrastructure Deficiencies
 Y Need for more ESI hospitals and dispensaries in industrial clusters
 Y Modernization of existing facilities required
 Y Shortage of specialized medical equipment and personnel
5. Compliance and Enforcement
 Y Dual labour market due to limited law applicability
 Y Number filters excluding smaller establishments
 Y Need for technology-enabled monitoring systems

9.2.5 Way Forward
Strategic Initiatives
1. Universal Coverage and Inclusion
 Y Expand registration drives for unorganized workers through e-Shram portal
 Y Implement newly notified Acts for gig workers, domestic workers, and cinema workers
 Y Strengthen outreach through AI-based Karmika Seva Kendras
 Y Achieve “Child and Adolescent Labour Free Karnataka” status through intensive IEC campaigns
2. Technology Integration
 Y Leverage Artificial Intelligence for beneficiary registration and service delivery
 Y Enhance online platforms for transparent, time-bound services
 Y Implement digital monitoring systems for compliance tracking
 Y Use data analytics for risk-based factory inspections
3. Healthcare Infrastructure Enhancement
 Y Complete sanctioned hospital and dispensary projects on priority
 Y Upgrade existing facilities with modern equipment and technology
 Y Establish specialized units (ICU, dialysis, modular OT) across all major ESI hospitals
 Y Strengthen PPP models for sustainable healthcare delivery
4. Occupational Safety Focus
 Y Intensify risk-based inspections in Major Accident Hazard factories
 Y Conduct regular capacity building programs for inspectors
 Y Promote safety awareness among employers and workers
 Y Develop sector-specific safety protocols for hazardous industries
5. Worker Welfare Enhancement
 Y Increase budget allocation for welfare schemes to meet growing demand
 Y Streamline benefit delivery through single-window systems
 Y Expand educational and skill development assistance
 Y Strengthen maternity and healthcare benefits
6. Stakeholder Engagement
 Y Build partnerships with employers for voluntary compliance
 Y Engage trade unions in policy formulation
 Y Collaborate with civil society for awareness campaigns
 Y Create feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement

 Y Implement Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers Act, 2025
 Y Finalize Karnataka Domestic Workers Act, 2025

10.1 POWER SECTOR
Power generation in the public sector is managed by the Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL) whereas 
the Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL) deals with transmission of power and load 
despatch functions. As part of the restructuring of the power sector in the State, the erstwhile Karnataka 
Electricity Board (KEB) was restructured as KPTCL in 1999 by giving it a corporate status. As per the Electricity 
Act 2003, KPTCL, being the State’s transmission utility, is not empowered to trade in electricity. Therefore, the 
distribution companies directly procure power from power generators, both public and private and ESCOMs 
own distribution network, and use KPTCL’s transmission network to distribute electricity.
10.1.1 Power Generation
The total installed generation capacity both in the public sector and private sector including the State’s share 
in the Central Generation Station (CGS) up to December-2025 is 37072.95 MW. The installed capacity in the 
public sector is 13759.78 MW (including CGS allocation) and the private sector’s share is 23313.17 MW. In 
the private sector capacity, the percentage share of renewable energy sources of power generation capacity 
(excluding the Share of IPP Thermal & Mini Hydel) to overall installed capacity is 53.32%. The status of power 
sector in terms of both installed capacity and electricity generation for Karnataka is provided in Table 10.1.

Transmission & Distribution Losses: (T&D Losses)
The State has taken various measures to reduce T&D and AT&C losses. 
 Y Establishment of new Substations and Transmission Lines.
 Y Augmentation of Existing Sub Station & Replacement of age-old conductors.
 Y Bifurcation of lengthy   High Tension/Low Tension (HT / LT) lines& overloaded 11kVfeeders.
 Y Re-conductoringof HT/LT lines and reduction of HT/LT ratio.
 Y Providing additional transformers to release over loaded DTCs.
 Y 100% Metering and Accuracy in Billing.
 Y Load balancing and bifurcation of load.
 Y Strengthening of Vigilance/MT Activities.
 Y Replacing Electro Mechanical meters by Static/energy meter.
 Y Encouraging consumers to install energy efficient equipment’s.
Measures taken for reduction of AT&C Loss
 Y Accuracy and 100% billing of consumer installations.
 Y 100% collection efficiency.
 Y Improving vigilance activities.
 Y Periodical rating of HT & LT Installations.

10.1.4 Electricity, Demand and Supply Status
The State of Karnataka has achieved near self-sufficiency in power generation to meet the growing demand. 
The occasional gap due to seasonal variation in demand and supply is met through short term purchases. 
Trends in peak demand for power and peak energy supply per day during the years 2020-21 to 2025-26 
(Upto Dec-2025) are given in Figure 10.2. It may be observed that both the peak demand and peak energy 
supply per day are showing increasing trend. The peak demand met during 2024-25 was 18395MW and that 
in 2025-26 (Upto Dec-25) was 17336MW. The anticipated peak demand to be met during 2025-26 is around 
18986MW.
Figures 10.3 and 10.4 show the trends in estimated gaps in demand and supply for both power and energy.
There is no power supply shortage since last 7 years.

There are a total number of 35.67 lakhs Irrigation Pump sets upto 10 HP in the State as of December-2025. 
The power supply to IP sets (Upto 10 HP) has been made free with effect from 01.08.2008. The entire cost 
of supply of free power to agricultural sector (IP set upto 10 HP connected load) has been made good by the 
State Government through subsidy.

GruhaJyothi Subsidy
Out of the 5 guarantees announced by the Government, the most important guarantee “GruhaJyothi” scheme 
has been implemented by Energy Department from 01.07.2023. Under this scheme, every household in the 
State is provided free electricity supply every month subject to a maximum consumption limit of 200 units 
per month. Out of 1.75 Cr registered consumers, presently 1.66 Cr consumers are getting benefit in this 
scheme. The earlier schemes such as “Bhagyajyothi and “Kuteerajyothi” and “Amruthajyothi” schemes have 
been subsumed in this GruhaJyothi Scheme. The subsidy given under Gruha Jyothi scheme from 01.07.2023 
to 31.12.2025 is Rs. 22,040.00 Crore.

10.1.8 Demand Side Management (DSM)
Energy Efficiency and Energy Conservation endeavour is critical for meeting India’s Nationally Determined 
Contribution in the emission intensity of its GDP by 33% - 35% by 2030 from 2005 level. The Government of 
Karnataka has implemented several programmes to conserve energy as part of its DSM initiatives. Some of 
the important programmes are:
1. Tim e of Day Tariff Metering is mandatory for industrial consumers and especially for HT consumers having 
sanction load of 500 kVA and above.
2. Ins talling Energy efficient street lighting systems and Electronic Time Switches for street light installations 
for switching “ON” and “OFF”.
3. Adop tion of High Voltage Distribution System (HVDS) for agricultural loads in rural areas.
4. Enc ouraging domestic consumers to use solar water heaters.
5. Manda tory use of solar water heating systems for all residential buildings with built-up area of 600 
Sq. feet and above constructed on sites measuring 1200 Sq. feet and above falling within the limits of 
Municipalities / Corporations and Bangalore Development Authority sectors.
6. Manda tory use of LED bulb/tube lights in Government buildings/Aided institutions/ Boards /Corporations.

PDF_PAGE 422
414
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
7. Manda tory use of star rated energy efficient irrigation pump sets conforming to standards prescribed by 
the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE).
8. Pr omotion of energy efficient building designs.
9. Implemen tation of PM-Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana.
10. Implemen tation of Off grid solar pumps under KUSUM-B and feeder level solarization under KUSUM-C.
11. Vid hyuthJagruthiYojana, an awareness programme on DSM activities for students.
12. Deplo yment of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations to promote Electric Vehicles.

10.1.11: Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Limited (KREDL)
KREDL is the nodal agency for the development of renewable energy sources in Karnataka. To harness green 
and clean renewable energy sources in the State for environmental benefits and energy security and to initiate 
energy conservation & efficiency measures in all the sectors for sustainable development, the Government 
of Karnataka notified a policy on renewable energy (for the period 2009-14) in 2010, Solar Policy 2014-21 in 
2014 & Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-27 in 2022.
Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-27
State notified Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-27 to facilitate Government of India in meeting the 
Renewable Energy target of 500 GW by 2030 and to promote new initiatives and emerging energy technologies 
in the State and to continue Karnataka State’s position as a preferred investment destination in the Renewable 
Energy sector and create an ecosystem for sustainable and green energy development in the State. 
KREDL, the nodal agency envisages private sector investment for renewable energy development in the State. 
The capacity addition under renewable energy during 2024-25 was 1209.19 MW and it is 1762.64 MW during 
2025-26 (upto Dec–25) (as shown in Table 10.14).

10.1.13 Centrally Sponsored Scheme
1. Atal Bhujal Yojana
Atal Bhujal Yojana is a program of GoI to improve the management of groundwater resources in the water 
stressed areas of the State. The Scheme has been launched in Dec 2019.

PDF_PAGE 425
417
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Dept of Minor Irrigation and Ground Water Development (MI & GWD), GoK is implementing the scheme in 
1,199 water stressed Gram Panchayats of the State with a budget of Rs.1,201 Cr. Funding of Rs.10.50 Cr. is 
sanctioned to Energy Department for Segregation of 17 feeders by creating 10 new feeders in BESCOM. All 
the 10 number of feeders are completed by the end of May 2025. Grant amount of Rs.5.70 Crs has been 
released till Dec 2025.
2. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)
GoI has launched the PM-JANMAN scheme in Nov-2023. The scheme aims to provide basic infrastructure for 
the comprehensive development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG). 
DPR for an amount of Rs.4.6 Cr. has been sanctioned to electrify 1,794 PVTG households in 5 districts (Dakshina 
Kannada, Udupi, Mysore, Chamarajanagar & Kodagu) in the state.
All 1,725 feasible households are completed by the end of Mar 2025. Remaining households could not be 
taken up due to migration, court case, kutcha houses. Grant amount of Rs.1.74 Crs. has been released till Dec 
2025
3. Dharti Aaba – Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA)
Ministry of Tribal affairs (MoTA), GoI is implementing the scheme.The scheme aims at improving the socio-
economic conditions of tribal communities by providing basic facilities to 1,089 tribal majority villages in the 
State. The scheme was launched by GoIin Oct 2024. The scheme period is from 2024-25 to 2028-29.
Energy Department facilitates electrification of Tribal HHs. DPR for an amount of Rs. 40.41 Crs has been 
sanctioned for electrification of 5,288 HHs in 186 habitations in BESCOM, CESC and GESCOM jurisdiction in 
6 districts (Chitradurga, Tumkur, Mysore, Chamarajanagar, Kodagu and Raichur). 1052 no of HHs have been 
electrified as on Dec 2025 and the remaining households are in progress. Grant amount of Rs.4.23 Crs has 
been released till Dec 2025.

10.1.16 Achievements of Energy Sector during 2025-26
 Y Considering the demand for electricity during the summer season, and to meet long term energy needs 
of the State, the following measures have been taken to ensure adequate supply of electricity to all 
categories of consumers.
 ) The State recorded highest peak demand of 18395 MW on March 7, 2025 and the highest daily 
energy consumption of 356.88 MU on March 19, 2025. PCKL has procured 3417 MUs in FY2024-25 
through exchanges to meet the increased demand in the State of Karnataka.  
 ) The state experienced a power surplus due to a good monsoon, and the surplus quantum of 3785 
MU was traded on Energy Exchanges during the monsoon months, i.e. June 2024 to October 2024.

10.1.17 Way Forward
Different strategies are framed in various Policies-Karnataka State Renewable Energy Policy, Energy Efficiency 
and Energy Conservation Policy for Affordable and Clean Energy for all.
 Y Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited (KPTCL) is identified as the nodal agency to plan and 
monitor the SDG-7. There is need to prepare periodic plans for all ESCOMs, to implementtheir distribution 
infrastructure in a coordinated manner, as grid modernization and up-rating of the distribution network 
for the absorption of power will involve significant capital infusion.
 Y There is a need to rectify the balance sheet of state power utilities by rate-design reforms, plugging 
revenue leakage, squaring cumulative losses, and issuance of bonds. Additionally, quality-rated 
distribution transformers are required to reduce the length to ensure optimum efficiency.
 Y There is need to promote Utility business model to transform from generation sales to mediator for sales 
for sustenance in the long-term. This would keep the consumers connected to the distribution networks 
to transact their surplus energy.
 Y Timely formulation and implementation of action plans.
 Y Re-assessment of cross-subsidies by cost-effective tariffs and regulatory innovations for electricity to 
evolve from a public utility model to a product/commodity model.
 Y Need for application of IT solutions such as SCADA to augment collection and collation of data and reduce 
manual interventions to ensure maximum uninterrupted power supply.
 Y Change management programmes of local power distribution as well as reactivation of the franchisee 
system to be promoted by involving local youths under Skill India Mission.
 Y There is need to regulate farm power by limiting the number of wells per unit area and checking misuse of 
subsidy. Also, going forward, there is need for increasing testing labs for solar panels as well as innovation 
labs such as YESSCALE (aggro tech, clean tech and smart cities) as alternate source of energy.
 Y Companies need to promote initiatives like internet of things block chain, machine learning, mobile 
intelligence, mini-grids and micro grids in future.

PDF_PAGE 428
420
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
 Y To ensure sustainable up take of these technological innovations, there is a need for coherence between 
institutions and technological processes to ensure satisfactory functioning of electricity infrastructure.
 Y Network strengthening and using efficient irrigation pump sets. Convergence of State’s Ganga Kalyana 
scheme with the Central Government’s KUSUM scheme in feasible areas, which will help in promoting 
solar energy and reduce subsidy burden.

Planning and Roads Asset Management Centre (PRAMC)
Planning and Roads Asset Management Centre has been established to strengthen the plans, schemes and 
other prescribed functions of the department. It functions as the apex institutional body under government 
supervision for policy formulation, planning, and management of road assets. The main objectives of the 
centre are as follows.  
 Y To function as a nodal agency for preparing plans, budgets, and programmes for roads in Karnataka 
within the Public Works Department.
 Y To improve planning and decision-making processes in the Department.
 Y To effectively and efficiently use information technology and to implement IT systems across the 
Department.
 Y To enhance human resource capacity through training programmes and skill development of departmental 
officers and staff.
 Y To implement a Pavement Management System and a Bridge Management System.
 Y To continuously manage and update the Road Information System (RIS)and Progress Monitoring System 
and other asset management systems.
 Y To carry out any additional responsibilities assigned from time to time.
With assistance from the Asian Development Bank, a consultancy team was appointed and is actively working. 
Required equipment and software have been procured and handed over to the consultants. Details of the 
procured equipment are provided below.
a)  R oad Condition Data Collection Vehicle (RCDCV): These laser-based devices collect data such as 
International Roughness Index (IRI), rutting, ravelling, potholes, and other parameters required for 
planning.
b) Falling Weight Deflectometer (FWD): This is a non-destructive testing device used to evaluate pavement 
structural strength without causing damage. It works by applying a load on the pavement surface and 
measuring surface deflections, from which pavement performance is assessed.
c) Ground Penetration Radar (GPR): The Ground Penetration Radar (GPR) uses radar pulses to detect 
subsurface features and physical properties without excavation. It is a fast, non-destructive, and highly 
effective tool for assessing pavement layer thickness and composition.
Data collected using these devices is analysed through specialized software and used to prepare the Annual 
Works Programme. As per Government Order prioritization of road widening, strengthening, and improvement 
works must be done using the KRAMS software developed by PRAMC.
In 2017-18, the State Government created a separate budget head for road safety works. The Supreme Court 
Committee on Road Safety has issued several guidelines, which the State has incorporated into its road safety 
policy and protocols.

Challenges
The total number of vehicles in the state was 3.35 crore in March-2025 and increased to 3.37 crore in 
August-2025. The process of widening lanes on the roads should be carried out in a balanced manner in line 
with the increase in vehicle density on roads.
Way Forward
 Y For the all-round development of the state’s roads, national highways will be constructed in innovative 
models with high durability, 4-lane/6-lane and state highways will be converted into two-lane and district 
major roads as medium-lane roads.
 Y Road safety works will be carried out on priority where necessary for the safety of road users.
 Y Identify the places where bridges are required and provide all-season connectivity to residential areas by 
constructing bridges.
 Y Construction of footbridges will be undertaken to connect the people of coastal, Malnad and Ghat areas.

 Y Vehicle Location Tracking Device & Emergency Button Installation Scheme in Public Service Vehicles: 
The central government’s notification and guidelines, the installation of Vehicle Location Tracking Devices 
and Emergency Buttons in public service vehicles such as minibuses, school buses, private service vehicles, 
maxi cabs, contract vehicles, motor cabs, and goods transport vehicles operating on national highways 
has been implemented under the Nirbhaya Scheme for the safety of women and children. The scheme 
was launched on 19th June 2024. In the state, there are a total of 6,04,863 public service vehicles, of 
which, by 31.12.2025,  2,10,006 vehicles have been equipped with Vehicle Location Tracking Devices and 
Emergency Panic Buttons.

(HSRP) has been made mandatory for all old vehicles registered before 1st April 2019 in the state of 
Karnataka and the said scheme has been implemented on 18.08.2023. From 18-08-2023 to 31.12.2025, 
a total of 59,65,027 vehicles registered in the state. 
 Y Retro Reflective Tape : Retro Reflective Tape & rear marking plates help drivers of other vehicles to 
quickly identify the movement of vehicles when vehicles are moving at night, even if the tail lamps and 
indicators of the vehicles are not in good condition, thus controlling possible accidents. Accordingly, 
in the state, the installation of Retro Reflective Tape & rear marking plates for transport vehicles has 
been made mandatory from 05.04.2024, in the interest of road safety and the public and motor vehicle 
owners/driverless.
 Y  Aut omated Driving Test Tracks :  In order to scientifically test the driving skills of applicants for driving 
licenses without human intervention, it is intended to construct automated driving test tracks within 
the jurisdiction of all Assistant/Regional Transport Offices in the state. Currently, automated tracks are 
operating in Jnana Bharathi, Electronic City, Mysuru, Kalaburagi, Shivamogga, Dharwad, Hassan and 
Mangalore. Raichur and Belagavi works are under progress.In the year 2024-25, approval has been given 
for the construction of    automatic test track in Puttur, Madikeri, Hunsur and Madhugiri. The construction 
work of Nelamangala and Chikkaballapur Automatic Test Track is in progress.In the year 2025-26, approval 
has been given for the construction of automatic test track in chitradurga, chamarajnagar  and Honnavara 
at Tender stage.

Achievement / Impact of the Project / Intervention
I. A survey on the Shakti scheme conducted by the “M2M Media Network LLP” in September-2023 and 
November-2023 revealed the following findings.
 Y Women have responded positively to the Shakti scheme. Women’s participation in the Shakti scheme has 
increased from 57% in September-23 to 64% in November-23.
 Y Women’s daily transport usage increased from 20% in September-23 to 27% in November-23.
 Y Shakti Scheme has encouraged 50 percent of women to enter employment. 
 Y The overall Shakti Scheme is perceived as a positive catalyst for women empowerment and economic 
contribution.
II. A study on “Fiscal Effects of Shakhti Scheme in the Government of Karnataka” conducted by the Fiscal 
Policy Institute revealed the following findings.
 Y Comparison of labour force participation and worker population ratio before and after the implementation 
of the Scheme shows that despite a decrease in the overall LFPR (Labour Force Participation Rate) and 
WPR (Worker Population Ratio), the female labour force participation rate and female worker population 
ratio have increased.
 Y LFPR and WPR increased by 5% year-on-year. Details given in Table 10.22.
 Y This indicates an increase in women’s interest in participation of economic activity and their share in the 
job market.

III.  The Sustainable Mobility Network and Nikore Associates, a New Delhi-based economic research and 
policy advisory think-tank, has conducted a study in 10 cities of which Delhi and Karnataka State have free 
travel plans, whereas West Bengal and Kerala State do not have it and Maharashtra State has a 50% discount 
on travel fares. This is the first analytical report prepared after conducting the survey in several states on free 
public transport scheme. The organizations released the report on 25.07.2025. The outcomes of the study 
are as mentioned below.
 Y The Shakti Scheme has created more employment opportunities for women across the state, contributing 
economic empowerment.
 Y Due to the Shakti Scheme, the employment rate of women has increased by 23% in Bengaluru and 21% 
in Hubballi-Dharwad.
 Y While other states have implemented several schemes like free travel on government transport and 50% 
discount on travel fares, similar to the State’s Shakti Scheme, Karnataka’s performance has surpassed 
other states.
 Y Women are able to save between 30% and 50% every month due to the free bus service.
 Y Shakthi Scheme has empowered women by providing them with better job opportunities, better wages, 
and better market facilities to become entrepreneurs.

I. Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation
KSRTC with its head office in Bengaluru provides bus service primarily to moffusil areas of southern Karnataka 
while BMTC, also headquarter in Bengaluru provides transportation to the capital city. The NWKRTC with 
headquarters in Hubballi provides transportation to the North Western Districts of Karnataka while KKRTC 
with headquarters in Kalburgi provides transportation to the North Eastern Districts of Karnataka.
Physical performance: KSRTC has in its jurisdiction seventeen southern districts of Karnataka and provides bus 
service to 20090 villages out of 21748 villages, the percentage service provided being 92.4%. 8261 schedules 
were operated as on 31.12.2025, by utilizing 8766 vehicles, for the cumulative period the operation was 
average of 29.95 lakh kms/day earning gross revenue of Rs.1435.57 lakh and carrying 34.81 lakh commuters 
on an average daily with workforce of 34236 employees. The Physical statistics of KSRTC, BMTC, NWKRTC and 
KKRTC for the year 2024-25 (upto December-2024) and 2025-26 (upto December-2025) is furnished in the 
Appendix 10.1.
Thus KSRTC operated 8237.09 lakh effective kms. during the year 2025-26 (upto December-2025) as against 
7887.38 lakh effective kms operated during the same period of previous year. The percentage fleet utilization 
has increased to 91.5 during the current year as against 89.5 in previous year. During the current year period 
KSRTC has inducted 10 new buses to its fleet and replaced 163 old vehicles which were not fit for operation. 
Financial Performance: During the year 2024-25, the Corporation incurred a loss of Rs.81.83 crore as against 
a loss of Rs.295.43 crore during 2023-24. During the year 2025-26 (upto December 2025), the Corporation 
incurred a loss of Rs.231.94 crore as against a loss of Rs.222.44 crore incurred during 2024-25(upto December 
2024). The financial statistics of KSRTC, BMTC, NWRTC and KKRTC for the year 2024-25 (upto December-2024) 
and 2025-26 (upto December-2025) is furnished in the Appendix 10.2.
During the year 2024-25, the Corporation by utilizing its internal resources and grants released by the 
Government under KGIDF, has taken up 81 works at an estimated cost of Rs.27440.06 lakhs of which an 
amount of Rs.11559.17 lakhs was spent for 69 civil works including the works under progress during the year. 
The details of the works are as mentioned below. 
 Y One work taken up under TSP Scheme is in progress, for which an amount of  Rs.221.45 lakhs has been 
incurred during the year 2024-25.
 Y Under KGIDF Scheme, Out of 31 works, 13 works for the development of infrastructure have been 
completed and 18 works are in progress. Under the said scheme, a total expenditure of Rs. 1801.66 lakhs 
has been incurred in the year 2024-25.
 Y During 2025-26, The Corporation by utilizing its internal resources and grants released by DULT has taken 
up 78 works at an approximate cost of Rs. 7204 lakhs of which 72 are under progress. The expenditure 
incurred upto Dec-2025 is Rs.1899.16 lakhs. 
Social Obligations
1. The financial compensation given to the dependents of the passengers who die in accidents of KSRTC 
buses has been increased from Rs.3 lakh to Rs.10 lakh.
2. All the four Corporations(KSRTC, BMTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC) have been fulfilling it`s social obligation by 
providing free/concession passes to several sections of the society namely, students, physically challenged, 
blind, freedom fighters, senior citizens, Olympians, para olympians, Arjuna awardees, National Shourya 
prashasti awardees, Ex- MLAs & Ex-MLCs within state and inter-state in any bus along with a companion, 
sitting MLAs & MLCs within state and inter-state in any bus with gold pass  etc.

Android based Smart Electronic Ticketing Machine (ETM): KSRTC deployed Android-based Smart Electronic 
Ticketing Machines (ETMs) across all KSRTC depots to modernize on-board ticketing operations, enhance 
transparency, and promote digital payments. 
UPI-Based (Dynamic QR) Digital Payment in KSRTC ETMs: KSRTC implemented a Dynamic QR-based UPI digital 
payment system across all Smart Electronic Ticketing Machines (ETMs) with effect from 11.11.2024, enabling 
passengers to make seamless cashless payments using any UPI application. This initiative strengthened digital 
transactions, improved transparency, reduced cash handling and enhanced passenger convenience across 
KSRTC services.
Achievements 
 Y For the first time in the history of the country’s road transport corporations, an accident insurance 
scheme of Rs. 1.00 crore has been implemented for on-duty and off-duty accidents.
 Y Compensation amount of Rs. 20.00 lakhs is given to the dependents of the deceased in the event of 
untimely death of the employee. 
 Y KSRTC has launched a cashless medical treatment scheme called “KSRTC-Arogya” for all it’s employees 
and their dependents.
Way Forward 
 Y KSRTC has planned to induct 1500 buses during the year 2026-27.
 Y KSRTC is in the process of implementing VTMS (Vehicle Tracking and Monitoring System) with AIS-140 
compliant tracking system and panic buttons in all the buses under the scheme “Central assistance for 
strengthening Public Transport”.  
 Y To enhance safety, security, and operational transparency in KSRTC bus operations, initiated the Bus 
Surveillance Camera Project, proposing the installation of surveillance cameras in 1,000 KSRTC buses. 
The system design includes two cameras per bus, comprising a saloon camera to monitor passenger 
activities and ensure in-bus security, and a dashboard-facing (dash) camera to capture road conditions 
and driving events.
II. Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation
The Corporation is providing quality, safe, reliable, clean and affordable travel facility to the commuters 
through its various initiatives and adoption of new technology and induction of new type of buses as per 
the increasing number of passengers. The Corporation is providing services by scientific fare system. The 
operational jurisdiction of BMTC went beyond B.B.M.P limits by 25 kms of Bengaluru, thus providing services 
to commuters in and around sub-urban of Bengaluru city.  
As on 31.12.2025, the Corporation has operated 6291 Schedules by utilizing 6984 vehicles, it has operated  
average schedules of 5860.4 and covers daily 12.07 lakhs kms. and earns average revenue of Rs. 731.36 
lakh Traffic revenue  by carrying 42.98 lakh passengers daily. The workforce of the Corporation is 29280.  In 
the year 2025-26 (Upto Dec-2025), the corporation has inducted 322 Electric vehicles (private) which are 
operating on GCC model scrapped 127 old vehicles. 
Financial Performance: During the year 2025-26 (upto December-25) the Corporation has operated 33.19 
crore effective kms, earned gross revenue of Rs. 2396.60 crores (including Rs. 206.52 crores financial assistance 
from government) and incurred an expenditure of Rs. 2697.12 crore and sustained a loss of Rs. 300.52 crore.

I. Airport Projects
Karnataka State Industrial & Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (KSIIDC)
KSIIDC continued its proactive role in the promotion of infrastructure projects on Public Private Partnership 
basis, as a nodal agency for Bengaluru International Airport Project.  Considering the initiatives taken up by 
KSIIDC in the infrastructure sector, its name was changed to “Karnataka State Industrial and Infrastructure 
Development Corporation Limited” with effect from November 22, 2010. Major developmental activities 
undertaken by the corporation during the year are as follows:
a. Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru
Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (KIAB), the 3rd busiest airport in the country in terms of the 
passenger traffic, handled 41.88 million passengers during 2024-25. Domestic passenger traffic saw a 10% 
growth, reaching 36.05 million, while international passenger numbers surged by 25%, exceeding 5.83 million 
during 2024-25. The airport also processed over 5,00,000 metric tons of cargo during FY 2024-25 compared 
to 4,39,495 metric tons in FY 2023-24, representing a growth of over 14%. During 2025, KIAB received the 
prestigious 5-Star Airport Terminal Rating from Skytrax, a UK-based organization evaluating airports based on 
quality and passenger experience. This makes Terminal 2 the first and only airport terminal in India to achieve 
this recognition. It was also named the best regional airport in India and South Asia.
As per the stand alone audited financial figures, Kempegowda International Airport Limited  earned total 
revenue of Rs. 3732 Cr and achieved a profit after tax of Rs. 510 Cr for FY 2024-25 mainly due to the increase 
in passenger and expansion of operations at Terminal 2. This Increase in passenger growth has translated into 
higher revenues across all non-aero revenues reflecting a higher spend per passenger. 
b. Aviation Development including development of Airports & Heliports: KSIIDC is the  Nodal Agency for the 
development of airports, airstrips, heliports, and water aerodromes across the State. It has undertaken the 
following aviation projects.
 Y  KSIIDC facilitated the completion and commissioning of the Kalaburagi Airport. The Airport Authority of 
India (AAI) has since taken over the operation and maintenance of the airport.

To create an accessible, efficient, and integrated railway system that enhances connectivity, promotes 
balanced economic growth, strengthens freight and logistics efficiency, and enables seamless multimodal 
integration—positioning railways as the backbone of sustainable mobility and development in the State. An 
amount of Rs.600 crores has been allotted for these projects during 2025-26, of which Rs.463.47 crores has

Bengaluru Suburban Railway Project: Bengaluru Suburban Railway Project is being implemented through the 
joint collaboration of Government of Karnataka and the Ministry of Railways at an estimated cost of Rs.15767 
crore. It is intended to build a 148 km long railway network with 57 railway stations. BSRP aims to connect 
Bengaluru city to its suburbs and satellite townships and will carry about 9.84 lakhs passengers per day upon 
completion. Thus, decongesting the road traffic of Bengaluru city. BSRP is the first project in India which is 
being implemented under National Suburban Rail Policy, 2018. Project was sanctioned by the Govt of India 
through Ministry of Railways on 21st Oct 2020. Details are given in Table 10.23.

Way forward
 Y Infrastructure Expansion & Modernisation - Enhance network capacity and connectivity by commissioning 
new rail lines, undertaking gauge conversions, doubling and electrifying high-density routes—including 
the Ramanagaram–Mysuru section—and introducing new passenger services, including high-speed and 
semi-high-speed trains, to meet future passenger and freight demand efficiently and sustainably.
 Y Inter-State & Port Connectivity - Strengthen rail links to ports and neighbouring states to support industrial 
growth, exports, tourism, and regional economic integration.
 Y High-Speed Corridor Planning - Identify priority high-speed and semi-high-speed corridors and undertake 
feasibility studies and Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for phased implementation.
 Y Freight & Logistics Growth - Build on record freight loading by strengthening freight corridors, developing 
logistics parks and private freight terminals, and increasing capacity for cargo wagon utilisation, including 
alongside passenger train operations.
 Y Bengaluru Suburban Rail Project (BSRP) - Accelerate implementation of the Bengaluru Suburban Rail 
Project through close coordination among stakeholders to significantly improve urban and peri-urban 
mobility.
 Y Multimodal Integration under PM Gati Shakti - Integrate railway infrastructure with highways, ports, 
airports, and logistics hubs to enable seamless multimodal connectivity and efficient movement of 
people and goods.
 Y Station Redevelopment & Urban Integration - Modernise stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme 
and promote station-centric development to enhance passenger amenities, accessibility, and urban 
integration.
 Y Last-Mile & Rural Connectivity - Improve last-mile rail connectivity to rural, semi-urban, agricultural, and 
industrial areas through sidings, feeder routes, and improved station access.
 Y Safety & Operational Modernisation - Enhance safety through elimination of level crossings, construction 
of ROBs/RUBs, deployment of modern signalling and train protection systems, and fencing in high-density 
sections.
 Y Green & Sustainable Railways - Promote energy efficiency and sustainability through electrification, 
renewable energy adoption, water conservation, and waste management initiatives.
III. Ports and Inland Water Transport
The State of Karnataka possesses an extensive coastline of approximately 320 km, which plays a pivotal role 
in maritime trade and commercial activities. The State’s maritime infrastructure currently comprises one 
Major Port and 13 Minor Ports. New Mangalore Port is the sole Major Port in the State and functions under 
the direct administrative jurisdiction of the Ministry of Shipping, Government of India. A total of 13 Minor 
Ports are operational under the administrative control of the State Government. Among the 13 Minor Ports, 
international trade operations (Import and Export cargo handling) are currently restricted to the Karwar and 

PDF_PAGE 454
446
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
Old Mangalore ports. The remaining Minor Ports are predominantly utilized for fishing-related activities and 
local maritime requirements. 
1. Financial performance and Revenue
The Department of Ports and Inland Water Transport has achieved significant revenue generation through 
maritime operations and land lease rentals. The performance highlights are as follows:
 Y Fiscal Year 2024-25:  During this financial year, a total of 6.07 lakh Metric Tonnes (MT) of cargo was 
handled across the State’s Minor Ports. The department remitted a total revenue of Rs.23.80 Crore to 
the government exchequer, accrued from maritime activities, land leases, and inland water transport 
services.
 Y Fiscal Year 2025-26: For the period spanning April 2025 to December 2025, the total cargo handled stood 
at 4.54 lakh Metric Tonnes. The department remitted a  total revenue of Rs.11.35 Crore to the government 
exchequer, accrued from maritime activities, land leases, and inland water transport services.
2. Developmental  works and utilization of grants
The Government has been consistently allocating funds to enhance port infrastructure across the State. The 
details of the grants provided and their utilization are as follows:
 Y Development during 2024-25: In the fiscal year 2024-25, a total grant of Rs.57.50 Crore was earmarked 
for the infrastructure development of Minor Ports. Out of this allocation, various developmental projects 
amounting to Rs.20.44 Crore were successfully implemented.
 Y Progress during 2025-26 : For the current financial year, a substantial outlay of Rs.74.36 Crore has been 
provided to further development works. As at the end of December 2025, an expenditure of Rs.10.93 
Crore has been incurred towards various projects currently in different stages of execution.
3. Port Development And Karnataka Maritime Development Policy – 2024
To incentivize large-scale investments in the maritime sector and facilitate the creation of advanced 
infrastructure, the Government promulgated the ‘Karnataka Maritime Development Policy – 2024’ on January 
4, 2025.
Vision
 Y To transform the State of Karnataka into India’s most technologically advanced, sustainable, and 
competitive Maritime Hub.
 Y To fortify the Blue Economy through the establishment of world-class infrastructure, thereby driving 
comprehensive economic growth across the coastal region.
Mission
 Y Private Sector Participation: To attract capital investments exceeding Rs.4,000 Crore in the maritime 
sector through the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
 Y Modernization of Ports: To develop the State’s Minor Ports into Greenfield Ports and significantly augment 
existing cargo-handling capacities.
 Y Eco-friendly Transportation: To alleviate pressure on road networks by expanding Water Metro services 
and reinforcing the inland water transport framework.

447
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
 Y Tourism Infrastructure: To achieve global recognition for coastal tourism by constructing international-
standard Cruise Terminals and Floating Jetties.
4. Shoreline Management Plan (Smp)
To facilitate coastal protection and ensure sustainable development, the State Government is implementing 
the Shoreline Management Plan (SMP) based on scientific parameters. The procurement of Coastal Regulation 
Zone (CRZ) clearance is mandatory for any developmental activities within the coastal tracts. Pursuant to the 
order passed by the Hon’ble National Green Tribunal (NGT), Chennai Bench, the preparation of a Shoreline 
Management Plan is an essential prerequisite for granting CRZ clearances. 
Plan Formulation: The Government of Karnataka, in coordination with the Karnataka State Coastal Zone 
Management Authority (KSCZMA), entrusted the task of drafting the SMP to the National Centre for Sustainable 
Coastal Management (NCSCM), Chennai. The NCSCM has since submitted the SMP report to KSCZMA, and 
Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) are currently being formulated in accordance with the guidelines stipulated 
in this report. 
District-wise DPR Preparation and Allocation of Grants: In 2024, administrative approval was accorded for 
Rs.300.00 Lakh towards consultancy services for the preparation of DPRs for anti-sea erosion and coastal 
protection works across the following 3 districts. Namely, Dakshina Kannada: Rs.100 Lakh,  Udupi: Rs.80 Lakh 
and Uttara Kannada: Rs.120 Lakh.
Current Progress
 Y Udupi and Dakshina Kannada: Consultants have been officially on boarded for these districts. Data 
acquisition and preliminary technical studies are currently in progress. The finalized DPRs will be 
submitted to the competent authority shortly.
 Y Uttara Kannada: The initial tender process for the appointment of consultants did not elicit any bids. 
Consequently, a re-tendering process has been initiated to secure consultancy services.
5. Development of Karwar Port 
As the State’s premier commercial Minor Port, Karwar Port is undergoing significant modernization and 
capacity augmentation. To ensure the safe navigation of large vessels and facilitate efficient cargo handling, 
dredging operations have been initiated to maintain a depth of 8.00 meters in the port’s Turning Circle, Basin, 
and Channels. A total budgetary outlay of Rs.40 Crore has been allocated for this project. Under the Centrally 
Sponsored Sagarmala Scheme, specialized infrastructure is being developed for the safe handling of ‘Class-B’ 
petroleum products at Karwar Port.
In compliance with the Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD)–156 guidelines, the installation of advanced 
fire-fighting equipment has been physically completed at an estimated cost of Rs.19.00 Crore. The project 
has secured the mandatory ‘No Objection Certificate’ (NOC) from the Petroleum and Explosives Safety 
Organization (PESO) on November 25, 2025. An expenditure of Rs.14.40 Crore has been incurred to date, 
demonstrating steady financial progress in line with project milestones.
To safeguard the maritime environment from potential oil spills and pollution, a project for the Operation 
and Maintenance (O&M) of existing oil pollution control equipment has been commissioned. This initiative, 
valued at Rs.6.50 Crore, covers a service period of three years.

PDF_PAGE 456
448
Economic Infrastructure
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
6. Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Projects
To optimize the economic potential of the State’s coastline and attract substantial capital investments, several 
landmark projects have been initiated under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework.
a. Keni Port Development: This project involves the development of a state-of-the-art Greenfield Port at 
Ankola in the Uttara Kannada district. The port is being developed at a total cost of Rs.4,118.00 Crore 
with a projected cargo-handling capacity of 30 MTPA (Million Tonnes Per Annum). Preliminary studies 
are currently in progress. A Public Hearing was successfully conducted on August 22, 2025, and the final 
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is currently awaited.
b.  Pavinakurve Port Development: A Greenfield port with a capacity of 14 MTPA was originally envisioned 
at Pavinakurve with an estimated investment of Rs.3,047.00 Crore under the PPP model. Despite inviting 
tenders on three occasions, the process did not elicit any bids. Consequently, the project is now being 
transitioned to the New Mangalore Port Authority (NMPA) to be developed as an independent port.
c. Manki Port Development: A Feasibility Report for the comprehensive development of Manki Port has 
been prepared by IIT Madras. To enhance operational efficiency, a dedicated rail link is essential; in this 
regard, the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) is currently preparing a Detailed Project Report 
(DPR) for rail connectivity.
d. Jalmetro (Water Metro) Services: To modernize the urban transportation network of Mangaluru and 
leverage its riverine routes, Jalmetro services are proposed for the Gurupura and Netravati rivers. A 
Transaction Advisor has been appointed for the project, and the draft report submitted by them is 
currently under review.
e. Management of Port Berths – ROMT Model: The Government has accorded approval to manage berths 
at selected ports under the PPP model on a Rehabilitation, Operation, Maintenance, and Transfer (ROMT) 
basis. Identified Ports are: (i) Karwar, (ii) Old Mangalore(Bendre Side), (iii) Old Mangalore (City Side), and 
(iv) Malpe. Necessary administrative measures are being taken to appoint Concessionaires through a 
competitive tendering process.
f. Comprehensive Development of Islands: Strategic steps have been initiated to develop islands in 
the Uttara Kannada district to bolster coastal tourism. Seven major islands have been identified for 
development, and a Geographic Information System (GIS)-based Master Plan has been finalized. A 
Transaction Advisor has been on boarded. Action is being taken to present the TFER, RFP(Request for 
proposal), and DCA(Draft Concession Agreement) reports before the PPP Appraisal Committee (PPAC).
g. International Cruise and Tourism Port (ICTP): An International Cruise and Tourism Port of global 
standards is proposed for development in the Dakshina Kannada district. IIT Madras has submitted the 
draft feasibility report, and subsequent proceedings are being initiated based on the recommendations 
therein.
7. Centrally Sponsored Sagarmala Project
To augment infrastructure at major and minor ports, promote maritime cargo and passenger transport, and 
develop national waterways, the Ministry of Shipping, Government of India, has implemented the Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme (CSS) under the Sagarmala program. In the State of Karnataka, a total of 26 projects with 
an aggregate outlay of Rs.1085.16 Crore have been approved by the Union Ministry of Shipping. The details 
of the key projects are as follows:
1. Con struction of a 350-meter Coastal Berth at Old Mangalore Port: Estimated Cost of the project is  
Rs.65.00 Crore. The project has achieved 90% physical completion. Key components including the deck 
slab, overhead tank, warehouse, and approach roads are finished. Cumulative expenditure stands at 
Rs.57.79 Crore, with a target completion date of March 2026.

Sea Erosion Protection Works
To mitigate the impact of severe sea erosion across the coastal districts of Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, and 
Uttara Kannada, and to safeguard human settlements and vital infrastructure, the Department is implementing 
various scientific protection measures. During the financial year 2024-25,  a total of 2,285 meters of sea 
erosion protection walls were successfully constructed at highly vulnerable locations across the three coastal 
districts incurring an Expenditure of  Rs.28.57 Crores. An amount of  Rs.15.00 Crore  has been allocated for 
these works d uring financial year 2025-26 (Up to December 2025). Construction of 600 meters of sea erosion 
protection walls has been completed during the current fiscal year as of the end of the third quarter incurring 
an expenditure of Rs.7.50 Crores upto Dec-2025.
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) and National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF): In accordance 
with the recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission, specialized financial mechanisms National 
Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) & National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) have been operationalized for 
the scientific and long-term resolution of sea erosion. To initiate permanent remedial measures in high-risk 
zones, Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) have been prepared and submitted for administrative processing:

Inland Water Transport Ferry Services: To facilitate seamless public transit across the State’s rivers and 
backwater regions, ferry services are being effectively managed and operated under the Inland Water Transport 
(IWT) framework. Currently, a total of 67 ferry and boating service points are operational across the State. A 
total of 09 ferry services are directly managed by the Department through the deployment of departmental 
mechanized vessels. 28 ferry services are operated through a public auction and lease process, functioning 
under the technical supervision and regulatory oversight of the Department. The remaining 30 ferry points 
are managed and operated by Zilla Panchayats, the Department of Tourism, the Forest Department, and 
various private organizations.
Inventory of Vessels: To ensure efficient and safe operations across various ferry points, the Department 
maintains and deploys a diverse fleet of vessels(Landing Craft Tank (LCT), Mini LCT Fiberglass, Mechanized 
Boat Mechanized Steel Boat, Wooden Dumb Boat, OBM (Outboard Motor), Fiberglass Boat and Aluminium 
Boat).
Revenue Performance: For the current financial year 2025-26 (from April 2025 to December 2025), the 
Karnataka Maritime Board has collected a total revenue of Rs.0.65 Crore from ferry service operations.
Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL)
In order to augment to the public transportation in Bengaluru and also to reduce the pressure of traffic, Metro 
Rail has come up in Bengaluru. It is a vital component of the transformation of the urban transport scenario. 
With urban population continuously growing, there is a need for green solutions. Mass Rapid Transit Systems 
are fast, safe and comfortable to travel. This alone will encourage people to switch over from personalized 
vehicles to public transport. 
Bangalore Metro Rail Project Phase-1 having a total track length of 42.3 Kms, is already running from 2011. 
East to West from Bayyappanahalli to Mysuru Road (18.10 Kms) and North to South from Nagasandra to 
Yelachenahalli (24.20 Kms).
Bangalore Metro Rail Project Phase-2 consists of Extensions to 4 existing lines of Phase-1 and 2 New Lines. 
The total length of Phase-2 is 75.06 Kms with 61 stations (49 Elevated and 12 Underground).  The estimated 
project cost is Rs. 30,695 Cr.  Presently, 53.80 Kms is completed and commissioned. 7.50 Kms length of 
elevated section in Reach-6 from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere is scheduled to be opened in May-2026.  
13.76 Kms Underground section in Reach-6 is scheduled to be opened in December-2026.  Physical and 
Financial progress as on December-2025 is 95.10% & 92.99% respectively.

10.3 BANKING AND FINANCE INCLUDING COOPERATIVES- 2025-26
10.3.1  Introduction
Karnataka State has a fairly well-developed financial infrastructure. The State has pioneered in establishment 
of many leading commercial banks and is home to a wide network of commercial bank branches in the 
country. Currently, 12 Public Sector Banks, 21 Private Commercial Banks, 1 Regional Rural Bank, 1 Apex Co-
operative Bank, 21 DCC Banks, 1 KSCARD Bank, 1 KSFC, 8 Small Finance Banks, 3 Payment’s Banks  and 1 Local 
Area Bank are operating in the State. Disbursement of credit in rural areas takes place through these banks.
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), as an apex level financial institution, plays 
a lead role in the promotion of agriculture and rural development, by preparing Potential Linked Credit 
Plans (PLPs) and annual action plans at the grass root level. A major portion of NABARD’s refinance and 
developmental initiatives are channelized through the banking sector.

A. Refinance Support: NABARD offers short-term refinance to State Cooperative Banks, Regional Rural 
Banks, and approved financial institutions for activities related to agriculture, rural development, and small 
industries, including artisan and cottage industries. The various products through which NABARD extends this 
refinance is as follows:
NABARD extends refinance to Cooperative Banks and Regional Rural Banks at a concessional rate of 4.5%. It 
also extends refinance to Scheduled Commercial Banks at the same rate for the ceded PACS. Additional Short 
Term Seasonal Agricultural Operations at a competitive rate has been introduced to address severe liquidity 
problems in cooperative banks. 
B. Short Term Credit for purposes other than crop production: NABARD provides Short Term refinance to 
Cooperative Banks and RRBs to meet various short-term credit needs of farmers, including crop marketing, 
fisheries support, and working capital for economic activities. It also extends Short Term refinance for 
handloom weavers and related organizations.
C. Interest Subvention Scheme of the Government of India: NABARD implements the Government of India’s 
Interest Subvention Scheme for RRBs and Cooperative Banks, offering a 1.5% interest subvention on crop 
loans up to Rs. 3 lakh at a rate of 7% per annum along with a 3% incentive for promptly repaying farmers.
D. The KCC Scheme, introduced in 1998-99 is a step towards providing hassle free, adequate and timely credit 
to the farmers from the banking sector. Progress under Kisan Credit Card  Scheme in Karnataka is shown in 
Table 10.36.

interest subvention to financially support projects aimed at boosting ethanol distillation capacity or setting 
up distilleries for 1st Generation (1G) ethanol production from feed stocks such as cereals and sugarcane.
F. Investment Credit for Agriculture: NABARD offers long-term refinancing to banks to boost credit for farmers 
and rural artisans, supporting both agricultural and non-agricultural sectors. This facilitates capital formation 
and rural employment, while also meeting the credit needs of Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Self-Help Groups 
(SHGs), and government subsidy schemes.

H. Apart from regular refinancing support, NABARD has innovatively revitalized the rural economy during the 
Covid-19 pandemic. Some of the special refinance schemes are as follows.
i)  Special Refinance Facility for World’s Largest Grain Storage:  This initiative focuses on improving 
food grain storage and minimizing waste by evolving Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) into 
multifunctional entities. It enhances food security and boosts farmers’ pricing power, with the first phase 
successfully completed at Ekamba PACS in Karnataka and the second phase currently in progress.
ii)  Special Refinance Scheme under the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME): 
This scheme aims to enhance credit access for rural micro-food processing businesses, modernizing 
family-run enterprises and aiding their formal sector transition. It promotes sustainable livelihoods 
and women’s employment, offering long-term refinance at a concessional 4% interest rate through the 
Automatic Refinance Facility (ARF).
iii)  Special Refinance Scheme on Aspirational Districts and Credit Starved Districts: Under this scheme 
Raichur and Yadgir districts are eligible for special refinance of upto Rs. 1,000 Crore to RRBs & Cooperative 
Banks with 100 bps less than  the prevailing interest rate.
iv)  Special Refinance Scheme on Deendayal Antyodava Yojana : National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-
NRLM): The interest rate on refinance is @4% for loans given to all women SHGs upto Rs.3 lakh with 
maximum interest rate of 7% p.a. and @3% for loans given from Rs.3 lakh to Rs. 5 lakh with maximum 
interest rate of 10% p.a. 
v)  Special Refinance Scheme for Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development: This scheme, 
implemented from 24 June 2020, offers a rate of interest 50 bps points lower than the prevailing rates 
for RRB and Cooperative Banks. It aims to address infrastructure gaps and mobilize investment in Animal 
Husbandry Infrastructure through the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) by 
the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, 
GoI.
vi)  Special Refinance Scheme for Rural Home Loans bundled with Solar Roof Top (SRT) with 0.5% rebate on 
prevailing interest for prompt repayment of principal & interest.

vii)  NA BARD provides long-term loans to State Governments for contributing to the share capital of

viii) NA BARD provides relief to farmers affected by natural disasters by converting short-term agricultural

10.3.9   Impact of RIDF in the State
Some of the outcomes under RIDF Projects in the state are increasing the state’s irrigation potential to 5.64 
lakh hectares. Enhancement of Rural connectivity through strengthening and improvement of 45,972 km 
of rural roads and the construction of 58,874 meters of rural bridges. Development of  2,030 veterinary 
institutions, 262 rural godowns, 925 rural market infrastructures, 317 Raita Sampark Kendras, 33 fish jetties, 
and 12 fish farms/ponds in the agriculture and allied sector. Additionally, the social sector has seen support 
for 13,501 rural educational institutions and improvements in 345 public health institutions.
10.3.10 Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF)
Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF), initiated in the FY2020 Union Budget with a total corpus of Rs.10,000 crore, aims 
to enhance micro-irrigation coverage. It includes a 3% interest subvention by the GoI and additional state 
resources beyond the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana —Per Drop More Crop. So far, Rs.290 crore
