6. NAAC Accrediation: The apex Quality Assurance Agency of the country, NAAC has practiced the philosophy 
of being an ‘enabling organization’, to achieve the desired quality consciousness for global competence among 
Higher Education Institutions (HEIs).
7. Three-Tier Quality Assurance Structure
 1. Na tional level – National Assessment & Accreditation Council (NAAC)
 2. St ate-level – State Quality Assurance Cell (SQAC)
 3. Ins titution level – Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)
State Quality Assurance Cell (SQAC): State Quality Assurance Cell (SQAC) is a cell monitored by the 
Commissioner of Collegiate Education. The SQAC will guide and coordinate the work of the Internal Quality 
Assurance Cell (IQAC) of Colleges to achieve the desired quality in higher education and also to obtain good 
grades in the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) A&A process. The role of SQAC starts 
with the allocation of funds to colleges for annual IQAC activities and the NAAC A&A process, monitoring the 
functions of IQACs, assisting in the documentation of IQAC as per the NAAC requirements at the college level. 
SQAC will also coordinate with NAAC to assist the colleges with the required information which is necessary 
for the process. Vision: “To enhance quality initiatives of Government First Grade Colleges in Karnataka”.  The 
total allocation of Rs.200 lakhs for the year 2025-26 is released for the following. 
 Y Rs. 50 lakhs to 406 colleges for IQAC related activities at the rate of Rs. 12,300/- per college.
 Y Rs. 50 lakhs to 200 colleges for purchase of printers at the rate of Rs. 25,000 per college.
 Y Rs. 100 lakhs to 221 colleges to purchase of printers at the rate of Rs. 9650 and Rs. 9650 for 421 colleges 
for FQAC activities.

7. Challenges
Government First Grade Colleges under the purview of the Department of Collegiate Education are facing 
shortage of Physical and Academic Infrastructure. 
a) In troduction of new subjects, new courses, new combinations and ever-increasing student strength has 
led to shortage of classrooms, laboratories and Library facilities.
b)  Man y Government First Grade Colleges do not have own buildings and hence it is difficult for these 
colleges to undertake development activities in a full fledged manner and get good NAAC grades.
c)  Ab sence of Compound wall, play ground, drinking water, toilet and internet facilities in most of the 
Government First Grade Colleges. 
d)  Ther e is a perceptible dearth of teaching-non-teaching staff in Government First Grade Colleges due to 
the introduction of new courses and subject combinations. 
e)  Acut e shortage of Research Grants and research facilities in Government First Grade Colleges are a grim 
reality.
Way Forward
a) Impr oving the Gross Enrolment ratio (GER) by providing required infrastructure and filling the vacant 
teaching staff. 
b) Iden tifing and introducing market-driven courses to enhance the employability of students by imparting 
training in conversational English. 
c) Str engthening  the Placement Cells in Colleges to provide employment opportunities to the students.

11.3 WELFARE OF SCHEDULED CASTES 
The Government of Karnataka is striving to achieve faster, sustainable, and more inclusive growth, with a 
particular focus on improving the capabilities and productive endowments of the economically disadvantaged 
and socially marginalized sections of the State. To achieve this, the Social Welfare Department and development 
corporations of the State are implementing a range of programs designed to promote the welfare of SCs and 
thereby place them on the path of mainstream of development. Notably, the SC population has increased 
from 0.86 crores during the 2001 census to 1.05 crores in the 2011 census, and the ST population has similarly 
increased from 0.35 crores during the 2001 census to 0.42 crores in the 2011 census. As per the projected 
population for the year 2025, the SC population is 1.42 crores and ST population is 0.60 crores. District wise 
population of SC/ST as per the census 2001, 2011 and projected for the year 2025 is given in Appendix 11.8. 
The Department of Social Welfare implements various Programs and Schemes for the upliftment of Scheduled 
Castes. Department aims to empower scheduled castes and ensure protection of their constitutional rights.
During the year 2025-26, an amount of Rs.5989.66 crores has been allocated, of which Rs.3601.95 crore has 
been released and expenditure incurred up to end of December 2025 is Rs.3264.01 crores.  
Details of various Schemes implemented by the department are as below:
i) Pre-matric Scholarships
Pre-matric scholarship is a significant scheme, introduced to encourage children belonging to SC households, 
with annual family income less than Rs.6.00 lakhs to continue their school education. Pre-Matric scholarship 
is sanctioned annually at the rates mentioned below: -
Class / Standard Boys Girls 
1 – 5 Rs.1000 Rs.1100
6 – 7 Rs.1150 Rs.1250
8 Rs.1250 Rs.1350
The scholarship for 9th and 10th standard students with annual family income of less than Rs.2.50 lakhs, 
is sanctioned by the Central Government.Rs.3,500 for Day Scholars and Rs.7,000 for Hostellers is being 
provided. During the year 2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an amount of Rs.9258.00 lakhs has been 
spent providing scholarship to 8.21 lakh students.
ii) Post-matric Scholarships
Post-matric scholarships include day scholarships, compulsory fees for educational institutions, and 
maintenance costs for hostel students. The post matric scholarship is directly debited to the bank account 
of students whose annual family income is less than Rs.2.50 lakhs. During the year 2025-26 up to the end 
December 2025, an amount of Rs.25000.00 lakhs has been spent providing scholarship to 2.55 lakh students.
iii) Prize Money to Meritorious Students
The main objective of this scheme is to reward talented Scheduled Caste students and to encourage them 
to continue their education. Under this scheme, the prize money is awarded to Scheduled Caste students 
who have passed first class in the SSLC and Post-Matric Courses in the first attempt. The financial incentive 
of Rs.7,000/- to Rs. 35,000 / - is awarded under this scheme. In addition, students securing 1st to 5th 
rank in universities are awarded Rs.50,000/-. Also students who are admitted in National level prestigious 
Institutions like IITs/IIMs/AIMs/IISc/NITs are being given an one-time financial incentive of Rs.2.00 lakhs. 
Further, students who clear CA/ICWA/Company Secretary Examinations are awarded Rs.1.00 lakh incentive 

PDF_PAGE 530
522
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
for clearing both intermediate and final exams. During the year 2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an 
amount of Rs.10,000.00 lakhs has been spent for providing prize money to 69114 students.
iv)  Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Overseas Scholarship for students studying in foreign universities
Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to those who pursue post graduate and PhD at reputed 
foreign universities/institutions approved by the government. Selected candidates with an annual family 
income of Rs.8.00 lakh are paid/reimbursed 100% tuition and other fees. 50% of the cost is reimbursed 
to beneficiaries with an annual income limit of Rs 8.00 lakh to Rs.15.00 lakhs. Further, 33% of the cost is 
reimbursed to beneficiaries with an annual income of Rs.15.00 lakhs to Rs.25.00 lakhs. During the year 2025-
26 up to the end December 2025, an amount of Rs.5000.00 lakhs has been spent for providing overseas 
scholarships to 362 students.
v) Indira Gandhi Professional Development Institute
Pre-examination training is imparted for various competitive exams such as UPSC/KAS/Group-C/SSC/RRB & 
Banking examinations, at free of cost in prestigious coaching institutes of New Delhi, Hyderabad and various 
State level institutions. Candidates selected for the training will receive tuition fees and scholarship. During 
the year 2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an amount of Rs.850.00 lakhs has been spent for providing 
training to 2500 students. 
vi) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Post-Metric Hostels
There are 719 post-metric hostels to encourage SC students to pursue their higher education at college 
level. During the year 2025-26 up to the end of December 2025, for the maintenance of these hostels, the 
Government has incurred an expenditure of Rs.30,000.00 lakhs benefitting 1.18 lakh students.
vii) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Pre-metric Hostels
There are 1215 pre-metric hostels Students staying in hostels from 5th to 10th grade will be provided with 
meals, books, toothpaste, uniforms, beds, shoes, etc., During the year 2025-26 up to the end of December 
2025, for the maintenance of these hostels, the Government has incurred an expenditure of Rs.33,320.00 
lakhs benefitting 98489 students.
viii) Construction of Hostel Buildings
Pre-metric and post-metric hostel buildings for students belonging to the SC community are constructed.
During the year 2024-25, an amount of Rs.22,500.00 lakhs had been spent to construct 119 hostels. During 
the year 2025-26, Rs.6,374.00 lakhs has been spent up to the end of December 2025 and the construction of 
hostels is under progress.
ix) KREIS Residential Schools
The Department of Social Welfare has set up Karnataka Residential Education Institutions Society (KREIS), to 
provide quality residential education to students from 6th to 10th standard. Totally, 529 residential schools 
are run by the KREIS under SC Department. 47 schools have been upgraded to offer PUC education at the 
KREIS schools.
Along with academic classes, these residential schools are providing students with facilities such as meals, 
stationery and books, uniforms, shoes, socks, tie-belts, bedding, oil, soap and medical facilities. During the

11.3.1. Dr.B.R. Ambedkar Development Corporation (ADCL)

I. Self-employment Programme
Under Self-employment Scheme, unemployed Scheduled Caste prospective beneficiaries are being

II. I.S.B (Industries service and Business) Scheme
This scheme is introduced mainly to help unemployed Scheduled Caste to improve their economic condition 
by taking up business activities such as HOPCOMs, grocery shops and other micro business. 
III. Land Purchase Scheme
The scheme was launched during 1990-91 to make the landless agricultural labourers as land holders by 
purchasing lands from non-SC/ST land holders. Under this scheme, 2 acres of dry land or 1 acre of wet land 
will be distributed to the beneficiaries. The unit cost fixed is Rs.25.00 lakhs, for 5 districts (Bengaluru urban, 
Bengaluru Rural, Chikkaballapura, Ramanagar and Kolar) and Rs.20.00 lakhs for the remaining 26 districts.  
Under this scheme, 50% will be subsidy and 50% as term loan with 6% interest rate which has to be repaid

11.4 SCHEDULED TRIBES WELFARE
The Government of Karnataka’s priority is to create an environment where people from the fringes of society 
can live with self-respect. This goal will be achieved through education, employment and empowerment. In 
this regard, the Government is implementing several development programs for the welfare of Scheduled 
Tribes through the Department of Scheduled Tribe Welfare and the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled 
Tribes Development Corporation, a brief description of which is as follows.
The Department of Scheduled Tribes Welfare implements various Programs and Schemes for the upliftment of 
Scheduled Tribes. Department aims to empower scheduled tribes and ensure protection of their constitutional 
rights. During the year 2025-26, an amount of Rs.2,213.36 crores has been allocated, of which Rs.1,421.70 
crore has been released and up to end of December 2025 an expenditure of Rs.964.22 crores is incurred.  
Details of various Schemes implemented by the department are as below:
i) Admission of Scheduled Tribe Talented Students to Prestigious Schools
Talented Scheduled Tribe students are selected and admitted from 6th standard to prestigious residential/
non-residential schools in respective districts. Under this scheme, the fees and other maintenance expenses 
of each student are borne by the department. During the year 2025-26 up to the end of December 2025,an 
amount of Rs.621.58 lakhs has been spent and 2336 students have benefited from this scheme.
ii) Pre-matric Scholarships
Pre-matric scholarship is a significant scheme, introduced to encourage children belonging to ST households, 
with annual family income of less than Rs.6.00 lakhs to continue their school education. Pre-Matric scholarship 
is sanctioned annually at the rates mentioned below: -
Class / Standard Boys Girls 
1 – 5 Rs.1000 Rs.1100
6 – 7 Rs.1150 Rs.1250
8 Rs.1250 Rs.1350
The scholarship for 9th and 10th standard students with annual family income of less than Rs.2.50 lakhs, 
is sanctioned by the Central Government. Rs.3,000, for Day Scholars and Rs.6,250 for Hostellers is being 
provided. During the year 2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an amount of Rs.3,962.30 lakhs has been 
spent providing scholarship to 2.21 lakh students.
iii) Post-matric Scholarships
Post-matric scholarships include day scholarships, compulsory fees for educational institutions, and 
maintenance costs for hostel students. The post matric scholarship is directly debited to the bank account 

PDF_PAGE 537
529
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
of students whose annual family income is less than Rs.2.50 lakhs. During the year 2025-26 up to the end 
December 2025, an amount of Rs.19,690.67 lakhs has been spent providing scholarship to 36128 students.
iv) Prize Money to Meritorious Students
The main objective of this scheme is to reward talented Scheduled Tribe students and to encourage them 
to continue their education. Under this scheme, the prize money is awarded to Scheduled Tribe students 
who have passed with first class in the SSLC and Post-Matric Courses in the first attempt. The financial 
incentive of Rs.7,000/- to Rs. 35,000/- is awarded under this scheme. In addition, students securing 1st to 
5th rank in universities are awarded Rs.50,000/-. Also students who are admitted in National level prestigious 
Institutions like IITs/IIMs/AIMs/IISc/NITs are being given an one-time financial incentive of Rs.2.00 lakhs. 
Further, students who clear CA/ICWA/Company Secretary Examinations are awarded Rs.1.00 lakh incentive 
for clearing both intermediate and final exams. During the year 2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an 
amount of Rs.5,818.59 lakhs has been spent for providing prize money to 31918 students.
v)  Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Scholarship Scheme (Prabuddha)
Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to those who pursue post graduate and PhD at reputed 
foreign universities/institutions approved by the government. Selected candidates with an annual family 
income of Rs.8.00 lakhs are paid/reimbursed 100% tuition and other fees. 50% of the cost is reimbursed 
to beneficiaries with an annual income limit of Rs 8.00 lakhs to Rs.15.00 lakhs. Further, 33% of the cost 
is reimbursed to beneficiaries with an annual income of Rs.15.00 lakhs to Rs.25.00 lakhs. During the year  
2025-26 up to the end December 2025, an amount of Rs.1,384.22 lakhs has been spent for providing overseas 
scholarships to 52 students.
vi) Pre-Examination Training for various competitive exams
Pre-examination training is imparted for various competitive exams such as UPSC/KAS/Group-C/SSC/RRB 
& Banking examinations at free of cost in prestigious coaching Institutes of New Delhi, Hyderabad and 
various State level institutions. Candidates selected for the training will receive tuition fee and scholarship.
During the year 2025-26 (Up to December-2025), an amount of Rs. 550.00 lakhs has been spent benefitting 
958candidates.

meals, books, toothpaste, uniforms, beds, shoes, etc., During the year 2025-26 up to the end of December

xxii) Nutrition program for Aboriginals
The aboriginal tribes of Koraga and Jenukurubaare living in Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kodagu, Mysore, Uttara

11.4.1 Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation 
A large number of ST households continue to be deprived of productive assets and income earning avenues. 
Therefore, Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation is implementing several 
developmental schemes such as Self-Employment Scheme, Land Purchase Scheme, Ganga Kalyana Scheme 
& Micro Credit Scheme for the economic development of Scheduled Tribes households in the State. A brief 
progress of the schemes implemented by the Corporation is presented below.
1) Direct Loan under Self Employment
From 2020-21, Self-Employment Direct Loan Scheme is being implemented under the Self-Employment 
Program, for the scheduled tribe unemployed youth/women to undertake self-employment, 50% of the 
target of the scheme is dairy farming and the remaining 50% target is vegetable, fruit growing, fish and meat 
sales, sheep/pig/rabbit farming. 50% loan and 50% subsidy on the unit cost of Rs.1,00,000/- will be released 
in 02 instalments at the rate of 4% p.a. During the year 2025-26, up to the end of December 2025 an amount 
of Rs.323.00 lakhs has been spent for 323 beneficiaries. 
2) Self-employment (ISB)
Under this scheme, the scheme will be implemented with the assistance of the Corporation and bank facilities 
for the youth of the Scheduled Tribes to start self-employment units in small business, small industry and 
service sectors. 70% of the unit cost or a maximum of Rs.2.00 lakhs will be subsidized and the remaining 
amount will be a bank loan. For the purpose of purchasing goods transport vehicles, 70% of the unit cost 
or a maximum of Rs.4.00 lakhs will be subsidized and the remaining amount will be a bank loan. During the 
year 2025-26 up to the end of December 2025 an amount of Rs.1,119.07.00 lakhs has been spent for 156 
beneficiaries.
3) Micro Credit Finance
Under this scheme, skilled or unskilled Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries belonging to semi urban or urban areas 
of the Self-Help Groups are covered to develop their small business activities. The unit cost is Rs.25,000/- per 
beneficiary, out of which Rs.15,000/- is subsidy and Rs.10,000/- is margin money from State Government.  
The term loan will carry interest @ 4% per annum. During the year 2023-24, an expenditure of Rs.45.00 lakhs 
has been spent for 09 beneficiaries.  For the year 2025-26, an amount of Rs.325.00 lakhs has been allocated 
to cover 1300 beneficiaries. 
4)   Ganga Kalyana Scheme
a. Individual Irrigation Borewell Scheme
Irrigation facility will be provided to the agricultural lands held by small and marginal scheduled tribe farmers 
by digging bore well/open well, Installation of pump, motor and accessories followed by energization of 
borewell.
The unit cost is Rs.3.75 lakhs, which includes subsidy of Rs.3.25 lakhs and loan of Rs.0.50 lakh.  Subsidy of 
Rs.3.25 lakhs include energization of Rs.0.75 lakh.  However, in respect of Kolar, Ramanagara, Chikkaballapura, 
Bengaluru Urban & Bengaluru Rural and Tumkur districts where ground water table is depleted, the unit cost 
is fixed at Rs.4.75 lakhs, inclusive of subsidy of Rs.4.25 lakhs and Loan Rs.0.50 lakh.  Subsidy of Rs.4.25 lakhs 

PDF_PAGE 541
533
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
include energization of Rs.0.50 lakh.  Loan sanctioned to the beneficiaries carries an interest of 6% p.a.  Loan 
and interest are repayable in 6 years in half yearly instalments.
b. Lift Irrigation Scheme
Irrigation facility at free of cost will be provided to the agricultural lands held by minimum 3 small and marginal 
scheduled tribe farmers having their lands nearby river/canal by drawing pipeline and installing pump sets.   
Unit cost is Rs.4.00 lakhs for units upto 8-00 acres of land and Rs.9.00 lakhs in respect of units upto 15-00 
acres of land.
During the year 2025-26 (up to December 2025), an expenditure of Rs.2,701.75 lakhs has been spent for 1462 
beneficiaries under Ganga Kalyana Scheme.

11.5 WELFARE OF BACKWARD CLASSES  
The Backward classes (BCs) constitute major chunk of population who are also deprived of educational 
and economic advancement in the state. Therefore, the Department of Backward Classes Welfare and 
the D. Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (DBCDC) have been implementing various 
developmental programs for socio-economic welfare of the Backward Classes in the state. During the year 
2025-26, an amount of Rs.4789.66 crores has been allocated, out of which Rs.2423.71 crores has been 
released and expenditure incurred up to the end of December is Rs.1322.36 crores. Scheme wise details are 
given below.
11.5.1 Department of Backward Classes Welfare
1. Pre-matric and post-matric scholarships
Pre-matric and post-matric scholarships are being sanctioned to the post matric and pre matric backward 
classes students whose annual family income is not more than Rs.2.50 Lakhs. A scholarship will be granted for 
the backward classes students studying from 9th to 10th class,similarly students studying in PUC and degree 
education, students studying in post-graduation courses and students studying in technical and professional 
courses will be sanctioned annually.

11.5.2 Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (Karnataka Government 
undertaking)
In order to improve economic status of the Backward classes, various schemes sponsored by the State 
Government have been implemented in the State by the D. Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development 
Corporation (DBCDC).
Budget for the Year 2025-26: The State Government has approved Rs.37478 lakhs to the Corporation for the 
year 2025-26. The opening balance as on 01.04.2025 of the corporation’s PD account is Rs 43148 lakhs. A 
total of Rs. 12284 lakhs are proposed to allocate and implement the following schemes for the development 
of Backward classes for the year 2025-26.
1. D. Devaraj Urs Self-employment Individual Loan Scheme
A Financial assistance upto Rs.2,00,000/- per beneficiary is being sanctioned to the members of Backward 
classes, annual income should be within Rs.98000/- for rural area and Rs.120000/- for urban area. Financial 
assistance up to a maximum of Rs.2.00 lakhs for undertaking self-employment, agricultural allied activities, 
business, industry, transport and service sectors, 20% or maximum subsidy of Rs.20,000/- on loan up to a 
minimum of Rs.1.00 lakh and Rs.1.00 to Rs.2.00 lakhs at 15% or minimum Rs. 20,000/- maximum Rs.30,000/-
balance amount of Rs.1,70,000/-will be provided at the rate of interest of 4% per annum. An amount of Rs. 
2859.00 lakhs have been spent on 2859 beneficiaries up to end of December 2025.
2. Ganga Kalyana Irrigation Scheme
Individual irrigation: Irrigation facilities will be provided to the Small and Marginal farmers of the Backward 
classes.
Unit Cost: The total unit cost for Individual Borewell Project is Rs. 4.75 lakhs for Bengaluru urban, Bengaluru 
Rural, Ramanagara, Kolar, Chikkaballapura and Tumakuru Districts in which electrification cost Rs. 75,000/-
per Borewell to be paid to ESCOMs Rs. 3.75 lakhs for other districts out of which electrification cost of Rs. 
75000/- per Borewell will be paid to ESCOMs. In case the unit cannot be completed, a loan of Rs. 50,000/-will 
be sanctioned at an interest rate of 4% per annum.
In this scheme, at least 1 acre of land should be available in Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, Uttara Kannda, 
Chikkamagaluru, Shivamogga and Hassan Districts. In the remaining districts, the farmer should have a 
minimum of 2 acres and a maximum of 5 acres of land.
Open well: in the districts of Coastal and Malenadu regions, Open well Irrigation facility will be provided at a 
fixed unit cost for individual Irrigation borewell scheme. An amount of Rs. 5098.00 lakhs have been spent for 
3338 beneficiaries up to end of December 2025. 

PDF_PAGE 545
537
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
3. Arivu-Education Loan Scheme
The Corporation extends educational loan to the students who are selected through CET studying Medical, 
Dental, Engineering and other 28 Professional courses. The Corporation releases loan maximum of Rs. 1.00 
lakh per annum and Rs. 4 to 5 lakhs for the entire course or actual cost incurred by the student towards 
Admission fees, Tuition fee, Laboratory fee, Examination fee etc., for his/her education. The rate of interest is 
2% per annum. Applicant’s family annual income has to be less than Rs. 3.50 lakhs. An amount of Rs. 1106.54 
lakhs have been spent for 1192 beneficiaries up to end of December 2025.
4. Loan for Higher Education in Foreign Universities
The maximum loan of Rs.25.00 lakhs per annum or a maximum of Rs.50.00 lakhs for the entire course will be 
given to the students to pursue Post doctoral, Master Degree Courses and Ph.D courses at the rate of Zero 
percent interest. The amount also covers the cost of Airfare, Tuition fee, etc., prescribed for all level of courses 
covered under the scheme. Applicant’s family annual income has to be less than Rs.15.00 lakh. An amount of 
Rs. 800.00 lakhs have been provided for 32 beneficiaries during 2025-26. In current financial year 18 students 
have been selected by the selection committee and Rs.50.00 lakhs been released for 2 beneficiaries.
5. Swathantrya Amrutha Mahothsavada MunnadeYojane
A new scheme “Amrutha Munnade” is initiated to provide Skill Development Training to youths of Backward 
classes through short term courses and advanced skill training through government institutions like ITI, GTTC, 
KGTTI, ATDC, Sri Kalidasa Educational Society, VTUs to make them employable to improve their employability 
and socio/economic status. There is no annual family income limit criteria if the applicant is a candidate 
belonging to Category-1. If the applicant belongs to Category 2A, 3A, 3B, the annual family income limit is 
Rs.8.00 lakhs. 1807 beneficiaries have been benefitted up to end of December 2025.
6. Swavalambhi Sarathi Scheme
Under the Swavalambhi Sarathi Yojana a subsidy of 50%, up to a maximum of Rs.3.00 lakhs, will be sanctioned 
for the purchase of a four-wheeler under the Swavalambhi Sarathi Yojana, for unemployed youth from the 
backward classes to undertake self-employment by the D. Devaraja Urs Backward Classes Development 
Corporation. An amount of Rs. 486.00 lakhs have been spent for 162 beneficiaries up to end of December 
2025.
7. Self-Employment Loan through Banks Scheme
A subsidy of 20% of the loan amount availed from the bank or a maximum Rs.1.00 lakh will be provided 
to candidates of Backward classes to perform economic activities/enterprises in order to make them self-
employed. An amount of Rs. 151.80 lakhs have been spent for 254 beneficiaries up to end of December 2025.
8. Sewing Machine Distribution Scheme
D. Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation is currently implementing a scheme of distribution 
of sewing machines to backward classes from poor families. To avail the facility in the said scheme one should 
belong to Backward Classes Category-1, 2A, 3A and 3B. Annual family income for rural area is Rs.98,000/-for 
urban area is Rs. 1,20,000/-. The age limit should be 18 to 55 years. 1444 beneficiaries have been benefited 
up to end of December 2025.

11.5.14 Challenges faced 
 Y Currently, 183338 students are admitted in 1414 post-matric hostels and 67303 students in 1245 pre-
matric hostels under the Backward Classes Welfare Department, total 250641 students are admitted 
in 2659 hostels. Out of 2659 pre-matric and post-matric hostels, 1634 hostels are functioning in own 
buildings, 253 hostels are functioning in free buildings and remaining 772 hostels are functioning in 
rented buildings. 772 hostels are functioning in rented buildings will require construction of own 
buildings. Currently, 415 sites are available for construction of Department own buildings.
 Y Due to the high demand from various Castes of backward Classes Community for construction of 
community halls/Hostel buildings under the various communities development programme Scheme, 
additional grant is required for the above said programme.
 Y There is a lack of basic amenities (CC roads, drainage, and drinking water) in the colonies, where nomadic/
semi-nomadic communities live in the state. Grants are required to provide basic amenities to facilitate 
better quality of life for the nomadic/semi-nomadic community. 
 Y Currently 1414 post-matric hostels are functioning under the department, in which 183338 students 
have been admitted in the Post -Matric hostels. However, there is a high demand for post-matric hostels 

PDF_PAGE 549
541
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
in major educational hubs. Due to more demand in educational centres, there is a need for another 100 
Post-matric hostels with a sanction strength of 100 in each Post matric Hostels.
 Y The students are deprived of the basic necessary facilities in the hostels functioning under the department, 
the necessary basic facilities such as Two Tier Cot, Coir Mattress, Dining Table, Water Purifier, Solar Water 
Heater/Heat Pump, Computer, UPS, Digital Library etc., need to be provided to the hostels, for which an 
estimated grant of Rs.200.00 Crores is required.
 Y There is a high demand from the candidates of backward classes community for UPSC, KAS and Banking 
PO Pre Examination Coaching from reputed training Institutions. Therefore, grant of Rs.30.00 crores is 
required under the training program to provide the said program to more backward classes candidates.
11.5.15 Way Forward
 Y Under the Department of Backward Classes Welfare, 1634 hostels are functioning in own buildings, 253 
Hostels are function in free buildings and 772 Hostels are functioning in rented buildings. In which 772 
hostels functioning in rented buildings will be constructed in a phased manner, if they provide additional 
grants for the construction of the building in every financial year.

11.6 WELFARE OF MINORITIES
The Population of religious minorities as per 2011 census is about 96 lakhs which forms 15.92% of the total 
population of Karnataka.  People belonging to Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, Jain, Sikh and Parsi communities 
comes under religious minorities.  To improve the socio-economic conditions of the minority communities, 
the department is implementing various departmental schemes through Directorate of minorities, Karnataka 
Minorities Development Corporation and other boards. During 2025-26 an amount of Rs.3961.63 crores has 
been allocated, out of which Rs. 2205.39 crores have been released and expenditure incurred up to end of 
December 2025 is Rs. 1789.30 crores. 
11.6.1 Directorate of Minorities
1. Minority Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement
a) Pre-Matric Scholarship
The Pre-matric Scholarship encourages parents of minority communities to send their children to school and 
helps them complete their schooling by reducing the financial burden on the parents. This scheme lays the 
foundation for their academic achievement. The objective of this scheme is to empower minority communities 

PDF_PAGE 550
542
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
through education, leading to upliftment of socio-economic conditions. Scholarships are awarded to students 
who have secured more than 50% marks in the previous class annual examination and the annual income of 
the student parents from all sources does not exceed Rs. 1.00 lakhs. 30% of the scholarship will be reserved 
for girl students. In case sufficient eligible girl students are not available, the remaining scholarship will be 
given to eligible boys.
The said scheme is being implemented by the State Government from 2023-24 as the Pre-matric Scholarship 
(Class 1 to 8) provided by the Central Government to minority students has been discontinued.
During the year 2025-26.Rs. 7017.00 Lakhs has been disbursed to 465813 students till December-2025 
b) Post-Matric Fee Reimbursement Scholarship
The objective of the ‘Fees Reimbursement’ scheme is to provide scholarships and incentives to minority 
community students pursuing post-matric undergraduate, graduate, postgraduate and professional, technical 
and MPhil & Ph.D. courses in government and private colleges/universities in India/Karnataka State.
Scholarship is given to students who have secured more than 50% marks or equivalent in the previous year’s 
semester/final examination. The annual family income of a student pursuing post-matric courses should not 
exceed Rs.2 lakhs.
The annual family income of a student pursuing merit cum means (technical and professional courses) should 
not exceed Rs.2.50 lakhs.
During the year 2025-26, Rs.11556.00 lakhs have been disbursed to 124909 students under the Post-
Matric Scholarship and Fee Reimbursement Scheme for students who were due in 2023-24 & 2024-25 till 
December-2025 
c) National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for students pursuing higher education in abroad
A scholarship scheme is being implemented to provide scholarships to students belonging to the minority 
community of Karnataka state to pursue postgraduate studies in the QS Top 500 universities List-2025 for 
maximum of 2 years abroad. If the annual income of the student family is less than Rs. 8.00 lakhs, a maximum 
scholarship of Rs. 15.00 lakhs will be given for 2 years and if the annual income of the student family is 
between Rs. 8.00 lakhs and Rs. 15.00 lakhs a maximum scholarship of Rs. 7.5 lakhs will be given for 2 years.
During the year 2025-26, Rs. 3919.00 lakhs scholarship has been disbursed to 321 students till December 
2025.
d) M. Phil and PhD Fellowship Scheme
A fellowship programme of Rs. 10,000/- per month has been implemented for a maximum of 03 years for 
minority students pursuing Ph.D. in recognized universities of India/Karnataka State and for a maximum of 02 
years for minority students pursuing M. Phil on JRF model.
During the year 2025-26, An amount of Rs. 52.00 Lakhs scholarship have been spent on 114 students till the 
end of December-2025.
e) B.Sc & GNM Nursing Incentive/Fellowship Scheme
As announced in the Budget Speech 2024-25, an incentive/fellowship amount of Rs. 25,000/- will be provided 
through DBT to minority community students pursuing B.Sc Nursing in Government/Private colleges. During 
2025-26, Rs.162.00 lakhs spent to 650 students who were pending in 2024-25.

4. Hostels for Minorities
a) Pre-Matric Hostels
To facilitate the education of students from religious minority communities, a total strength of 1825 are being

Students from minority communities studying in PUC, Degree, Post-graduate and other courses are eligible

In view of the safety of working women in Bangalore and the municipal corporation limits, 10 working 
women’s hostels have been opened for women.

by the end of December 2025.

11.6.2 Karnataka Minorities Development Corporation Ltd.
The main objective of the Corporation is to extend loan facility to the poorest of the poor among minorities 
so as to enable them to become self-reliant and also to provide social justice, infrastructure, education 
and employment. The Corporation implements the various schemes to improve the social economic and 
educational conditions of the minorities.

7. Direct Business Loan Scheme
Under this scheme, loan to the extent of Rs. 20 Lakhs will be provided to each selected beneficiary for carrying

11.7. WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT
I. Women Population and Women Development Programmes
As per 2011 Census, women population constitute 49.31% of the total state population and the southern 
states of India also have a similar pattern. The following schemes which aim not only on empowering women, 
but also for their well-being in various spheres implemented in the State.
A. Gruhalakshmi Scheme
Gruhalakshmi scheme will play a prominent role in easing the daily financial pressures and ensuring the 
economic empowerment of women. Under this scheme Rs.2000/- will be directly transferred to the female 
head of the family to their accounts every month. It is undoubtedly, the largest financial security scheme that 
has been launched in the country. under this program beneficiaries have been successfully paid through DBT 
till the end of September-2025 and total 12888617 beneficiaries have been enrolled up to November-2025.
For the year 2025-26 an amount of Rs.2860800.00 lakhs has been allocated for this scheme and overall 
of Rs.1375819.19 lakhs have been released, Rs.1133499.20 lakhs expenditure has been incurred. 82.38% 
expenditure has been achieved against the releases.
B. Stree Shakthi
At present there are 1.65 lakh self-help groups in the state, comprising 25.36 lakh women members. Up to 
December-2025 the groups had saved Rs.3425.20 crore since inception. Bank loans have been availed by 
132684 groups to the extent of Rs.3790.80 crore and there has been internal loan circulation for taking up 
various Income Generating Activities. Several programmes like revolving fund, financial incentives, providing 
marketing facilities for the products produced by SHGs etc. are taken up by the department.
It is proposed to provide revolving funds to 3240 Scheduled Caste groups in the year 2025-26 An expenditure 
of Rs.76.70 lakhs have been incurred for 1534 groups as on December -2025.
An amount of Rs.357.20 lakhs has been allocated for the year 2025-26, for the strengthening of groups under 
Stree Shakthi scheme out of which Rs.239.58 lakh has been released till December-2025 and Rs.176.80 lakhs 
expenditure has been incurred.
C. Gender based Budget (Women Component Plan)
Gender Budget is implemented from the State during 2007-08. In Gender Budget, the Government Programmes 
& Schemes under the 29 demands for grants are classified into 2 categories. Schemes and programmes that 
are categorised under the “A” are exclusively for women and girls with 100% financial allocation to women. 
The coverage of the women beneficiaries under the “B” category schemes and programmes ranges from 30% 
to 90%. There are a total of 953 schemes is under category A & B in the Gender Based Budget for the 2025-26, 
out of which 79 schemes are in category ‘A’ & 874 schemes are in category ‘B’ schemes and these schemes 
are being implemented by concerned departments. 
D. Working Women’s Hostel
In the interest of protection and safety of working women, 23 hostels for working women have been started 
in rented buildings in Bengaluru city, Mysuru, Hubli-Dharwad, Belagavi, Dakshina Kannada and Kalaburagi

districts in 2022-23. Women working in garments, industries and other unorganized sectors and working

E. One Stop Centre (Sakhi) (CSS 100%)
The One Stop Centre (OSC), aimed at providing comprehensive care to women survivors of abuse, violence, 
and trauma. OSCs offer a range of essential services such as medical, legal, temporary shelter, police 
assistance, psychological and counselling support. OSCs facilitate aid for women in distress, ensuring prompt 
support and promoting long-term empowerment by providing access to government programs. OSCs also 
foster coordination with other initiatives to combat violence against women effectively.
For the year 2025-26 a revised grant of Rs.1523.84 lakhs has been allocated under this scheme, out of which 
Rs.756.48 lakhs has been released up to December-2025 and Rs.692.51 lakhs expenditure has been incurred. 
Various service facilities have been provided to 7,865 women under this scheme.
F. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence
The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and Rules, 2006 are being implemented in the 
Karnataka state, which is mainly aimed at preventing violence against women and is a major step towards 
achieving gender equality. Free legal services and advice are being provided by the Karnataka State Legal 
Services Authority. 40 Swadhar Kendras established to provide temporary shelter for Domestic Violence 
affected women and counselling services are being provided through 178 Santhwana Centers. 
For the year 2025-26 a revised grant of Rs.1704.35 lakhs have been allocated and an Rs.1012.76 lakhs have 
been released up to December-2025 and Rs.783.52 lakhs expenditure has been incurred. Total 4,470 cases 
have been registered under this Act.
G. Santwana
Santhwana scheme has been implemented since 2000-01. This scheme functioning and providing service 
24X7 counselling and necessary assistance to violence affected women, Legal assistance and counselling 
services are provided to women having dowry harassment, sexual harassment, family violence, rape, etc. At 
present 178 Santwana centers are functioning through NGOs Total 32,883 women are provided counselling 
services by the end of December-2025 
An amount of Rs.1100.71 lakhs have been allocated for the year 2025-26 and an Rs.550.50 lakhs have been 
released up to December-2025 and Rs.541.66 lakhs expenditure has been incurred.
H. Shakthi Sadan (Swadhar Greh & Ujjwala)
The main objective of Swadhar Greh Yojana is to empower women in difficult situations economically and 
socially by providing shelter, training and education. Ujjwala Yojana aims to prevent trafficking of women 
and children and to protect and rehabilitate those who are subjected to trafficking and commercial sexual 
exploitation and to reunite them with their families.
Combining these two schemes, ‘Shakti Sadan’ - a comprehensive relief and rehabilitation home that will 
provide accommodation and various facilities to 50 residents, is being implemented through the services of 
voluntary organizations. At Present 40 Sakthi Sadan are Functioning in the State.

I. Aganwadi Cum Crèches (AWCC)
The Government’s sustained initiative on education and employment of women has resulted in increased 
opportunities for their employment, and more and more women are now in gainful employment, working 
within or outside their homes. The growing industrialization and urban development have led to increased 
migration into the cities. The past few decades have shown a rapid increase in nuclear families. Thus, the 
children of such working women, who were earlier getting support from families while they were at work, are 
now in need of day care services which provide quality care and protection for the children. At Present 128 
Aganwadi Cum Crches (AWCC) functioning in State. And Total 1664 children have received the facility by the 
end of December 2025.
For the year 2025-26 a revised grant of Rs.143.44 lakhs has been allocated by the Central Government (Central 
Share) for the year 2025-26, out of which Rs.143.44 lakhs have been released up to December-2025. Also, 
a revised grant of Rs.95.63 lakhs has been allocated by the State Government (State Share), out of which 
Rs.95.63 lakhs have been released up to December-2025.
J. Women help Line-181 (CSS 100%)
The Women Helpline provides toll-free 24-hours telecom service to women seeking support and information 
by connecting them with Emergency Response Support System (ERSS) for all emergency services like police/ 
fire/ Ambulance services and with One Stop Centres.
Any woman in distress or facing violence within public or private sphere of her life or seeking information 
about women related schemes/programmes, or someone calling on her behalf, can contact the Women 
Helpline-181 for assistance. A total of 102229 calls have been received up to December 2025.
An amount of Rs. 100.00 lakhs have been allocated for the year 2025-26, and an Rs.72.30 lakhs have been

(DHEW) (31 districts) are established.

V. Child Development Programmes
A. Bhagyalakshmi-Sukanya Samridhi Account Scheme
Bhagyalakshmi is a flagship programme of the Women and Child Development department, the state aims 
to improving the sex ratio by encouraging the birth of girl child in the BPL families, and is trying to eradicate 
social evils such as child labour, female foeticide, child marriage and child trafficking. Eligibility criteria to 
enroll under the scheme is extended up to two years after the birth of the child.
Two girl children born in a BPL family are eligible to enroll under the scheme. A fixed amount is deposited with 
the financial partner namely, Life Insurance Corporation of India and the maturity amount is paid to the girl 
child on completion of 18 years of age only after fulfilling the conditions laid down under the scheme.
“Child Tracking System” software is being developed with assistance from NIC to track Bhagyalakshmi 
beneficiaries up to the age of 18 years. All information such as health status, education and migration 
pertaining to the beneficiaries are tracked through the software.
“Bhagyalakshmi-Sukanya Samurdhi Account Yojana” (2020-21): From 2006-07 to 2019-20, LIC was the 
Financial partner of the Scheme, and due to some administrative reasons from 2020-21, the Bhagyalakshmi 
Scheme is implemented through the Sukanya Samruddhi Account Scheme through the Postal Department. 
The name of the Bhagyalakshmi scheme and the conditions for registration of beneficiaries is continued as 
per earlier criteria.
An order has been issued on 10-11-2020 to redesign the Bhagyalakshmi scheme is implemented through 
the Sukanya Samrudhi Scheme of the Postal Department. An amount of Rs.3000/- per annum is deposited in

ICDS is a centrally sponsored scheme, which provides a package of six services i.e., supplementary nutrition, 
immunization, health check-up, referral services, nutrition and health education for mothers and non-formal 
pre-school education for children between the ages of 3-6 years.
There are 69,922 Anganwadi Centres in the state with the total children of 36.13 lakhs out of 69922 AWC in

i. Supplementary Nutrition Programme
Supplementary nutrition is provided to the beneficiaries under the ICDS programme with revised feeding 
norms of 500 calories of energy and 12-15 grams of protein to 0-6 years’ children, 600 calories of energy 
and 18-20 grams of protein to pregnant women/lactating mothers/adolescents girls, 800 calories of energy 
and 20-25 grams of protein to severely malnourished children as a supplement to their normal intake, as 
envisaged in the schematic guidelines. Supplementary nutrition is given for 300 days in a year. The unit cost 
has been revised to Rs.8.00 per beneficiary per day for normal children and Rs.9.50 per beneficiary per day 
for Pregnant/ Lactating/ adolescent girls and Rs.12.00 per severely malnourished children. As per the revised 
unit cost supplementary nutrition food is being provided for 300 days in a year.
During 2025-26, up to December-2025 an amount of Rs.101115.30 lakhs of expenditure has been incurred

C. Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
The PMMVY Scheme provides financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers to improve the health and 
nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. PMMVY is a Centrally Sponsored 
Maternity Benefits Scheme under which cash incentives of Rs.5,000/- is provided directly to the Bank/Post 
Office account of the beneficiary in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode for first child in two installment(1st 
installment Rs.3000/- and 2nd installment Rs.2000/-). The eligible beneficiaries receive the remaining cash 
incentive, as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana after institutional 
delivery, so that on an average a woman gets Rs.6000/-. Under Mission Shakti, cash incentive of Rs.6000/- is 
also provided under PMMVY to eligible beneficiaries for second child subject to the second child being a girl. 
However, to avail benefits for a second child registration during pregnancy is mandatory. This has contributed 
to improving the sex ratio at birth and preventing female foeticide.
Under this scheme 3,14,175 beneficiaries are benefitted up to the end of December-2025. For the year  
2025-26 an amount of Rs.12744.00 lakhs has been allocated by the Central Government (Central Share), 
out of which Rs.4162.10 lakhs have been released up to December-2025 and an expenditure of Rs.2959.93 
lakhs has been incurred. In addition, a grant of Rs.8496.00 lakhs has been allocated by the State Government 
(State Share), out of which Rs.2774.74 lakhs have been released up to December-2025 and an expenditure of 
Rs.1973.28 lakhs has been incurred.

K. Dharti Abha Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA)
This scheme has been launched in the year 2025-26. 164 State Anganwadi Centers have been sanctioned as 
Centrally Awarded Anganwadi Centers under the DA-JGUA scheme in the Scheduled Caste and Tribal villages 
identified by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
L. Chiguru
An innovative scheme called “Chiguru”, a Community Based Acute Malnutrition Management Programme, has 
been implemented in the revenue divisions of Ballari, Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Belagavi, Raichur, Chitradurga 
and Vijayanagar districts of the state in collaboration with UNICEF, CEGIS and IPE global organizations, to 
identify malnutrition in children below six years of age enrolled in Anganwadi centres and improve the 
condition of children suffering from severe and moderate malnutrition.
This project identifies severe malnutrition at early stages, provides medicalnutrition and highly nutritious 
food to children suffering from severe and moderate malnutrition without medical problems, ensuring the 
active participation of pregnant women, lactating mothers and mothers of children under six years of age, 
and promotes community awareness that child nutrition is not only the responsibility of the mother but also 
the shared responsibility of the entire family.
Way Forward
 Y There are 69,922 Anganwadi centers in the state, of which 55526 are in rural areas and 14396 are in 
urban areas. Of the total Anganwadi centers in the state, only 68.19% have their own buildings, while 
22249 Anganwadi centers do not have their own buildings. In addition, 4243 sites are available in rural 
areas and 1092 sites in urban areas for the construction of Anganwadi centers. Due to shortage of sites, 
high cost of purchasing sites and construction, Anganwadi centers have been built in rural/urban areas. 
Government-owned sites can be acquired and construction of priority Anganwadi buildings can be 
undertaken.
 Y Addressing malnutrition among pregnant women, lactating mothers, and children.

providing training programmes for personnel working under the ICDS through government-run 
institutions.
 Y Construction of Anganwadi buildings, from industrial and corporate organizations in the districts and 
Providing basic facilities required for Anganwadi Centers under CSR grants.
 Y A new head of account will be created for the purchase of C.A sites or for building construction, thereby

11.8 KARNATAKA STATE WOMEN’S DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION 
Karnataka State Women’s Development Corporation was established in 1987 for the social and economic 
development of the weaker sections of women in the state. A total grant of Rs.4313.17 lakhs has been allocated 
to this corporation for the year 2025-26. Allocation has been made, out of which a grant of Rs.2343.02 lakhs 
has been released. An expenditure of Rs.2305.51 lakhs has been incurred till December-2025. The projects 
being implemented by the Corporation are as follows:
1. Udyogini Yojane
The main objective of this scheme is to enable women to engage in income generating activities and become 
self-employed and to avoid taking loans through private financial institutions. The Karnataka State Women 
Development Corporation is providing subsidy by facilitating them to get loans through banks. A grant of 
Rs.1500.00 lakhs has been allocated for the year 2025-26 and it is intended to provide financial facilities 
to 1482 beneficiaries. Rs.750.00 lakhs will be released by the end of December-2025. Under the scheme 
Applications are received till 15.01.2026. The applications are currently being reviewed and the achievement 
is under process. 
2. Ex-Devadasis Rehabilitation Scheme
The aim of this scheme is to eradicate the Devadasi system and direct assistance is being provided to 
former Devadasi women under the Devadasi Rehabilitation Scheme. This scheme is being implemented in 
15 districts of the state namely Belagavi, Vijayapura, Bagalkot, Ballari, Koppal, Raichur, Kalaburgi, Dharwad, 
Haveri, Shivamogga, Chitradurga, Yadgir, Davangere, Vijayanagara and Gadag districts. Financial facilities of 
Rs.30,000/- are being provided directly from the Women’s Development Corporation to former Devadasi 
women to undertake various income generating activities like animal husbandry, small shops etc. and make 
them self-reliant.
A grant of Rs.286.44 lakhs has been allocated for the year 2025-26, the target is to provide financial assistance 
to 568 former Devadasi women under the said scheme and progress. The selection process of candidates is 
in progress. A grant of Rs.143.22 lakhs has been released by the end of December-2025. Under the scheme 
Applications are received till 15.01.2026. The applications are currently being reviewed and the achievement 
is under process.

11.9 DIRECTORATE OF CHILD PROTECTION 
Directorate of Child Protection aims to strengthen child protection system at family and community level, 
identify risks and vulnerabilities affecting children, create and promote preventive measures to protect 
children from situations of vulnerability, risk and abuse. 
Mission Vatsalya (Centrally Sponsored Scheme): The Central Government has implemented Mission Vatsalya 
scheme in the year 2022-23 for care and protection of children. This scheme is a road map to achieve 
development and child protection priorities aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It lays 
emphasis on child rights, advocacy and awareness along with strengthening of the juvenile justice care and 
protection system with the moto to “Leave no child behind”. 
An amount of Rs.29167.34 lakhs is earmarked for the year 2025-26, for the implementation of various

11.10 PROGRAMMES FOR THE EMPOWERMENT OF DIFFERENTLY ABLED & SENIOR CITIZENS
The Dept. for Empowerment of Differently Abled & Senior Citizens has been established in the year 1988. 
Department is facilitating Differently Abled Persons to get the benefits of the different schemes implemented 
by the department in order to bring them to the mainstream of the society. The Differently Abled persons are 
categorized 21 Types of Disabilities as per the Rights of Persons With Disabilities (RPWD) Act.
Departmental Programmes 
The programmes of the department are broadly classified into three categories 
1.  Pr ogrammes for Development of Differently Abled persons.
2.  Pr ogrammes for Development of Senior Citizens. 
3.  Soc ial Security and protection programmes.
During 2025-26, an amount of Rs.272.25 Crores is earmarked, released an amount of Rs. 196.49 Crores and 
an amount of Rs.152.29 Crores expenditure is incurred up to the end of December 2025.

Specific challenges and the future vision of the department
 Y As per Census 2011, the population of Differently Abled persons in Karnataka is 13,24,205, which includes 
only 7 different disabilities notified by the government. The Government of India has notified 21 different 
disabilities on 19.04.2017. Therefore, the department in collaboration with the department of Health 
and Family Welfare needs to undertake a regular survey of every Differently Abled person in all the 
districts of the state to bring them into the mainstream of society economically and socially.
 Y Steps will be taken to start rehabilitation centres in those districts where there are no District Rehabilitation 
Centres for the Disabled.
 Y Rehabilitation centres will be provided to all mentally retarded children at the district level.
 Y It will be necessary to provide monthly allowance to the caregivers who take extra care of those with 
severe mental retardation, autism, cerebral palsy, multiple disabilities.
 Y The government should start separate hostels and care homes for employed disabled men.
 Y The department should identify the government land and construct a well-equipped and disability-
friendly residential training center building at all district levels to provide skill development and vocational 
training to 21 types of disabled people, and formulate a scheme to empower disabled people with 8th 
standard and above education to get employment in self-employment/business/nearby industrial areas, 
to be implemented directly by the department.
 Y The department should identify the government land and construct a well-equipped building, a centre 
with spacious premises for senior citizens, nature/natural therapy, yoga/meditation hall and many other 
facilities in all districts, to be implemented directly by the department. This centre should be designed to 
be different from old age homes.
Senior Citizen Cell
As per census 2011, out of total population of 611 lakhs in Karnataka, approximately 7.72% population is 
of senior citizens aged above 60 years which is around 47.18 lakhs. The life expectancy of the Karnataka 
government has been extended to the general public as health care and other related facilities have been 
extended. To ensure the provision of high quality of life to senior citizens as published under Article 41 
of the Constitution of India. The Govt. of Karnataka has formulated State Policy for senior citizens from 
Dated:5-9-2003 which has been evolved with the motto of ensuring better quality of life.
Senior Citizens Welfare Scheme/ Programmes
1.  Fin ancial Assistance to NGO’s to run the Old Age Home: It has been envisaged to provide grants to 
voluntary service organizations to run 65 old age homes in 31 districts of the state. Under this scheme, 
a total annual grant of Rs.12.00 lakhs is being provided to voluntary service organizations through the 
Zilla Panchayat for staff expenses, maintenance expenses, medicines, building rent, newspaper and other 
expenses for a unit with 25 elderly people.
 An amount Rs.528.00 lakhs have been allocated for the year 2025-26, and an Rs.294.00 lakhs will be 
spent up to the end of December-2025.
2.  Gr ants to NGOs to run Helpline for Senior Citizens: Senior citizens are facing many problems like 
harassment, financial exploitation, mental anguish and weakness. To address such problems and provide 
emergency assistance, Senior Citizen Helpline Centres have been started in all the 28 districts of the 
state except Vijayanagara, Kalaburagi and Belagavi districts. This scheme is being run in the premises of 
the District Superintendent of Police of the respective district, in collaboration with voluntary service 
organizations. An annual grant of Rs. 8.75 lakhs, including recurrent and non-recurrent expenses, is 

PDF_PAGE 578
570
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
being provided to the voluntary service organizations running Senior Citizen Helpline Centres.  Rs.192.00 
lakhs has been allocated in the budget for 2025-26 and Rs.11.01 lakhs will be spent up to the end of 
December-2025.
3.  Da y Care Centres for Senior Citizen’s: To facilitate senior citizens to spend time with their peers during 
the day, one-day wellness center has been approved for implementation by voluntary organizations in 
each district. Currently, 27day wellness centers are functioning and steps are being taken to start day 
wellness centers in other districts as well. An annual grant of Rs.9.84 lakhs is being given to the voluntary 
organizations running the day wellness centers, and light breakfast, medical facilities, magazines and 
newspapers will be provided once a day at the day wellness center. Senior citizens also get entertainment 
through TV, radio etc. Rs.208.00 lakhs has been budgeted for the year 2025-26 and Rs.11.28 lakhs will be 
spent till the end of December-2025.
4.  Dis tribution of ID Cards to Senior citizens through online: Identity cards were being distributed to senior 
citizens above 60 years of age through voluntary service organizations recognized by the department. To 
facilitate this system, the Directorate of Electronic Civil Service Delivery (EDCS) has prepared a suitable 
technique under the Seva Sindhu scheme of the e-Governance Department through which senior citizens 
can obtain identity cards online from Integrated Citizen Services Centers such as Bengaluru-1, CSC Seva 
Kendra, Karnataka-1, Atal Ji Janasnehi Kendra and Bapuji Kendra. From date: 01.10.2018 in the current 
year, 406427 cards have been distributed by the end of December-2025.
5.  Con cession in Bus Fare: Senior citizens aged 60 and above are being given a 25% discount on bus fare. To 
avail the benefits of this scheme, senior citizens will have to show any one of the following: identity card, 
voter ID card, driving license issued by the department or an identity card issued by KSRTC.

11.11 HUMAN AND GENDER DEVELOPMENT
Human Development concept richly contributed for human wellbeing. United Nation Development 
Programme (UNDP) states that human development approach focuses on people, their opportunities and 
choices. Hence human development emphasizes mainly on health, education, and standard of living. It 
also includes other dimensions like gender, child, poverty, food security, region, religion, caste, ecology and 
environment, development throughout the life cycle or life span, etc. 

PDF_PAGE 579
571
Human Development
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
The efforts to quantify the qualitative results of human development processes has taken the forms of many 
such HD-Indices as Human Development Index (HDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII) etc.
HDI provides a single measure capturing three basic dimensions of human development viz., health, education 
and living standards. In HDI, economic welfare is given more importance than economic growth. It emphasizes 
that the individual’s capabilities must be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of the country. 
Human Development Reports in Karnataka – An Overview
Karnataka has been a pioneering State in addressing the issues concerned to human development through 
various policy initiatives consequent upon the preparation of human development reports at various levels 
over the years. The first Karnataka State Human Development Report (KSHDR) was published in 1999 which 
helped the State to realize the existence of sharp socio-economic disparities between districts. The second 
KSHDR-2005 provides a comprehensive analysis of district human development goals and outcomes especially 
for vulnerable sections and also examined the efficacy of service delivery mechanisms. 
To understand the status of various indicators of human development at the taluk level, a pilot project of 
preparing the District Human Development Report for Kalaburagi (then Gulbarga), Mysuru (then Mysore), 
Udupi and Vijayapura (then Bijapur) districts was undertaken in collaboration with UNDP during 2005-08 
and these reports were released in 2010. It provides the status of various indicators of human development 
at the taluk level. It is a matter of pride that the Udupi and Vijayapura District Human Development  
Reports were recognized at the national level. Also, the first India Human Development Award - Manav 
Vikas was awarded to the Udupi District Human Development Report for its emphasis on innovation in 
‘Measurement Methodology’. The Vijayapura District Human Development Report reached the final stage of 
the award.
Karnataka is the first State in the country to bring out District Human Development reports for all the  
30 districts in the state simultaneously with assistance of the Zilla Panchayaths in 2014. Based on all the  
30 DHDRs, a compendium titled, “Human Development: Performance of Districts, Taluks and Urban Local 
Bodies in Karnataka, 2014 – A Snapshot”, has also been brought out with a slightly modified methodology in 
2015. It presents details on the relative performance of districts / taluks/ urban local bodies (ULBs) on various 
indices.
The third Karnataka State Human Development Report-2015 was brought out with a specific theme 
on “Accelerating Equitable Human Development”. The approach was to assess inclusiveness of human 
development across caste, class, gender, regions and social groups and accelerate the process.
The Fourth Karnataka State Human Development Report-2022 was brought out with a theme “Bridging  
the Gaps towards sustainable wellbeing”.  The report is being presented with a specific action-oriented  
agenda to reach the human development milestones in Sustainable Development Goals. The effort is to 
explore the strategies and policies that helps to bridge the gaps and promote sustainable wellbeing at micro 
level.
At present the preparation of “District Human Development Report-2025” at 31 District is under process.

Gender Inequality Index (GII)
GII combines some aspects of Gender Development Index(GDI) and Gender Empowerment Index(GEM) and 
it is an innovative approach to assess gender inequality.  It measures gender inequalities in three important 
aspects of human development—reproductive health, measured by maternal mortality ratio and adolescent 
birth rates; empowerment, measured by proportion of parliamentary seats occupied by females and 
proportion of adult females and males aged 25 years and older with at least some secondary education; and 
economic status, expressed as labour market participation and measured by labour force participation rate of 
female and male populations aged 15 years and older. It measures the human development costs of gender 
inequality. Thus the higher the GII value the more disparities between females and males and the more loss 
to human development.

variation in percentage of loss due to gender inequality is from 21% (Udupi) to 44% (Dharwad) (Table 11.32).

Karnataka 84 34 53.0 47.0 31.6 44.2 33.8 77.4 0.377
Source: Karnataka Human Development Report-2022.
Loss due to inequality is lowest among the districts Udupi, Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu and 
Gadag. Dharwad district had highest gender inequality. Bengaluru Rural, Belagavi and Tumakuru are the next 
three districts with high gender inequality index. Bengaluru urban stands at 7th position with GII being 0.322 
indicating 32% loss in achievement across three dimensions due to gender inequality.  
Conclusion & Way forward
The status of human development in Karnataka is witnessing an improving trend over the years. However, the 
variation across districts is high with respect to both Education and Income indicators. 
 Y  Ther e are many flagship programmes like Samagra Shikshan Abhiyana Karnataka and MGNREGA NFSM 
etc. that can be designed and implemented effectively based on local needs. 
 Y More emphasis should be on education outcomes to bring down the disparity across districts. 
 Y  Pr ovide Basic infrastructure facility and medical facilities to Government Hospitals as per the norms.
 Y  The GII can be reduced through improving the reproductive health, female labour force participation and 
political participation.

 ) Promoting entrepreneurship among women- Focused schemes in Animal Husbandry, Dairy, 
Household industries. Expanding coverage of Udyogini scheme. 
 ) Capacity building of women in e-trading and e-commerce. Re-training and skill upgradation in 
existing sectors.
 ) Banks should adopt a single window approach to overcome the procedural and other barriers to 
accessing loans by women, especially those belonging to marginalized groups and communities.
 ) Providing Social Security to women workers in Unorganized sectors.

12.1 CENTRE FOR E-GOVERNANCE (CEG) INITIATIVES RELATING TO THE DEPARTMENT OF 
PERSONNEL AND ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS (E-GOVERNANCE)
Karnataka has an exclusive e-Governance Division in the Department of Personnel & Administrative Reforms, 
headed by Secretary to Government. This was set up in the year 2003 with a view to accelerate the process of 
IT enabling e.g. Government processes for the benefit of citizens and to improve transparency and efficiency 
in administration. The Department of Personnel & Administrative reforms (e-Governance) has created the 
necessary infrastructure for implementing e-Governance initiatives in the state. For the year 2025-26 an 
amount of Rs. 11,061.91 crores, has been provided to the department in which up to December 2025 an 
amount of Rs. 8966.06 crores is released, the expenditure incurred is Rs. 7262.77 crores. The Schemes of the 
e-Governance Department are as follows.
 12.1.1. Karnataka Web Portal
The web portal of Government of Karnataka is an integrated solution providing a single point of information 
and interaction, for all citizens, visitors and businesses. The websites of various Departments are further 
enabling the Government to bring G2C, G2G and G2B services to the citizens and external agencies, increasing 
its authenticity, uniformity and trustworthiness.

12.1.3  Single Sign On (SSO) Pr oject
In the current digital world more and more applications / services are offered online at citizen’s doorstep. The 
spread of web and mobile services has surely simplified life of citizens; however, it also makes it vulnerable. A 
wall of security which was there due to one’s physical presence is now removed. Possibility of stealing one’s 
valuable data by forgery is a threat if proper security measures are not taken. Some of the online services are 
trying to secure the data and communication by authenticating the user through login- password mechanism. 
The approach however has multiple limitations such as:     
 Y Single way Authentication: The authentication mechanism provides only one-way authentication. Only 
service user gets authenticated to the service, however, the authenticity of the service may not be 
guaranteed to the User. User may be accessing a phishing site and is unaware of it. 
 Y Multiple Logins: Users have to remember many logins and passwords to access various services which 
becomes a tedious task and users start maintaining login password list which defeats the whole purpose.
 Y Authentication Mechanism Change: Sometimes online services realize that the data they are sharing is 
more sensitive and will need stronger authentication to improve security. If authentication is implemented 
at every service level there are time, cost and efforts implications.
 Y In order to address these concerns a centralized authentication framework was designed. It provides 
unified login through its own SAML 2.0 based Single Sign On (SSO) for applications in an integrated manner. 
The SSO feature provides registered users a single window to access all services that are integrated with 
this framework.
Secure authentication with four levels (password, OTP , Digital Certificate, Biometrics)  of assurances and Fraud 
management techniques like Symmetric channel encryption, Digitally Signed Token, Alert notifications to

596

Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
users on Browser / OS usage pattern changes, etc. 67 departments have been onboarded for SSO Application 
and many more departments are in the process of onboarding. 
Summary of annual transactions of SSO Application for 2024-25 and 2025-26 (upto end of November 25) 
12,69,171 and 5,18,159 respectively.
12.1.4  e-Kannada Project
The e-Kannada Project aims to effectively implement Kannada across all fields that use information 
technology including the development of software-based services and administrative functions. Its goal is to 
make software services available in Kannada and to ensure the implementation of Kannada in government 
software.
 Y Padakanaja Software: Padakanaja has been developed as a unified digital platform to provide the public 
with various dictionaries and lexicons available from different sources.
 Y Localization (Translation and Transliteration of Technical Terms): The primary purpose of localization 
is to promote the use of Kannada in Karnataka Government’s software-based services and to maintain 
uniformity and standardization of Kannada terminology in software user interfaces.
 Y E-Learning Academy Portal: This is a platform that uses the internet and technology to teach Kannada to 
interested Kannadigas, non-Kannada speakers, and the general public.
 Y Transliteration: Transliteration is software that converts text from one script to another.
 Y Spell-checker Software: The Kannada spell-checking tool helps identify and correct spelling errors in 
Kannada text.
 Y Machine Translation Software (Kannada Kasturi) : In collaboration with the University of Hyderabad, 
English–Kannada machine translation software has been developed. It supports translation from Kannada 
to English, English to Kannada, and Kannada to Hindi.
Goals achieved by the department in the previous period
 Y Padakanaja Software: Padakanaja currently provides 95 dictionaries/lexicons for public use. It contains 
a total of 219,092 Kannada root words and 120,395 English root words.
 Y Padakanaja Mobile Application: A mobile application of Padakanaja has been developed by the 
e-Kannada project and is available to the public through the Google Play Store.
 Y Transliteration: Transliteration services are now available for 14 Indian languages including Assamese, 
Odia, and Gujarati.
 Y Localization: Technical terms from 16 government departments have been localized to ensure uniform 
Kannada terminology across software interfaces.
 Y E-Learning Academy Portal: Kannada learning lessons developed by Dr. PurushothamaBilimale, 
Chairperson of Kannada Development Authority and retired Professor, Kannada Studies Centre, Jawaharlal 
Nehru University, New Delhi have been newly made available e-kalika website (https://kannadakalike.
org/).
 Y Bhashini Agreement: In 2025, the e-Governance Centre signed an agreement with Digital India Bhashini. 
The AIML unit of Centre for e-Governance manages this software. Its corpus is being used in e-Kannada 
applications, and additional corpus will be provided to Bhashini tools in the future.

12.1.5  Karnataka Public Procurement Portal
Karnataka Public Procurement Portal is aimed to enhance transparency, accountability and reliability and 
responsiveness in all Government procurement activities. The Karnataka Public Procurement Portal is 
implemented on an ‘end to end’ solution. It is to the Credit of the project that it is a less-paper office.
The new Karnataka Public Procurement Portal (KPPP) 2.0 has been designed and developed using a micro 
services-based architecture to meet growing demands, leverage technological advancements, and build on 
over a decade of experience. Several key enhancements such as robust workflow engine, layered security, 
mobile enabled, well designed post award of contract module, integrated accounting module, user friendly 
interface, external integration for seamless data exchange and a robust e-auction module are envisaged for 
Karnataka Public Procurement Portal 2.0 This upgraded portal enables procurement processes from estimate 
creation to contract award for all procurement entities across the state. One of its key features is the robust 
Contract Management module.Contract Management module has been implemented with effect from 
31.10.2023 and can be used by all procurement entities. As in Para 422 of the Budget Speech 2024-25, Under 
the Karnataka Public Procurement Platform 2.0, the Contract Management Module will be extended to all 
departments in a phased manner. Accordingly, usage of Contract Management Module is made mandatory 
with effect from 01.08.2024. ”Roster-Based Randomization” in compliance with GO No: FD 707 EXP-12/2024, 

PDF_PAGE 607
599

Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
dated 05.11.2024, has been Implemented in KPP Portal with effect from 01-01-2025. The Uni-Schedule of 
Rates (Uni-SR) has been implemented across all procurement entities for works tenders, ensuring consistency 
and standardization in tendering processes.
In the second phase of the project, e Bank Guarantee (Performance Security Deposit) has been implemented 
with 12 Banks - Canara Bank, State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, City Union Bank, HDFC bank, Indian Bank,

12.1.6 Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)
Direct Benefit Transfer is a major reform initiative to re-engineer the existing delivery processes of the 
Government using IT. Vision of DBT is to enable departments to transfer benefits directly into aadhaar 
seeded bank accounts of targeted beneficiaries. DBT is intended to resolve the issues related to wrong 
inclusion/exclusion of beneficiaries accurately, inaccurate beneficiary identification and unreliable database

12.1.7 e-Office
The e-Office is a Mission Mode Project (MMP) under the National e-Governance Program (NeGP) of the 
Government of India developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), e-Office facilitates the electronic 
management of office procedures, transforming government operations to be more efficient, effective, and 
transparent in handling intra-government processes and transactions. It is designed as a unified, reusable 
system that integrates independent functions and systems within a single framework to promote transparency, 
accountability, and a positive transformation in government work culture and ethics.
Key Features of e-Office are Common Data Sets and Standards, Role-Based Access Control for authorization, 
Workflow Management for streamlined processes,Based on Open Standards and Technologies, Unicode

integrity, transform the government work culture.

12.1.10 Karnataka Resident Data Hub (KRDH)
Karnataka Resident Data Hub was created as a platform to deliver eSign, Aadhaar-related services such as 
Aadhaar authentication and Name matcher services to departments. KRDH collaborates closely with the 
department’s technical team, effectively assisting them with e-Sign services, Aadhaar Authentication, Name 
matcher, Transliteration services. It includes on-boarding process as well as the integration of these services 
with departmental applications.
a) Authentication User Agency/Authentication Service Agency (AUA /ASA)
Aadhaar Authentication means the process by which the Aadhaar number along with the Aadhaar holder’s 
personal identity data such as biometric/demographic information is submitted to UIDAI (Central Identities 
Data Repository-CIDR) for matching, following which the UIDAI verifies the correctness thereof on the basis of 
the match with the Aadhaar holder’s identity information available with it. The purpose of Authentication is 
to enable Aadhaar-holders to prove their identity and for service providers to confirm the resident’s identity 
claim in order to provide services and give access to benefits.
To filter and control the AUA/ASA services availability to the departments of GoK the DBT cell has developed a 
platform called Aadhaar as a service. All the departments are routed through ‘Aadhaar as a service’ platform 
for AUA/ASA transactions. Total 97 departments are using authentication services. The total of 29,79,38,429 
authentication transactions have been performed in Production environment and 1,13,631 in preproduction 
AUA. 29,80,52,060 authentication transactions have been performed in ASA production from Jan 2025 to end 
of Dec-2025. 
Aadhaar authentication services are being used in Five guaranteed schemes. Aadhaar authentication services 
has been extended for Department of Food and Civil supplies for the Ration distribution for 1.6 crore 
beneficiaries. Aadhaar authentication services were effectively used for authentication purpose in Socio-
economic survey of Backward classes and Welfare department.
