12.1.11 Karnataka State Data Centre (SDC)
Government of Karnataka is committed to providing a secure, resilient, reliable and scalable information 
technology infrastructure for all Government Departments, Boards & Corporations for hosting & running their 
e-Governance applications/Initiatives in a secure manner for providing faster and reliable citizen services.To 
realize above objectives, the Centre for e-Governance, had setup a Karnataka State Data Centre in the year 
2011 for hosting the data and applications of various departments in the state. The data centre is being 
managed and supported by CeG hosting many applications of various departments.  At present SDC hosts 
about 535+ applications and 555+ web portals and maintaining infrastructure uptime of 99.95%. 
The data centre is being monitored and managed by skilled resources on 24/7 basis. The State Data Center 
has been hosting G2G, G2C and G2B applications of various departments, boards & Corporations. Some of 
the critical applications include Kutumba, FRUITS, Bhoomi, Seva Sindhu, Sakala, KAVERI 2.0, DBT, SSP , KSRSAC, 
UUCMS, KSBCL, e-Procurement etc. Also, KSDC is instrumental in successfully providing hosting infrastructure 
for registration of beneficiaries to Government Guarantee Schemes like GruhaJyothi, Gruha Lakshmi and 
Yuvanidhi.
In order to ensure business continuity for the critical applications, Disaster Recovery (DR) has been setup and 
operational in Mohali and Near DR in Bengaluru with 3-way data replication technology. 
12.1.12  Cyber Security Operation Centre for SDC (C-SOC-SDC)  
CeG had setup Cyber Security Operation Center to further strengthen the SDC to provide secured and 
robust IT infrastructure & to enable the Government departments to deliver the services more securely, 
and effectively to the citizens and stakeholders. CeG Cyber Security Operation Center is integrated with 
the Threat Intelligence and advisory feeds from CERT-IN, MEITY , NCIIPC to enhance the security posture 
of CeG Cyber Security Operation Center and to proactively mitigate the cyber threats.The existing Security 
Operations Centre (SOC) at the Karnataka State Data Centre is upgraded, and additional licenses for SIEM 
(Security Information and Event Management), EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response), and UEBA (User 
and Entity Behaviour Analytics) will be implemented to enhance data analysis capabilities.To enhance the 
security of applications hosted at the State Data Center the following controls & solutions are implemented. 
Web Application Firewall (WAF)technology has been implemented and 515 applications are created .The WAF 
helps protect web applications by filtering and monitoring HTTP/HTTPS traffic between the web application 
and internet users. It safeguards applications from attacks such as cross-site request forgery (CSRF), cross-site 
scripting (XSS), file inclusion, and SQL injection, among others. Additionally, it prevents malicious activities 
by internet users, protects web applications from external threats and attacks, and ensures that access is 
restricted to hosted content only.
SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) refers to a category of software solutions and 
tools that help organizations collect data about security threats from multiple sources and respond to those 
threats without human assistance. Its primary goal is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of security 
operations by integrating disparate security tools, automating repetitive tasks, and managing incident 
response workflows in a centralized platform.
Network Detection and Response (NDR) is a cybersecurity solution that continuously monitors and analyzes 
an organization’s raw network traffic in real time to detect and respond to suspicious or malicious activities. 
Unlike traditional signature-based tools that look for known threats, NDR primarily uses behavioral analytics 
and machine learning to establish a baseline of normal network behavior and identify deviations from it, such 
as unusual internal (east-west) or external (north-south) data flows, command-and-control communications, 
or lateral movement by an attacker. Upon detecting a potential threat, its main functions are to alert security 

PDF_PAGE 613
605
Good Governance Practices in Karnataka
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
teams and provide rich forensic data for investigation, and it can also initiate automated responses like 
blocking malicious IP addresses or isolating a compromised device to quickly contain the incident.
12.1.13 Karnataka Government Secretariat LAN (SecLAN)
The Secretariat LAN (SecLAN) is the largest Wi-Fi Network spread across VidhanaSoudha, VikasaSoudha, 
MS Building, Annex and Lokayukta. SecLAN 2.0 is the upgraded version providing both wired and Wireless 
connectivity. 1700 Access Points have been provided with adequate backup and 4200 end user devices are 
connected and each device gets a maximum of 700 Mbps bandwidth. The users of SecLAN network can access 
both Intranet applications hosted the State Data Centre and internet applications in Government portals. The 
SecLAN 2.0 project had been declared Go live on 23rd Dec 2021 and operational for 5 years from the Date of 
Go-Live.
Advantages of the SecLAN Network: SecLAN is a universal infrastructure that offers reliable and secure 
network services. It has robust security with multi-factor authentication, which includes electronic devices 
and end-users. A dedicated helpline and NOC (Network Operations Center) team is constantly working to 
provide immediate response and resolution for faults and complaints, It provides seamless connectivity to all 
buildings of the Ministry.
12.1.14 Karnataka State Wide Area Network
The Karnataka State Wide Area Network (KSWAN), operational since December 2009, functions as the state’s 
information highway, offering secure internet, data, and video services to various departments.
KSWAN 1.0 provided secure network connectivity to key Government of Karnataka departments and supported 
major applications such as Kaveri, Khajane, e-Hospital, Bhoomi, e-Procurement, and e-Office. Around 3,000 
government offices were connected through the network. District and Taluka-level KSWAN Control Rooms 
served as aggregation points for traffic, with bandwidth from BSNL and Airtel provisioned and upgraded as 
needed to meet growing demand.
Karnataka upgraded to KSWAN 2.0, a robust and secure network providing end-to-end MPLS-based WAN 
services and LAN connectivity in key government buildings. Numerous departments-including Panchayat Raj 
institutions, Police, Backward Classes Welfare, Agriculture, Education, Excise, and Horticulture-along with 
around 140 Boards and Corporations (nearly 500 links) have been on-boarded. KSWAN 2.0 features advanced 
security with IPSec, DMVPN, and MPLS, and offers dual connectivity for major departments, ensuring over 
99.99% network uptime.
KSWAN 3.0 has been proposed as an upgrade, thereby extending secure network connectivity to all Gram 
Panchayats, covering approximately 22,000 offices. The tender process for KSWAN 3.0 is currently under way.
To accelerate the commissioning of KSWAN links, additional telecom service providers-Vodafone Idea and 
Reliance Jio-have been integrated alongside BSNL and Airtel. Currently, KSWAN connectivity has been 
extended to 1,000 more government offices, bringing the total to about 8,500 offices that use the network 
for e-Office implementation and access to e-Governance services.
Karnataka introduced Video Conferencing (VC) services under the KSWAN 1.0 project in 2009 with 31 
endpoints installed in Deputy Commissioner offices and key rooms in Vidhana Soudha and Vikasa Soudha. 
In 2015, the Taluka VC project upgraded the central infrastructure and added 219 endpoints across Taluka 
offices, DC offices, District Courts, Prisons, and HoD offices in Bengaluru. In 2018, another 104 endpoints 
were deployed, providing second units in DC offices, new units in Zilla Panchayats, and 39 units in DSERT. A 
software-based VC solution was also rolled out to 1,000 Gram Panchayats. In 2022, the VC system was further

12.1.15  Farmer Registration and Unified Beneficiary Information System  (FRUITS)
FRUITS is an e-Governance initiative to have common database of farmers and other beneficiaries who want 
to avail farm related benefits and services from the Government. It also facilitates various departments in 
providing assistance to the beneficiary by connecting to DBT portal and therefore also acts as a repository 
of benefits provided. “FRUITS” is aimed at bringing departments like Agriculture, Horticulture, Sericulture, 
Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Sciences, Fisheries, Backward classes and Social welfare on to a single 
platform.
FRUITS helps in Registering Farmers and citizen involved in farm related activities and provides a unique 
Farmer ID (FID). The Registration is once in lifetime activity, as a result the beneficiary need not carry his/her 
documents to the next department and for every scheme. 
FRUITS is integrated with the state DBT portal and through the DBT portal it is integrated with Khajane II (K2) 
/Financial Management System.
Facilities provided under FRUITS
 Y Facility for departmental hierarchy to register and approve (Maker-Checker concept) and to register 
themselves online and choose adepartment to get  approved.
 Y To modify the registration details and toadd land parcels to an existing farmer.
 Y FRUITS is connected to the crop survey database and crop details are also available.
 Y FRUITS connect to DBT portal (of eGovernance department) and eases out the process of integration 
with K2 by individual departments and also avoids creating recipient ID for individual beneficiary.
 Y Facilitates data exchange with different departmental applications to maintain a common beneficiary 
database.
Till 31st of December 2025 more than 102.95 lakh farmers are registered in FRUITS of which around 71.30 
lakhs are with land. More than 84.40 lakh uniquely registered farmers availed benefits. Around Rs. 39596.98 
Crores of assistance provided through the system by various departments. Banks and Co-Operation institutes 
are also using FRUITS for extending agriculture loan.  More than 16,000 branches including more than 5,500 
PACs are using FRUITS data.
 Y The major benefits were provided to beneficiaries through FRUITS are Crop Insurance, PMKISAN, Market 
Intervention Scheme (MSP , PDPS etc), Milk incentives to milk pourers of KMF, disaster relief to damaged 
crops- Input subsidy for crop loss due to drought and flood, Crop loan through financial Institutions, 
various other schemes and services of Agriculture and allied departments.

12.1.17 Mahithi Kanaja
Mahiti Kanaja (translated as “Treasury of Information”) is a flagship e-governance initiative by the Government 
of Karnataka. It is a single-window web portal designed to promote transparency, accountability, and proactive 
disclosure of information as mandated by the Right to Information (RTI) Act.
The primary goal of Mahiti Kanaja is to comply with Section 4(2) of the RTI Act, 2005, which requires public 
authorities to provide information suomotu to the public. By making data available online, all departments, 
has been implemented on the Mahiti Kanaja portal and also data validation has been successfully carried out 
by the respective on boarded departments.
12.1.18 DigiLocker
DigiLocker is a flagship initiative of Ministry of Electronics & IT (MeitY) under Digital India Programme. 
DigiLocker aims at enhancing the concept of paperless governance. Thus, citizens can get their essential 
documents anytime anywhere authentically and electronically. DigiLocker provides the facility of sharing 
original copies of certificates / documents across different software applications, to citizens. Centre for 
e-Governance has been the nodal department to successfully implement the adoption of DigiLocker in the 
state of Karnataka.
Individual DigiLocker accounts were created and documents were fetched and stored in DigiLocker for rural

officers from various Gram Panchayats in the entire state of Karnataka.  
12.1.19 National Academic Depository (NAD)
The National Academic Depository (NAD) is an initiative of the Ministry of Education that provides universities 
and educational institutions with a 24×7 online depository to store and publish their students’ academic 
records (such as mark sheets and degree certificates). The digital depository ensures easy access to and 
retrieval of academic records, while ensuring their authentication, verification, and secure storage. This system 
helps to reduce the circulation of fake documents. Karnataka ranked No. 1 nationally for NAD implementation 
with 6.4 crore records uploaded, More than 60 educational institutions, including autonomous institutions, 
have been successfully onboarded to NAD.

12.1.20 Karnataka Open Data Initiative (KODI)
The Karnataka Open Data Initiative ecosystem provides support and collaboration to publish datasets 
presented by state departments and focuses on improving stakeholder management. It is designed to 
strengthen the State Open Data Policy, enable inter-departmental and cross-sectoral data sharing, activate 
data analysis, and drive open innovation by providing citizens access to datasets. This is expected to improve 
public understanding of various sectors and state operations. Meetings and training programs have been 
conducted for departments’ Chief Data Officers (CDOs) to promote and facilitate the uploading of data to the 
Open Data platform.To strengthen the implementation of the State Open Data leadership, CDOs have been 
successfully nominated from 37 departments and 165 line departments.

12.1.23  Integrated Public Grievances Redressal System (iPGRS)
Government of Karnataka launched Integrated Public Grievance Management System (iPGRS) on 1st November 
2021 - Kannada Rajyotsava Day. iPGRS, also known as Janaspandana, is a one stop multi-modal, data-driven & 
paperless IT platform to transform the Karnataka’s Grievance Management System for registration, processing 
and redressal of the public grievances regarding the delivery of services and schemes of various Departments 
of Government of Karnataka.
The citizens can register their grievances pertaining to 41 Departments and 3000+ schemes / services delivered 
by the Government. As on end of December 2025, 2,91,925+ grievances have been received through web 
portal (https://ipgrs.karnataka.gov.in), android mobile application -Janaspandana and dedicated call centre 
with the Helpline number 1902.
The iPGRS has also been integrated with the PG portal of Govt. of India- CPGRAMS to receive and redress 
the grievances registered on CPGRAMS. The information on redressal of such grievances will be sent to 
CPGRAMS through a web service. The citizens visiting CPGRAMS of GoI can select Karnataka State and file 
their grievances directly in iPGRS portal.
More than 6000 + probable grievances of the Government of Karnataka and field level officers have been pre-
mapped. More than 35,000 + LMF, L2, L3 officers have been trained.
CMJS (Hon’ble Chief Minister’s Janaspandana), DJS (District Janaspandana), CMO-LMS (Letter Monitoring 
System) & Chief Secretary office (CSO) modules have been newly developed in the IPGRS portal.
Hon’ble Chief Minister’s Janaspandana (CM-JS)
Two separate options are provided to register the applications received from citizens at various places by the 
Hon’ble Chief Minister in the IPGRS portal and is integrated with e-office.

concerned department.

12.1.24 Kutumba
The Department of e-Governance has implemented the “Kutumba” project which is a centralized data 
repository of families in Karnataka consisting of the individual and family attributes. Ration Card data has 
been used as the base and other department databases have been integrated with it. 5.8 Crore residents 
of Karnataka i.e. nearly 90% of the state population (as per 2011 census) have become part of the Kutumba 
system. Kutumba project has been recognised at National level and has been awarded the National 
e-Governance Award (Silver).
Kutumba is an Entitlement Management System which allows the Government to identify residents who 
are eligible for welfare benefits and suo-moto deliver the benefits “without the resident having to apply”. 
Kutumba data has supported Revenue Department to provide Gratuitous Relief for families under Disaster 
Relief activities. 
Kutumba system extends several benefits to citizens. It allows resident to give a single input and auto fetch 
required information without submitting any documents or remembering certificate numbers. Kutumba 

PDF_PAGE 619
611
Good Governance Practices in Karnataka
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
eases out resident interactions with the Government through simplifying processes and enabling objective 
criteria for eligibility. This results in residents having more trust in the Government.
Kutumba system empowers Departments to weed out deceased and ineligible beneficiaries from their IT 
systems. Kutumba has been integrated with the Birth and Death Registration system, which provides the 
details of both new born and deceased person details on a daily basis. Kutumba, in turn, shares the details 
of deceased persons to Department IT systems, which enables them to remove deceased beneficiaries from 
the databases. This has avoided the need for annual verification/life certificate for recurring benefits like 
social security pensions. Kutumba also enables Departments to identify ineligible beneficiaries. Departments 
seek information of beneficiary eligibility, for eg. income, as per scheme guidelines and identify ineligible 
beneficiaries based on Kutumba data and remove them.
Kutumba also aids the Government in Policy making, Planning and budgeting. It provides aggregated data on 
likely eligible beneficiaries and thus impact on budget (through financial outlay required). It also supports the 
Government to implement conditions in schemes like single benefit per family - Kutumba data has been used 
extensively by the Rajiv Gandhi Rural Housing Corporation to identify families.  
Kutumba System empowers Departments to weed out deceased and ineligible beneficiaries from their IT 
systems. Kutumba data has been provided to  the Departments namely, Department of Food, Civil Supplies, 
and Consumer Affairs Karnataka Building and other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Agriculture 
Department, Rajiv Gandhi Housing Corporation Limited, Atal Ji Janasnehi Kendra, Directorate of Electronic 
Delivery of Citizen Services, Directorate of Social Security and Pensions.
On the request of the Departments, Suvarna Arogya  Suraksha Trust, Housing department, Energy department, 
Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood departments. 
Data analysis reports have been prepared and provided to them. 
Kutumba has supported in the successful implementation of flagship Guarantee schemes of Gruha Jyothi and 
Gruha Lakshmi

12.1.25 Business Process Re-engineering (BPR Cell)
As per Budget announcement of 2023–24, a BPR Cell has been established under the Centre for e-Governance 
(CeG). The BPR Cell provides necessary guidance and recommendations to make the existing systems and 
processes more effective. BPR documents are prepared in consultation with the respective administrative 
departments. The BPR document includes details related to the effective use of available databases, simplified 
application forms, reduction in submission of documents, efficient verification processes, and faster service 
delivery.
During 2023–24, the BPR Cell was actively involved in the Business Process Re-engineering of 97 services, 33 
EoDB services. In addition, the BPR Cell continues to actively support various departments by providing BPR 
assistance for services requested by them.

12.1.27  Karnataka State Remote Sensing Applications Centre
Karnataka State Remote Sensing Application Centre (KSRSAC) was established in 1986 and recognizing the 
potential of advanced technologies like Remote Sensing, GIS and GPS in solving various problems of natural 
resource planning, development and management for equitable growth and balanced development on a 
sustainable basis identified as the nodal agency for implementation of Remote Sensing and GIS activities 
(including photogrammetry). It is functioning under the administrative control of the Department of Personnel 
and Administrative Reforms (e-Governance) from 01-04-2019. The functions of centre are as detailed below:
1. Act  as the nodal agency for all remote sensing and GIS activities of the State.
2.  Co ordinate the remote sensing data requirements of the State.
3. Act  as a data bank for satellite data and other data collections relevant to the departments of the State.
4. Assis t user departments /institutions/ agencies/academia / industries in implementation and evaluation 
of remote sensing applications.
5.  Establish, maintain and provide a centralized visual and digital remote sensing data analysis/interpretation 
facility for use by various departments of the State.
6. Undert ake and coordinate remote sensing application projects in various resource/development areas.
7.  Interact and collaborate with the Indian Space Research Organization, other national and international 
organizations in remote sensing and related fields.

12.1.28  Sakala Mission
The Sakala Mission aims to guarantee timely, transparent, and accountable delivery of Government services 
through implementation of The Karnataka Guarantee of Services to Citizens Act, 2011 and (Amendment) 
Act 2014. Vision is citizen friendly governance with time bound service guarantee. Mission is to ensure in-
time delivery of Government services to citizens by practicing innovative and efficient management systems 
through capacity building in Government and empowering citizens to exercise their right to service.
 Y The Sakala scheme legally mandates timelines for over 1,452 Government services under 114 institutions. 
In the year 2025, 209 new services were notified. This is the highest number of services notified under 
Sakala Act in the last 11 years.
 Y Compensation: Officer or his subordinate public servant who fails to dispose the citizen related services 
within the stipulated time line will face penalties for delayed disposition of service, thus ensuring 
accountability at all levels of Government. In the year 2024 an amount of Rs.6.86 lakhs and in the year 
2025 an amount of Rs15.95 lakhs has been paid as Compensation to the citizens who had filed the 
appeals. 
 Y Digital Tracking:  Citizens can monitor their applications in real-time through a seamless, digitized, 
platform, eliminating uncertainty and to ensure transparency and public trust in Government services.
 Y SMS Alert Service: Sakala Mission is implementing receipts and appeal prompt SMS to officers to clear 
the pendency within the stipulated time and also to citizen regarding their appeal status.
 Y Parking Facility: The innovative “Sakala Parking Facility” reduces application rejections for minor issues 
by proactively informing citizens about missing documents or time limit to pay the pending fee as per the 
service requirement. This provides a stipulated time frame to address these gaps. Thus further enhancing 
the in-time disposal of the service and thus contributing to reduction in overall data rejection rate of the 
State. As of now 15 services under 7 institutions have availed Parking facility.
 Y Reasons for Rejection (RFR) Module:   The Sakala Act mandates that a reason be provided for every 
rejection. Earlier the departments entered rejection reasons manually in text fields, often leading to 
vague or unclear justifications. To improve clarity and accountability, the Sakala Mission introduced the 
Reason for Rejection Module. This module provides a structured list of precise rejection reasons through 
primary and secondary categories presented as dropdowns or checkboxes. The primary reason serves 
as a broad category. The secondary Reason provides the exact and specific justification reflected in the 
applicant’s rejection order.
 Y  Sak ala Ranking System : Sakala Ranking formula has been revamped for District and Taluk wise ranking 
whereas new ranking system has been introduced for Institutions and Secretariat Departments 

PDF_PAGE 624
616
Good Governance Practices in Karnataka
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
performance evaluation under Sakala Act for the first time. This new ranking system ensures and promote 
healthy competition between the different entities. 
 Y  Sak ala Citizen Happiness Index : Sakala Citizen Happiness Index is based not just on the satisfaction 
of getting government services delivered in-time but also on the hassle-free journey while availing 
the service. Sakala had launched this initiative in the year 2021. During the year 2024-25 the Citizen 
Happiness Index was 90.79%.
 Y  iGO T:  Sakala Mission has developed a total of 5 modules including 2 exclusive in-house case studies. It may 
be stated that the Sakala Mission is the first institution in the State apart from ATI to post comprehensive 
and full-fledged study module on the iGOT platform.
AVALOKANA (https://avalokana.karnataka.gov.in) is a Government of Karnataka online system that works 
through a Monthly Programme Implementation Calendar (MPIC). It helps departments carry out activities 
in a planned and time-bound manner and uses automated financial data from Khajane-II. Regular updates 
and reviews ensure the timely achievement of targets. It helps to ensure proper preparation for programme 
implementation and avoids last-minute rush of expenditure at the end of the financial year. Monthly 
reporting of completed and pending activities helps implementing officers and reviewing authorities take 
timely corrective action to achieve financial and physical targets.
Based on the Avalokana information, the Hon’ble Chief Secretary conducts a monthly State level KDP Progress 
review meeting, in which the financial progress of programmes/schemes of all departments, the progress 
of Centrally Sponsored Schemes, SCSP/TSP programmes flagship programmes, and the Externally Aided 
Programmes are reviewed. The concerned departmental Secretaries can obtain the said information from 
the Avalokana software and utilize it to assess the progress of their respective departments.
12.2 SPECIAL DEVELOPMENT PLAN FOR BALANCED REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Karnataka has always demonstrated vibrant potential for growth. Despite the natural resource constraints and 
unfavorable conditions, the State could maintain above average performance in basic development indicators. 
It is placed at the median level on most of the development indicators. During the last five decades, the State 
has made efforts to achieve rapid growth through investments in agriculture, industry, infrastructure and 
other sectors. 
With the sharp North-South divide existing in the State, the regional gap emerged in the State on the eve of 
the reorganization of States in 1956. The new areas that joined the State from Hyderabad State and Bombay 
State were relatively less developed than the Old Mysore State. This area formed the Northern part of the 
State. In the absence of focused efforts in the past, the development gap increased over a period of time 
leading to marginalization and exclusion of the region and its people from the mainstream development 
process. Efforts have been made over a period of time to reduce the un-developmental gap. However, there 
has been a growing realization that investment and focus on the area especially on initiatives to improve the 
human development indicators must be further accelerated. 
12.2.1 High Power Committee for Redressal of Regional Imbalances (2000-2002)
The High-Power Committee for Redressal of Regional Imbalances (HPCRRI) constituted under the Chairmanship 
of Dr. D.M. Nanjunadappa assessed the level of development of 175 taluks in the state which spread over 
various sectors such as agriculture, industry, economic infrastructure, social infrastructure, and demography 
on the basis of 35 socio-economic indicators. Considering the state average of development in these indicators 
as the benchmark (equal to 1), the Committee estimated Comprehensive Composite Development Index 
(CCDI) with appropriate weights and identified 114 taluks as backward taluks. These taluks were further 
classified into most backward, more backward and backward taluks based on the value of CCDI. Taluks with

12.2.3 Special Development Plan
The Committee has estimated the required resource flow in the 114 backward taluks to bring them on par 
with other taluks in the State for which an Eight-year Special Development Plan (SDP) has been recommended 
for implementation with an investment of Rs.31,000 crore, which includes Rs.15,000 crore from Normal Plan 
programmes, and Rs.16,000 crore as additional grants. The objectives of the Special Development Plan are 
as mentioned below
 Y  T o give a thrust to the development programmes in the 114 backward taluks to move towards a more 
balanced development in the State. 
 Y  T o accelerate the growth in the backward taluks through the stimulus of additional investment in various 
sectors and areas. 
 Y  T o establish the needed institutions / organizations to redress the imbalances in the concerned sectors in 
backward taluks. 
 Y  T o provide location-specific sectoral schemes in backward taluks in order to raise the level of services in 
these sectors to the level of State average. 
12.2.4 Allocations under Special Development Plan 
An eight-year Special Development Plan (SDP) has been recommended for implementation with an investment 
of Rs. 31,000 crores which includes Rs. 15,000 crores from normal plan programmes and Rs. 16,000 crores as 
additional grants. The focus of the SDP is on irrigation, rural development and social sectors. Sectors like energy 
and agriculture are also given additional financial assistance. The allocations in SDP across the divisions were 
based on the Cumulative Deprivation Index (CDI). This is estimated on the basis of the distance of the CCDI 
value from the State average (CDI=1-CCDI). The allocation within the division and among the districts and 
taluks is again based on the respective CDI values of the additional investment of Rs. 16,000 crore. The share 
of Kalburgi division is the maximum i.e. Rs. 6,400 crore. This is because the extent of development deprivation 
is more in Kalburgi Division i.e. 8.06 (8.06/20.26X100 =40%) which is just equal to the total deprivation of 
entire South Karnataka.

12.3.1 Malnad Area Development Board
Malnad Area Development Board came into existence as per the Malnad Area Development Act 1991. The 
main objective of the board is specifically to achieve overall development of the Malnad Area. The Board covers 
46 Assembly Constituencies comprising 46 talukas of the remaining 10 districts, after excluding districts from 
Karavali Development Board. The board depending upon the grants available and determines the specific 

PDF_PAGE 629
621

requirements that needs to be made to fill gaps or those that cannot be funded from regular plans. The Board 
has taken up many initiatives including the formation of concrete roads in the areas inhabited by the weaker 
sections, providing safe drinking water in rural areas especially those affected by fluoride, construction of foot 
bridges and hanging bridges as well as formation of roads. 
From 1993-94 to 2025-26, an amount of Rs.1,058.78 crores has been allocated to the board of which Rs.985.84

12.3.2 Bayaluseeme Area Development Board
Bayaluseeme (Maidan Area) comprises 57 Taluks of the State which have been recognised as drought prone 
taluks, and pose special problems for development. To hasten the development of this area for bringing 
it on par with the other parts of the State, Bayaluseeme Area Development Board was established under 
Bayaluseeme Area Development Board Act 1994. There are 70 Assembly constituencies spread over 14 
districts, come under the purview of the board. The main objectives of the Board are as detailed below.
 Y  De velopment and Conservation measures in rain fed agriculture 
 Y  Adop ting soil and water conservation measures in rain fed agriculture afforestation.

12.3.3 Karavali Development Board
The Karavali Development Authority (KDA) was established in the year 2008 to foster the comprehensive 
development of the coastal districts of Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, and Uttara Kannada, with a mandate to 
strengthen infrastructure, conserve coastal resources, and promote agriculture, fisheries, and tourism. To 
further accelerate development and ensure parity with other regions of the State, The ‘Karavali Development 
Board’ (KDB) was constituted under Karavali Development Board Act, 2023, there by providing a comprehensive 
legislation. Objectives of the Board are as detailed below.
 Y  Pr omote development and conservation of water resources.
 Y  Adop t soil and water conservation measures in rainfed agriculture systems.

 Y  Enc ourage horticulture development.

 Y  Undert ake such other objects as directed by the Government.

12.3.4 Karnataka Border Area Development Authority
Karnataka Border Area Development Authority was started as per Karnataka Border Area Development 
Authority Act 2010. 63 border taluks of 19 border districts which are having border with the 6 States namely, 
Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Goa, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana comes under the purview of the 
authority. Important Functions of the Authority are as detailed below:
 Y  Implemen t, supervise and evaluate the development works in the border areas and also improve the 
educational, social and cultural conditions of Kannada speaking people in the border areas of the 
neighbouring States.
 Y  Pr ovide assistance for opening required number of Kannada medium schools in the areas outside the 
border of the State. 
 Y  Appoin tment of Kannada teachers and supply of text books to the students studying in Kannada medium 
in the border areas schools.
 Y  Open li braries in the border area to learn about the day today developments in Kannada Language.
 Y  Fulfil the cultural requirements of Kannadigas in the border area by organising cultural activities at border 
area.
 Y Construction fo cultural halls/kannada halls in the border areas of the State and outside States.

12.3.5 Article 371(J) – Special Status for the region of Kalyana-Karnataka 
The Article 371(J) has granted special status to seven backward districts of Kalyana Karnataka region namely, 
Bidar, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal, Ballari, Kalaburagi and Vijayanagar.
(1) The Hon’ble President may, by order, made with respect to the State of Karnataka, provide for any special 
responsibility of the Hon’ble Governor for – 
(a) Es tablishment of a separate development board for Kalyana-Karnataka Region with the provision 
that a report on the working of the board will be placed each year before the State Legislative 
Assembly;
(b) E quitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure over the said region, subject to the 
requirements of the State as a whole; and 
(c) E quitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging to the said region, in matters of 
public employment, education and vocational training, subject to the requirements of the State as 
a whole.
(2) An or der made under sub-clause (1) may provide for –
(a) R eservation of a proportion of seats in educational and vocational training institutions in the 
Kalyana-Karnataka region for students who belong to that region by birth or by domicile; and 
(b) Iden tification of posts under the State Government and in any body or organization under the 
control of the State Government in the Kalyana-Karnataka Region and reservation at the proportion 
of such posts for persons who belong to that region by birth or by domicile and for appointment 
there to by direct recruitment or by promotion or in any other manner as may be specified in the 
order.
The Constitutional obligation consequent to Amendment of Article 371(J) by insertion of Article 371(J), binds 
the State and Central Governments to put forth all out efforts for development of the Kalyana-Karnataka region 
besides ensuring the same by way of providing reservation in the Education and Public Employment sectors. 
A Cabinet Sub-Committee was constituted to advise the State Government for effective implementation of 
Article 371(J). The Cabinet Sub-Committee has held wide range of discussions with all stakeholders of the 
region and has submitted a report to the Government. In pursuance to the implementation of Article 371(J) 
the State has issued the following orders:
a. The K alyana-Karnataka Region Development Board Order, 2013.
b. The Karnataka Public Employment (Reservation in Appointment for Kalyana-Karnataka Region) Orders 
2013 – Provides for creation of a local cadre and reservation in the Kalyana-Karnataka Region as under, 
besides reservation of 8% of the posts in the State level offices or institutions or apex institutions.
c. The Karnataka Private Un-Aided Educational Institutions (Regulations of Admission in the Kalyana-
Karnataka Region) Order, 2013. - provides for reservation of 70% of the available seats in every course of 
study in any regional university or educational institution referred to in the First Schedule, besides 8% of 
the available seats in every course of study provided in a State wide university or a State wide educational 
institutions.

626

d. The Karnataka Educational Institutions (Regulations of Admission in the Kalyana-Karnataka Region) Order, 
2013 provides for reservation of 70% of available seats.
Reservation in Education sector and Recruitment in Public Employment under Article 371(J) of the Constitution 
of India
Special stress is laid upon for area development, reservation in public employment and reservation in 
admission to various courses for the local persons belonging to Kalyana (Hyderabad) Karnataka region under 
Article 371(J) of the Constitution of India conferring special status to the Kalyana (Hyderabad) Karnataka 
region. Consequential orders have been issued for implementation of Article 371(J).
A Cabinet Sub - Committee is reviewing the implementation of the same from time to time. The reservation 
imposed for filling up of vacant posts consequent upon the amendment to the Constitution by insertion of 
Article 371(J) has been relaxed permitting the appointing authorities to fill in the vacant posts both in the local 
and parent residual cadres after formation of local cadre and allotment of the local persons to the respective 
cadres based on their option. Clarifications and guidelines in the form of Circulars, Official Memorandum and 
Government Orders are issued from time to time for effective implementation. Action is being taken to fill 
in all the vacant posts in the Government offices located in the Kalyana-Karnataka region consequent to the 
accordable of special status to the Kalyana-Karnataka region providing for reservation in Public Employment 
and admissions to various courses in the educational institutions, ample opportunities are made available to 
the local persons in the Public Employment and Educational sectors.

Issues and Challenges
Despite the interventions to develop the Kalyana-Karnataka region on par with the relatively developed 
regions, vital indicators relating to human development, in particular, of the region depicts that the gaps 
in the indices still persists. This indicates that the barriers to development are still strong enough to retard 
the development processes. The focus, however, needs to be on education, health and nutrition and skill 
development along with development of farm and non-farm activities. Therefore, formulation and effective 
implementation of development programmes tailored to the needs of the region are required to meet the 
challenges of this region.
12.3.6 Karnataka Legislators Local Area Development Scheme
In order to accommodate local aspirations and needs and to ensure responsive planning and delivery of 
services, the Government has introduced the Karnataka Legislators Local Area Development Scheme 
(KLLADS) in 2001-02 with an allocation of Rs.25 lakhs per constituency. Schemes pertaining to asset creation, 
infrastructure development and employment generation for the benefit of the poor and weaker sections are 
taken up under this programme. 
The allocation has been enhanced from Rs.25 lakhs to Rs.100 lakhs per Legislature constituency from  
2006-07. Further the allocation has been enhanced from Rs.100 lakhs to Rs.200 lakhs per constituency from 
2013-14.

PDF_PAGE 636
628
Good Governance Practices in Karnataka
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
The KLLADS follows a participatory demand responsive development approach to address infrastructure 
development requirements of the local area within a Legislator’s Constituency. It also provides flexibility in 
taking up works which are otherwise not covered by other government programs. 
During 2024-25, an amount of Rs.600.00 crores was provided under this scheme of which an amount of 
Rs.595.00 crores was released. The expenditure incurred is Rs.516.37 crores up to Jan-2026. Out of 10,454 
works recommended 1,900 works have been completed with an expenditure of Rs.84.19 crores. The remaining 
8,554 works are under progress.
For 2025-26, an amount of Rs.600 crores was provided under this scheme of which an amount of Rs.594.00 
crores was released. The expenditure incurred is Rs.253.54 crores up to Jan-2026. Out of 5,001 works 
recommended 121 works have been completed with an expenditure of Rs.4.92 crores. The remaining 4,880 
works are under progress.
12.4 KARNATAKA MONITORING AND EVALUATION AUTHORITY (KMEA) 
Evaluation of government schemes/programmes 
Government of Karnataka formulated an Evaluation Policy during the year 2000 vide No.IFS 42 EVF (1) 1999 
Bangalore dated 17th November 2000. As per policy all schemes (PLAN) with more than Rs. 1 crore outlay 
were required to be evaluated at least once in 5 years by all the government departments, corporations, 
boards, local bodies and other publicly funded entities and 1% of the total outlay of a project/scheme, with an 
upper limit of Rs. 5 lakhs, is to be kept for evaluation purpose. It is mandatory for a scheme/project to continue 
beyond plan period to be justified by evaluation. Initially the Evaluation Policy was to be implemented by the 
Departmental Evaluation Committee (DEC) and State Evaluation Co-ordination Committee (SECC).
First of its kind in the country, Karnataka Monitoring and Evaluation Authority (KMEA) was set up vide 
Government Order No. PD/8/EVN (2)/2011 dated: 11.07.2011 for the purpose. KMEA is a society registered 
in September, 2011 under Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960 vide No. DRB-C/SOR/140/2011-12 dated 
19.09.2011. The State Government provides budget grants to facilitate the functioning of KMEA. It is an ISO 
9001:2015 certified body. KMEA is member of 3ie - an international organisation. KMEA provides technical 
guidance to all the Departments and Institutions an evaluation works taken by them. In addition, KMEA 
undertakes thematic/conceptual evaluations on key issues with its own resources and provides the feed back 
to the State Government.
Aims of Evaluation shall be keeping in place a transparent, effective and efficient practice of evaluation of its 
development policies and programmes. The Government recognizes the need for an effective use of credible 
evaluation as a tool to benchmark the state of affairs, refine its public policies, and designing programmes and 
schemes with prudent and optimal use of resources for maximizing the intended and measurable outcomes 
and citizen satisfaction.
Mission is 
 Y Prescribing standards of policy and programme formulation, monitoring, evaluation and refinement.
 Y Institutionalising enabled machinery backed by adequate financial resources and informed procedures 
to facilitate, supervise and enforce timely, useful and accountable evaluation.
 Y Enhanced technical capacities within the departments of the Government and by the independent 
evaluation agencies to undertake and effectively utilize evaluation outputs for informed decision-making.
 Y Enhanced Stakeholders’ satisfaction through participation, transparency and accountability.

12.5 DIRECTORATE OF ECONOMICS AND STATISTICS (DES)
The statistical system in Karnataka consists of the Directorate of Economics and Statistics (DES) & the 
statistical divisions in other departments of the Government. The DES is responsible for providing the 
necessary data base for formulation of programs and policies by the State. Statistical data on various socio-

PDF_PAGE 638
630
Good Governance Practices in Karnataka
Karnataka Economic Survey 2025-26
economic activities of the State are being collected, processed, analyzed and published from time to time. 
It also conducts sample surveys on various aspects of Socio-economic development. It acts as a Nodal 
Agency in respect of all the Statistical activities of the state and provide advice to all the departments in the 
statistical matters. DES also estimates hobli and grama panchayat level Insurance unit wise average yield for 
the notified crops under Karnataka Raita Suraksha Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and sent to Agriculture 
Department for settlement of insurance claims to the farmers. DES also estimates for Gross State Domestic 
Product (GSDP), Gross Districts Domestic Product (GDDP), Per capita Income of the State and districts, Index 
of industrial production, Wholesale and Retail Price Indices and Consumer Price Indices. DES also implements 
the registration of Births and Deaths events as per the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (Amended 
in 2023). 
The important activities of the Directorate is to participate in Agriculture Census, Economic Census, National 
Sample Survey, Sample check on Development Programs, Conduct of Crop Cutting Experiments, Estimation of 
Area Yield & Production of Agriculture Crops and bringing out various reports. Besides it also implements the 
centrally sponsored schemes of Improvement of Crop Statistics and Timely Reporting Scheme. During 2025-
26, the focus of the Directorate of Economics and Statistics was on the following.  
12.5.1 Registration of Births and Deaths in e-JanMa Web Application
Registration of Births and Deaths in Karnataka is carried out as per the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 
1969 (Amended in 2023) and Karnataka Registration of Births and Deaths Rules, 1999 (Amended in 2024). In 
accordance with the registration of births and deaths Amendment Act 2023, Karnataka Registration of Births 
and Deaths Rules 1999 is amended in 2024. e-JanMa (electronic Janana Marana) web based application is 
designed for births and deaths registration with an objective to ensure 100% registration of births and deaths 
in the State. 
As at the end of December 2025 registration of births and deaths is being done in 61,903 registration centers 
in the state, of which 61,250 centers are in rural area and 653 centers are in urban area. During 2025 the total 
number of births and deaths registered in the State is 10.19 lakhs and 5.61 lakhs respectively. The birth rate 
for the year 2024 is 13.88 as against 14.27 during the year 2023. The death rate for the year 2024 is 7.97 as 
against 7.84 during the year 2023.
Special features of e-JanMa
 Y Digital Signature of the Registrars/ Sub-registrars is made mandatory in the certificates. 
 Y SMS is being sent to the Registrars/ Sub-registrars regarding the pending events for approval. 
 Y SMS is being sent to the informants after the birth and death events are approved.
 Y A circular has been issued to Sub-Registrars to issue birth certificate before the discharge of the mother 
from the Hospital.
 Y Public can get the Birth and Death certificates issued already from concerned Birth and Death registration 
centers, citizen service centers - Seva Sindhu Centers and Bapuji Seva Kendras.
 Y The authenticity of the Birth or Death certificates can be verified in the e-JanMa portal by the public and 
agencies like School Authorities, Passport Offices, Insurance companies etc.
 Y Karnataka is the first State in the Country to incorporate Birth and Death Certificates registered in 
e-JanMa into Block chain application developed by Govt. of India. It prevents duplication of birth and 
death certificates and their misuse.
 Y Birth certificates of the child can be downloaded to Digilocker app based on pull service.

 Y e-JanMa application is currently integrated with the following department portals namely, Health and 
Family Welfare Department’s RCH, Horticulture Department’s FRUITS, Food and Civil Supply Department’s 
AHARA, e-Governance Department’s KUTUMBA and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology’s 
AADHAR software. This has saved crores of rupees to the Government by deleting deceased persons 
from the beneficiary list of the Development Programmes and Social Security Schemes.
 Y Uploading of Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form-4) to e-JanMa has been made compulsory for

12.5.2 Agriculture Statistics
 Y 11th Agriculture Census was conducted in the State in three phases. In the first phase, enumeration 
of different categories of land holders namely, marginal, small, semi-medium, medium and large land 
holders and the area of operation is completed and the same was submitted to Govt. of India.
 Y In the second phase, data on land use, sources of irrigation, cropping pattern and dispersal of operated 
area are also collected on sample basis in 20% of the total villages of the State and submitted to Govt. 
of India.
 Y In the third phase, input survey is conducted in 7% of the total villages of the State with an objective to 
collect the data on number of parcels, multiple cropping, land use pattern, use of chemical fertilizers, 
organic manure, agricultural implements and agricultural credit availed by cultivators. After the approval 
of the State Level  Co-ordination Committee the data will be submitted to Govt. of India.
 Y Preparation of report on Sample check survey conducted on “Infrastructure available in Anganawadis 
and extent of their utilization” during 2024-25 is in progress. 
 Y DES conducts crop cutting experiments to estimate average yield for the notified crops based on the 
results of crop cutting experiments under Karnataka Raitha Suraksha Pradhana Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana 
and insurance unit wise the average yield of the notified crops is sent to the Agriculture department for 
settlements of insurance claims to the farmers. During 2024-25, based on the results of the crop cutting 
experiments conducted at the field level, 13376 Gram Panchayathwise and 4487 Hobliwise totally 17863 
insurance units average yield is finalized.
 Y For 2025-26 kharif season, 82354 crop cutting experiments are planned for the notified crops of which 
80704 experiments are conducted upto 13/2/2026. The remaining experiments are under progress. Out 
of the total 12591 notified insurance units, till date 370 GP wise and 389 Hobliwise totally 759 insurance 
units of early Kharif crops average yield of the notified crops is finalized in CCE Samrakshane portal 
and sent to Agricultural department for settlements of insurance claims to the farmers. Preparation of 
insurance unit wise average yield of Kharif crops for the Kharif crops is under progress.
 Y The Directorate of Economic and Statistics estimates area, yield and production of important agriculture 
crops grown in the State. As per the final estimates, the area under major agriculture crops grown in the 
State during Kharif, Rabi and Summer seasons during 2024-25 was 112.09 lakh hectares, of which the 
area under food grains was 85.71 lakh hectares. Estimated production of food grains was 151.57 lakh 
tons.
 Y As per the Second Advanced Estimates of area and production for Kharif and Rabi seasons for 2025-26, 
the area of major agricultural crops is 107.1 lakh hectares, of which the area under food grains is 78.6 
lakh hectares. The estimated food production for Kharif and Rabi season is 136.22 lakh tons. 
 Y  Ar ea under different crops grown in the State is enumerated through Crop Survey using GIS basis Mobile 
App every year. About 2 crores plots are enumerated every year of which the area enumerated by the

12.5.3 Karnataka at a Glance and District at a Glance
The Directorate of Economic and Statistics publishes two important publications namely, “Karnataka at a 
Glance” and “District at a Glance” which are being brought out by collecting the information from the districts 
through online and by linking the geographical information system portal developed by the Karnataka  
State Remote Sensing Applications Centre (KSRSAC). These publications for the year 2023-24 are published 
which contain the information of about more than 2340 parameters both static information (Population 
Census, Agriculture Census and Livestock Census) and dynamic information pertaining to the development 
programmes of various departments in addition to Socio-Economic and Geographic information of districts/
taluks.
These publications contain not only statistical information but also the information of 35 indicators adopted by 
the High Power Committee on Redressal of Regional Imbalances headed by Dr. D.M. Nanjundappa to identify 
the backward taluks in the State and value of indicators assigned by the NITI Ayog for the development of 
Aspiration taluks. The indicators and the spatial maps in the publications are useful for the planners and 
administrators to identify the taluks which are less than the State average and to formulate suitable policies 
and plans for the backward taluks on priority basis. The preparation of Karnataka at a Glance and District at a 
Glance for 2024-25 is in progress. The information is available on the website www.des.karnataka.gov.in and 
www.planning.karnataka.gov.in. The statistics information of Karnataka compared with India is presented in 
Appendix 12.5 and 12.6.
12.5.4 Taluka at a Glance

preparation of this publication is in progress.

12.5.6 Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) 2.0 Scheme
The support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) is an on-going central sector sub-scheme implemented by the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI),GoI, which aims to improve/strengthen the 
statistical capacity and operations of the State Statistical System for collection, compiling and disseminating 
reliable official statistics. The main objectives of the scheme are as follows.
 Y Enhance the State’s participation in MoSPI statistical products and survey.
 Y Strengthen State Statistical Systems to produce high-quality, timely, and reliable official statistics at the 
granular level.
 Y Improve institutional and IT infrastructural capacity in States/UTs.
 Y Ensure official statistics are aligned with National/International standards, inter-operable data across 
departments, and widely used for policy.
 Y Build sustainable mechanisms for continuous statistical strengthening.
For the year 2025-26 an amount of Rs. 1.11 Crore is released by the MoSPI to purchase tablet PCs required 
to conduct National Sample Surveys on CAPI mode. An amount of Rs. 48 lakhs is spent up to December 2025 
towards purchase of 112 tablet PCs.
Way Forward
The Directorate of Economic and Statistics, under Planning, Programme Monitoring and Statistics Department 
is responsible for providing necessary database required for formulation of programmes and policies in 
the State. It has voluminous time series data on Population census, Agriculture Census, Economic Census, 
Livestock Census and the data on various programmes of the development departments, in addition to area, 
yield, production of various agricultural and horticultural crops. But at present it emphasizes more on data 
collection and less on data analysis. In the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Support for Statistical Strengthening 
(SSS) 2.0 there is a proposal to create data analytical centre to analyse the data with statistical tools with the 
domain experts of various fields. The focus will also be on improving the quality of data and aligning the data 
with SDG goals.

13.1 INTRODUCTION 
Karnataka has adopted a comprehensive and structured approach to achieving the Sustainable Development 
Goals (SDGs) under the United Nations 2030 Agenda. By integrating economic, social and environmental 
priorities, the State has embedded the SDG framework into its planning process. This has been achieved 
through the formation of dedicated Goal Committees, the establishment of robust monitoring mechanisms 
and the systematic alignment of government schemes with specific SDG targets, ensuring coordinated and 
measurable progress toward sustainable development.
With significant budgetary allocations, outcome-based planning and continuous tracking through the SDG 
India Index, Karnataka has demonstrated measurable progress while identifying priority gaps. The chapter 
reviews preparedness, performance trends, budget mapping, outcome budgeting, and strategic interventions 
aimed at accelerating progress toward inclusive, sustainable, and resilient development by 2030.
13.2 BACKGROUND AND GLOBAL CONTEXT OF THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS
The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the United Nations General Assembly during 
its 70th Session on 25 September 2015 through the landmark resolution, “Transforming our World: the 2030 
Agenda for Sustainable Development.” The agenda outlines 17 SDGs, supported by 169 targets and 232 
indicators, to be achieved by 2030. Effective from 1 January 2016, the SDGs provide a comprehensive global 
blueprint for advancing human well-being while safeguarding the planet for future generations.
Unlike earlier development frameworks, the SDGs integrate the three core dimensions of development, 
namely economic, social and environmental into a unified agenda. Building upon the Millennium Development 
Goals, these SDGs expand the focus to include climate change, economic inequality, innovation, sustainable 
consumption, peace, justice, and institutional strength. Although SDGs are interconnected, each goal has 
clearly defined targets to guide measurable progress.
For India, the SDGs are closely aligned with the national aspiration of attaining developed country status by 
2047 under the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. Achieving this ambition requires effective localisation of the 
SDGs and embedding global goals into national, state, district and local development planning. There is a 
growing global consensus that localisation is essential for meaningful progress, as the SDG agenda depends 
not only on governments but also on active participation from communities, civil society and the private 
sector.
An important instrument supporting localisation in India is the SDG India Index, which measures progress 
and encourages constructive competition among States and Union Territories. By ranking performance and 
tracking indicators at State, District and Block levels, the Index has strengthened data systems, improved 
accountability and promoted knowledge sharing across regions.
National initiatives such as the Aspirational District Programme and Aspirational Block Programme have 
further accelerated SDG implementation. Karnataka, through its “Special Development Plan” has been a 
pioneer in addressing regional imbalances even before these national interventions.
With only four years remaining until the 2030 deadline, and globally, just 17 percent of SDG targets are 
currently on track, renewed and coordinated efforts from all stakeholders are essential to achieve the 
transformative vision of sustainable development.

The SDGs will stimulate action in areas of: People, Planet, Prosperity, Peace and Partnership.
People: To end poverty and hunger, in all their forms and dimensions, and to ensure that all human beings can 
fulfil their potential in dignity and equality and in a healthy environment (SDGs 1,2,3,4 and 5).
Planet: To protect the planet from degradation, including through sustainable consumption and production, 
sustainably managing its natural resources and taking urgent action on climate change, so that it can support 
the needs of the present and future generations (SDGs 6,12,13,14 and 15).
Prosperity: To ensure that all human beings can enjoy prosperous and fulfilling lives and that economic, social 
and technological progress occurs in harmony with nature (SDGs 7,8,9,10 and 11).
Peace: To foster peaceful, justice and inclusive societies which are free from fear and violence. There can be 
no sustainable development without peace and no peace without sustainable development(SDG 16).
Partnership: To mobilize the means required to implement this agenda through a revitalised Global Partnership 
for Sustainable Development, based on a spirit of strengthened global solidarity, focused in particular on the 
needs of the poorest and most vulnerable and with the participation of all countries, all stakeholders and all 
people (SDG 17).
In a nutshell it is the universal, inclusive and indivisible agenda which calls for action by all participating 
countries to improve the lives of the people and the planet. While the SDG goals and targets set a global 
context, they have been designed in a way so that they can be adapted locally to meet the specific challenges. 
SDGs are interlinked (achieving one goal results in achieving other goals) and address all three dimensions of 
development viz; Economic, Social and Environmental aspects of development.

13.3 Preparedness of the state to implement SDG 2030
Karnataka being one of the progressive states in the country is highly sensitive to universal developmental 
programmes initiated by international institutions such as United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), 
World Bank, UN and other organizations. State has been the front-runner in formulating action plan, vision 
and targets of sustainable development goals and it is proactive in formulation and implementation of 
programmes, to achieve the targets of SDGs.
The State has formed Goal Committees to provide technical support to prepare Karnataka SDG vision 2030 
document. This document provides the road map for realizing goals and targets of the State. The State also 
constituted Monitoring and Coordination Committee and the State level Steering Committee for formulation 
of effective and efficient action plans for achieving SDGs.
Goal Committees have identified around 678 indicators which contains some of the national indicators and 
proxy state indicators (where data not available for national indicators). Baseline Data has been prepared by 
Goal Committees with all relevant information / present status of major indicators and given recommendations 
to achieve SDGs by 2030. Karnataka has been actively working towards spreading awareness about SDGs 
through establishing Sustainable Development Centre in Administrative Training Institute, Mysore. State has 
constituted revised goal committees under the chairmanship of the respective departments to prepare action 
plans based on the recommendations given by the earlier goal committees.
Goal Committees have identified around four hundred schemes and proposed a budget requirement of Rs.10 
lakh crore to achieve SDGs by 2030. An amount of Rs.356874.83 crore is provided under budget between 
2020-26 and Rs.249998.39 crore is spent between 2020-24. The details of budget proposed for 2030, budget 
allocated and actual expenditure occurred is given in the Table 13.1.

13.4 SDG India Index
With the objective of measuring the progress of SDGs and develop competitiveness among States and 
UTs, NITI Aayog has released four versions of SDG Index Reports till now. Based on the results of the SDG 
India Index Reports, States and UTs have been classified into four categories: Achiever(Score 100), Front 
runner(Score:65-99), Performer(50-64) and Aspirant(0-49).
SDG India Index 1.0: The first version of the Index i.e., SDG India Index Baseline Report, 2018 was released 
in December 2018. The index tracks the progress of all the States and UTs on a set of 62 indicators covering 
13SDGs (excluding SDGs 12, 13, 14 and 17 because of paucity of data). As per the report, Karnataka has been 
ranked as Performer with composite score at  64.
SDG India Index (2019-20) 2.0: It is the second version of the report which built upon its first version. It was 
launched in December 2019. The index has been constructed using 100 indicators that cover first 16 goals. As 
per the report, Karnataka has been ranked as Front Runner with composite score at 66.
SDG India Index (2020-21) 3.0: It is the third version of the report which was built upon its second version. It 
was launched in June 2021. The index has been constructed using 115 indicators that cover first 16 goals. The 
composite score for Karnataka improved from 66 in second version to 72 in 2020-21 in third version, albeit 
retaining its position in the Front Runner Category.
SDG India Index (2023-24) 4.0: It is the fourth version of the report which was built upon its third version. It 
was launched in July 2024, The index has been constructed using 113 indicators that cover first 16 goals. The 
composite score for Karnataka improved from 72 in third version to 75 in fourth version and maintaining same 
Front Runner Category.
Goal-wise analysis of Karnataka from version 1 to version 4 given in Table 13.2. The composite score for 
Karnataka was improved from 64 in first version to 75 in 4th version. The State has improved its performance 
in 11 goals in 2023-24 compared to 2020-21. They are, SDGs 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15 and 16 and slipped 
in four Goals, namely SDGs 4, 5, 9 and 12. As per the latest SDG India Index Report 2023-24 (Version 4.0), the 
State’s performance is better than All India’s performance in all SDGs except SDG15 (In SDG 15, State’s score 
is 70, whereas All India score is 75). As per SDG India Index version 4, SDG7 is under Achiever category, eleven 
Goals (SDGs 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16) are under Front runner category and four goals (SDGs 2, 
4, 5, and 9) are under Performer category.

13.5 ALIGNING SCHEMES(HEADS OF ACCOUNTS) TO SDGS  
SDGs do not have dedicated financial allocation of their own, they have to be achieved through existing and 
new schemes implemented by the respective departments. One of the crucial aspects of institutionalising 
the SDGs is to align state schemes to the SDGs and their targets. In Voluntary National Review 2020 Report, 
it was provisionally estimated that making India progress on SDGs would require an additional annual spend 
of 6.2% of GDP by 2030. The public money raised and spent has profound impact on Society, Economy and 
Environment. While there is no one to one relation between SDGs achievement and budget allocation, there 
is a clear benefit from being strategic in design of programmes, schemes and budgeting. There are 2295 heads 
of account (schemes) in the budget 2025-26(BE). The Budget for 2025-26(BE) is at Rs.409549.24 crore. All 
these schemes are mapped with one or other of sixteen SDGs. If a particular scheme mapped with multiple 
goals (based on the activities being taken up under the scheme), the allocation of the scheme is distributed 
to these multiple goals equally (Table 13.5).

13.6 SDG OUTCOME BUDGET 
State is preparing SDG outcome budget every year by identifying poor performing indicators as per latest SDG 
India Index report and estimated the budget required to improve performance in these indicators on par with 
best performing States. Accodingly, poor  indicators were identified (Table13.6) and analysed the Goal wise 
budget required for 2025-26 as against the budget provided (Table13.7). The gap between budget proposed 
and budgeted outlay for 2025-26 at Rs.10796.61 crore could be met through private sector under Corporate 
Social Responsibility platform.

13.7 WAY FORWARD
 Y  Allign S chemes to SDGs
 ) GSDP-SDG Linkage: Analyse and establish connection between sectoral parameters of GSDP and 
SDGs for comprehensive allignment.
 ) Private Sector ESG Framework: Encourage SDG implementation within private sector through 
application of  ESG (Environmental/Social/Governance) framework.
 ) Schematic Weighatages: Establish proper weighatages for schemes linked to multiple SDGs to 
reflect their proportionate SDG contributions.
 ) CSR Fund  Mobilisation: Encourage CSR funding for SDG related  projects at GP and TP level.
 ) SDG bounds for resource mobilisation: To raise targeted resources for SDG wise initiatives.
 ) Allign object heads with SDGs: Allign object heads with SDGs enabling better insights, strategic 
planning and Monitoring.
 Y Initatives to achieve SDGs
 ) Stateholders consultations (including Elected representatives and NGOs) is required to make 
policies and programmes towards achieving SDGs by 2030.
 ) Awareness among general public about SDGs should be created.
 ) As apart of SDG localisation, sub state level and sub district level monitoring of SDGs should be 
strengthen.
 ) Departments have to submit the latest data on the SDG indicators to the concerned Ministries in 
GoI in order to showcase the better performance of the State in SDG India Index Reports.

 ) SDG3: Good Health & Wellbeing

the results for monitoring, evaluation and decision making.
 ) SDG4: Quality Education
1. Ensur e arrest of dropouts at secondary level and career guidance to take them to higher 
education. Vocationalisation of education has to be thrust area in this sector’s strategy.

Provision of safe transport and 24/7 helpline for women by Home Department.
3. Incr easing Women’s work participation and valuation and equal distribution of work.
 )  SDG6: Clean W ater & Sanitation

water. 
2. Ensuring separ ate & functional toilets for girls in schools, colleges and Public Places.

Periodic plans for all ESCOMs to reinforce their distribution infrastructure in a coordinated manner.
